docs.title: Frappe Framework
docs.text:
Frappe Framework is a full-stack web framework in Python and JavaScript. It is metadata driven. You describe data as DocTypes, and Frappe makes the database tables, the REST API, the desk forms, lists and reports, and the permission checks. You put your code in apps. A bench runs many sites, and each site installs a set of apps.

Version: 15 (stable)

These pages describe version 15 (branch version-15-hotfix). Every page was verified against the code of this branch. Other versions: v16 (stable) and develop (unreleased).

docs.title: Start here
docs.text: If you want to Read Install Frappe and make a site Installation Understand how the parts fit Architecture Build a first app Quickstart Look up a term Glossary See what changed since version 14 What's New Move an app to version 15 Upgrading

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• User Guide: use the desk, set up users and permissions, automate work, print, report, publish web pages, blogs and newsletters.
  • Developer Guide: build apps: DocTypes, controllers, hooks, the database API, REST, background jobs, desk scripts, website pages and tests.
  • Reference: complete lists of hooks, CLI commands, REST endpoints, site config keys, Python and JavaScript APIs, field types and DocTypes.
  • For AI Agents: rules and facts for agents that write or change Frappe apps.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Examples use the app sample_app, the DocTypes Sample Item and Sample Order, the role Sample Role and the user user1@example.com.
  • File paths in frappe/... are relative to the frappe app repository. Paths in sample_app/... are files in your app.
  • Commands run from the bench folder. Replace <site> with your site name.

docs.title: For AI Agents
docs.text: Read this page before you write or change code for a Frappe app on version 15. Every fact here was checked in the version-15-hotfix branch. For an index of all pages with one-line summaries, read llms.txt.

docs.title: Know the version first
docs.text:
1. Run bench version or read frappe/__init__.py __version__. These docs are for 15.x.
  2. Do not use an API from a later version. Version 15 has no extend_doctype_class, frappe.read_doc, frappe.enqueue_task, Flow, Studio, MCP, Automation Flow, Sidebar or Dock. The desk is at /app, not /desk.

docs.text: Question Page Which hooks exist and what shape they take Hooks reference Run order of controller methods and doc_events Controllers Signatures of frappe.*, frappe.db.*, frappe.utils.* Python API, Database API, Utils Client-side frappe.* and frm API JavaScript API, Form Scripts REST routes REST Endpoints CLI commands and flags CLI Config keys Site Config Field types and DB columns Field Types

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Use frappe.session.user for the current user. frappe.user is None.
  • Check permissions in every whitelisted method. Use doc.check_permission("read") or frappe.has_permission. frappe.get_doc does not check read permission.
  • frappe.get_all ignores permissions. frappe.get_list applies them. Neither has a default row limit in Python. Pass limit. In JavaScript, frappe.db.get_list defaults to 20 rows.
  • frappe.db.set_value, frappe.db.sql and frappe.qb skip validations, controller methods and permissions.
  • frappe.qb.get_query has no permission arguments. It never applies permissions.
  • Do not call frappe.db.commit() in a request handler, a controller method or a doc_events handler. In version 15 a commit inside a handler really commits, and a later error cannot roll it back. The request commits when it succeeds, but only for POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE (or when frappe.local.flags.commit is set).
  • A doc_events handler must accept two arguments: (doc, method). A one-argument handler raises TypeError.
  • has_permission hooks run in reverse order. The first result that is not None decides. None means "no opinion" and allows.
  • @frappe.whitelist() takes allow_guest, xss_safe and methods. Without methods, the method accepts GET, POST, PUT and DELETE. Restrict methods that write: @frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"]).
  • The server does not evaluate depends_on, mandatory_depends_on or read_only_depends_on. Only the desk does.
  • Dotted paths in hooks.py fail only when the hook runs. Check that each path imports.
  • override_doctype_class, doctype_js and doctype_list_js do not apply to custom DocTypes (custom = 1).
  • Test classes are FrappeTestCase and MockedRequestTestCase in frappe.tests.utils.

docs.title: Lifecycle order (insert)
docs.text: before_insert → before_naming → autoname → before_validate → validate → before_save → DB insert → after_insert → on_update → on_change. For each step, Frappe runs the controller method, then the doc_events handlers for the DocType, then the "*" handlers. See Controllers for save, submit, cancel, delete and the exact rules.

docs.title: Pitfalls seen in this code base
docs.text:
• require_type_annotated_api_methods is set in frappe's own hooks.py, but no version 15 code reads it.
  • The regex filter makes invalid SQL on MariaDB. between on a number field makes invalid SQL in get_list.
  • frappe.sendmail(now=True) sends at once, before the transaction commits.
  • server_script_enabled works only in common_site_config.json.
  • Fixture import deletes and inserts again any record that already exists. Changes made on the site to a fixture record are lost at each bench migrate.

docs.text: frappe/utils/deprecations.py gives the @deprecated decorator and deprecation_warning(). Examples that warn in v15: frappe.handler.uploadfile (use upload_file), the cmd form parameter for RPC calls (use /api/method/<cmd>), frappe.db.set_value on a single DocType (use frappe.db.set_single_value), the job_name argument of frappe.enqueue (use job_id), and the gravatar helpers in frappe.utils.

docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text:
Build and extend Frappe apps: app structure, data model, database, security, APIs, background work, desk UI, website, output, low-code tools, testing and operations.

Topic What it covers Building Apps Create an app, use hooks, extend other apps, ship fixtures and patches, and translate. Data Model Define DocTypes, naming rules, controllers and the document lifecycle, and handle files. Database Read and write data with frappe.db and frappe.qb, and control transactions. Permissions and Security Control access with permissions, authenticate clients and write secure code. APIs Expose whitelisted methods and use the REST API. Jobs, Realtime and Caching Run background jobs and scheduled tasks, push realtime events and cache data. Desk UI Script forms and lists, call the server from JavaScript, and build desk pages and navigation. Website and Portal Build website pages, portal pages, routes and web forms. Reports, Printing and Email Write script and query reports, print formats and PDFs, and send email and notifications. Server and Client Scripts Use server scripts and client scripts, and decide when to write app code instead. Testing and Performance Test apps and make them fast. Configuration and Operations Configure sites, deploy to production and upgrade between versions.

docs.title: APIs
docs.text:
Expose whitelisted methods and use the REST API.

Page What it covers Whitelisted Methods Expose Python functions over HTTP with @frappe.whitelist, validate arguments with type annotations, restrict access by role, rate limit, and override methods of other apps. REST API Read and change documents and call whitelisted methods over HTTP with /api/v1 (resource, method) and /api/v2 (document, doctype, method), including list parameters, responses and errors.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text:
Every Frappe site has a REST API at /api. It gives access to every DocType and every whitelisted method, with the permissions of the authenticated user. There are two versions:

  • /api/v1/... (also served at /api/...). Routes resource and method. Results are in data or message.
  • /api/v2/.... Routes document, doctype and method. Results are always in data. Errors are a list in errors.

All requests on this page were sent with curl to http://frappe.localhost:8001 (a v15 site) as user1@example.com with token authentication. The responses are trimmed. To get a token, see Authentication.

S=http://frappe.localhost:8001
AUTH="Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>"

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Action v1 v2 List documents GET /api/resource/<doctype> GET /api/v2/document/<doctype> Create POST /api/resource/<doctype> POST /api/v2/document/<doctype> Read GET /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> GET /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> Update PUT /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> PUT or PATCH /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> Delete DELETE /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> DELETE /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> Call a document method POST /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> with run_method GET or POST /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/method/<method> Copy a document GET /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/copy Count GET /api/v2/doctype/<doctype>/count DocType metadata GET /api/v2/doctype/<doctype>/meta Call a whitelisted method /api/method/<dotted.path> /api/v2/method/<dotted.path> Call a function in a DocType module /api/v2/method/<doctype>/<function>

URL-encode spaces in DocType names (Sample%20Item). A trailing slash after the document name is accepted. v15 has no bulk routes. The full list is in REST endpoints.

docs.title: v1
docs.text:
curl -s -G "$S/api/resource/Sample%20Item" -H "$AUTH" \
  --data-urlencode 'fields=["name","rate"]' \
  --data-urlencode 'filters=[["category","=","Hardware"],["rate","<",100]]' \
  --data-urlencode 'order_by=rate asc'

{"data": [{"name": "Keyboard", "rate": 45.0}]}

GET /api/resource/<doctype> calls frappe.client.get_list with the query parameters:

Parameter Default Description fields ["name"] JSON list. Same syntax as frappe.get_list. filters none JSON dict or list. See Filters. or_filters none JSON dict or list, joined with OR. order_by DocType sort settings For example rate desc. group_by none Field name. limit_start 0 Offset. limit_page_length or limit 20 Page size. 0 returns all rows. as_dict 1 0 returns lists instead of objects. parent none Parent DocType, required for a child DocType. expand none JSON list of Link fields to replace with the linked document. debug 0 Print the query for debugging. 
curl -s -G "$S/api/resource/Sample%20Item" -H "$AUTH" \
  --data-urlencode 'fields=["name","rate"]' --data-urlencode 'as_dict=0' --data-urlencode 'limit=2'

{"data": [["Antivirus", 60.0], ["Installation", 80.0]]}

docs.title: v2
docs.text:
curl -s -G "$S/api/v2/document/Sample%20Item" -H "$AUTH" \
  --data-urlencode 'fields=["name","rate"]' \
  --data-urlencode 'filters={"category":"Hardware"}' \
  --data-urlencode 'order_by=rate desc' \
  --data-urlencode 'limit=2'

{"data": [{"name": "Laptop", "rate": 900.0}, {"name": "Monitor", "rate": 250.0}]}

Next page, with start=2:

{"data": [{"name": "Keyboard", "rate": 45.0}]}

v2 sets limit_page_length from limit (default 20) and limit_start from start (default 0). Then it calls frappe.client.get_list, so all v1 list parameters also work. The response has no has_next_page key. Ask for limit + 1 rows to know if another page exists.

docs.title: Count
docs.text:
curl -s -G "$S/api/v2/doctype/Sample%20Item/count" -H "$AUTH" --data-urlencode 'filters={"category":"Hardware"}'

{"data": 3}

The count route calls frappe.desk.reportview.get_count.

docs.title: Create a document
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$S/api/v2/document/Sample%20Item" -H "$AUTH" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"item_name": "Sample Mouse", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 25}'

{"data": {"name": "Sample Mouse", "owner": "user1@example.com", "creation": "2026-11-22 09:37:01.175667",
  "modified": "2026-11-22 09:37:01.175667", "modified_by": "user1@example.com", "docstatus": 0, "idx": 0,
  "item_name": "Sample Mouse", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 25.0, "disabled": 0, "description": null,
  "doctype": "Sample Item"}}

The body is the document as JSON. Include child rows as lists, for example "items": [{"item": "Laptop", "qty": 1}]. The document is inserted with doc.insert(), so validations, controller hooks and permission checks run. v1 POST /api/resource/<doctype> does the same.

docs.title: Read a document
docs.text:
curl -s "$S/api/v2/document/Sample%20Item/Sample%20Mouse" -H "$AUTH"

{"data": {"name": "Sample Mouse", "owner": "user1@example.com", "docstatus": 0,
  "item_name": "Sample Mouse", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 25.0, "disabled": 0, "description": null,
  "doctype": "Sample Item"}}

The response has all fields and child tables. v15 ignores a fields parameter on this route. Both versions check read and remove fields that the user cannot read (doc.apply_fieldlevel_read_permissions()). v1 accepts expand_links=1 to replace Link values with the linked documents.

docs.title: Update a document
docs.text:
curl -s -X PATCH "$S/api/v2/document/Sample%20Item/Sample%20Mouse" -H "$AUTH" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"rate": 30}'

{"data": {"name": "Sample Mouse", "modified": "2026-11-22 09:37:01.220335", "rate": 30.0, "doctype": "Sample Item"}}

Send only the fields to change. Frappe loads the document with for_update=True, applies the values and calls doc.save(), which checks write. A list for a table field replaces all child rows. v1 uses PUT /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> with the same body.

docs.title: Delete a document
docs.text:
curl -s -X DELETE "$S/api/v2/document/Sample%20Item/Sample%20Mouse" -H "$AUTH" -w '\n%{http_code}\n'

{"data":"ok"}
202

docs.title: Call methods
docs.text:
curl -s "$S/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" -H "$AUTH"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}
curl -s "$S/api/v2/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" -H "$AUTH"
# {"data":"user1@example.com"}
curl -s "$S/api/v2/method/User/get_current_user_roles" -H "$AUTH"
# {"data":["Sample Role","All","Guest","Desk User"]}

Send arguments as query parameters for GET, and as a JSON or form body for POST. Nested values (lists, dicts) need a JSON body or JSON-encoded parameters. See Whitelisted methods.

frappe.client has general methods, for example frappe.client.get_list, frappe.client.get_value, frappe.client.insert, frappe.client.set_value, frappe.client.submit, frappe.client.cancel and frappe.client.delete. They apply the permissions of the user.

curl -s -X POST "$S/api/v2/method/frappe.client.insert" -H "$AUTH" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"doc": {"doctype": "Sample Item", "item_name": "Sample Mouse C", "category": "Hardware"}}'

docs.title: Responses
docs.text: Key Where Content data v1 resource, all v2 Result message v1 method Return value of the method docs v2 document methods Changed documents _server_messages v1 JSON string with messages from frappe.msgprint messages v2 List of messages from frappe.msgprint

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The HTTP status comes from http_status_code of the exception class (frappe/exceptions.py):

Status Exception 400 frappe.CSRFTokenError 401 frappe.AuthenticationError, frappe.SessionExpired 403 frappe.PermissionError 404 frappe.DoesNotExistError 409 frappe.DuplicateEntryError (subclass of frappe.NameError) 417 frappe.ValidationError and subclasses (for example frappe.MandatoryError, frappe.TimestampMismatchError), frappe.FrappeTypeError 429 frappe.RateLimitExceededError, frappe.TooManyRequestsError 500 Other exceptions

v1 error:

{"exception": "frappe.exceptions.PermissionError",
 "exc_type": "PermissionError",
 "_server_messages": "[\"{\\\"message\\\": \\\"User <strong>user1@example.com</strong> does not have doctype access via role permission for document <strong>Sample Order</strong>\\\", \\\"title\\\": \\\"Message\\\"}\"]",
 "_error_message": "No permission for Sample Order"}

v2 error:

{"errors": [{"type": "PermissionError",
  "message": "User <strong>user1@example.com</strong> does not have doctype access via role permission for document <strong>Sample Order</strong>",
  "title": "Message"}]}

The traceback (exc in v1, exception in v2) is sent only when Show Full Error and Allow Reporting of Issues to the Developer (allow_error_traceback) is on in System Settings and the user is a system user (is_traceback_allowed in frappe/utils/response.py). It is not sent for HTTP 404 unless the logging site config is set.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text: A POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE request commits on success. A GET request is always rolled back. Any error rolls back the request. See Transactions.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• The list default is 20 rows. Pass limit=0 (v1) or a larger limit to get more.
  • JSON parameters in a GET URL must be URL-encoded. Use curl -G --data-urlencode.
  • v1 sends results in data for resources and in message for methods. v2 always uses data.
  • v15 v2 list responses have no has_next_page, and v2 read ignores fields.
  • The document method routes check only read (GET) or write (POST). They do not check the methods argument of @frappe.whitelist.

docs.title: Whitelisted Methods
docs.text: A whitelisted method is a Python function that clients can call over HTTP. Add @frappe.whitelist() to a function in your app, and it becomes available at /api/method/<dotted.path> and /api/v2/method/<dotted.path>. The desk calls these methods with frappe.call. Functions without the decorator cannot be called from a client.

docs.title: Write a method
docs.text:
# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_items(category: str, limit: int = 20) -> list[dict]:
    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Item",
        filters={"category": category, "disabled": 0},
        fields=["name", "rate"],
        order_by="rate desc",
        limit=limit,
    )

Call it:

curl -G "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/sample_app.api.get_items" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>" \
  --data-urlencode "category=Hardware" --data-urlencode "limit=2"

{"message": [{"name": "Laptop", "rate": 900.0}, {"name": "Monitor", "rate": 250.0}]}

How the call works (frappe/handler.py):

  1. The path after /api/method/ is the dotted path of the function.
  2. Frappe applies override_whitelisted_methods hooks.
  3. If a Server Script of type API has the same method name, the script runs instead.
  4. Frappe imports the function and checks that it is whitelisted and that the HTTP method is allowed.
  5. Frappe calls the function with the request parameters (frappe.form_dict). Parameters that the function does not declare are dropped, unless it has **kwargs.
  6. The return value goes into message (v1) or data (v2) of the JSON response.

The parameters ignore_permissions and flags are always removed before the call (frappe.get_newargs). A function without the decorator returns HTTP 403 with "Function ... is not whitelisted".

docs.title: Decorator options
docs.text:
frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=False, xss_safe=False, methods=None)
Name Type Default Description allow_guest bool False Allow calls from users who are not logged in. xss_safe bool False With allow_guest: do not sanitize HTML in string arguments of guest calls. methods list all Allowed HTTP methods. Default: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE.

v15 has no other decorator arguments.

docs.title: methods
docs.text:
A call with another HTTP method raises frappe.PermissionError (HTTP 403):

curl "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.client.set_value?doctype=Sample%20Item&name=Laptop&fieldname=rate&value=1" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>"

{"exception": "frappe.exceptions.PermissionError: Not permitted", "exc_type": "PermissionError"}

frappe.client.set_value declares methods=["POST", "PUT"].

Warning

Frappe rolls back the transaction at the end of every GET request. A method that writes data must declare methods=["POST"] (or PUT, DELETE). See Transactions.

docs.title: allow_guest
docs.text:
# sample_app/api.py
import frappe
from frappe.rate_limiter import rate_limit


@frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True, methods=["POST"])
@rate_limit(limit=5, seconds=60 * 60)
def subscribe(email: str):
    frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "Sample Subscriber", "email": email}).insert(ignore_permissions=True)

For guest calls, Frappe sanitizes HTML in every string value of frappe.form_dict (frappe.utils.sanitize_html), unless xss_safe=True.

For each guest method, declare methods and add @rate_limit(...) below @frappe.whitelist.

docs.title: Type annotations
docs.text:
The decorator wraps the function with validate_argument_types (frappe/utils/typing_validations.py). During a request (and in tests), Frappe validates each annotated argument with pydantic. Arguments without annotations are not checked:

  • Values are converted when the conversion is safe. The string "2" becomes 2 for an int argument.
  • A value that does not match raises frappe.FrappeTypeError (HTTP 417).
  • The type of the default value is also accepted. limit: int = None accepts None.
  • Annotations that cannot be resolved at runtime (for example, names imported only under TYPE_CHECKING) are not validated.
  • Direct Python calls outside a request are not validated.
curl -G "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.desk.search.get_names_for_mentions" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>" \
  --data-urlencode "search_term=user" --data-urlencode "page_length=two"

{"exception": "frappe.exceptions.FrappeTypeError: Argument 'page_length' should be of type 'int' but got 'str' instead.", "exc_type": "FrappeTypeError"}

v15 has no setting that makes annotations required. Annotate every argument yourself.

docs.title: Check access
docs.text:
The decorator only decides who can call the function. It does not check data permissions. Check them in the function:

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def close_order(name: str):
    doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name)
    doc.check_permission("write")
    doc.status = "Completed"
    doc.save()
    return doc.status
Tool Use it to frappe.only_for(roles, message=False) Allow only users with one of the roles. Raises frappe.PermissionError. frappe.has_permission(doctype, ptype, doc, throw=True) Check a right on a DocType or document. doc.check_permission(ptype) Check a right on a loaded document. frappe.get_list(...) Query with the permissions of the user.

frappe.core.doctype.user.user.generate_keys is an example. It starts with frappe.only_for("System Manager"). A call from another user returns HTTP 403. See Permissions.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
frappe.rate_limiter.rate_limit limits calls per endpoint. It counts calls in Redis.

rate_limit(key=None, limit=5, seconds=86400, methods="ALL", ip_based=True)
Name Type Default Description key str None Name of a request parameter. Its value is added to the counter key, for example "email". limit int or callable 5 Maximum calls in the window. A callable is evaluated on each call. seconds int 86400 Window length. methods str or list "ALL" Limit only these HTTP methods. ip_based bool True Count per client IP. With key, count per IP and key value.

When the limit is reached, the call raises frappe.RateLimitExceededError (HTTP 429). The limit applies only to HTTP requests. Direct Python calls are not counted.

Warning

Put @rate_limit below @frappe.whitelist. If it is above, the registered function is not the one that the module exports, and the method is not whitelisted.

The site config key rate_limit ({"limit": <seconds>, "window": <seconds>}) is a separate limit. It limits the total request processing time per site in each window. Over the limit, requests get HTTP 429. See Configuration.

docs.title: Controller methods
docs.text:
Whitelist a method of a DocType controller to call it on one document:

# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
import frappe
from frappe.model.document import Document


class SampleOrder(Document):
    @frappe.whitelist()
    def mark_completed(self):
        self.status = "Completed"
        self.save()
Route Permission checked POST /api/resource/Sample Order/SO-00001 with run_method=mark_completed write GET /api/resource/Sample Order/SO-00001?run_method=mark_completed read POST /api/v2/document/Sample Order/SO-00001/method/mark_completed write GET /api/v2/document/Sample Order/SO-00001/method/mark_completed read

The method also needs @frappe.whitelist(). These four routes do not check the methods argument of the decorator. Only frm.call (run_doc_method) and /api/v2/method/run_doc_method check it. In the desk, call it with frm.call("mark_completed"). See Form scripts.

A module-level function in a DocType module can be called by DocType name in v2: /api/v2/method/<DocType>/<function>. For example /api/v2/method/User/get_current_user_roles calls frappe.core.doctype.user.user.get_current_user_roles.

docs.title: Override a method of another app
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
override_whitelisted_methods = {
    "frappe.desk.doctype.event.event.get_events": "sample_app.overrides.get_events",
}
  • The key is the dotted path that clients call. The value is your function.
  • The new function must also be whitelisted.
  • If several apps override the same path, the app installed last wins.
  • The override applies to HTTP calls only. Python code that imports the original function still calls it.

See Extending apps.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A whitelisted method is a public endpoint. Validate every argument and check permissions in the function.
  • Do not use frappe.get_all or ignore_permissions=True to return data to the caller unless all callers may see all rows.
  • Do not build SQL from arguments. Use the Query builder or parameters.
  • Return values must be JSON serializable.

docs.title: Building Apps
docs.text:
Create an app, use hooks, extend other apps, ship fixtures and patches, and translate.

Page What it covers Apps Create a Frappe app, understand its files and folders, install it on a site, and build its assets. Hooks How hooks.py works, how hook values from all apps merge, and the hooks that apps use most. Extending Other Apps Change the behavior of DocTypes and methods from another app with doc_events, controller overrides, method overrides, doctype_js, custom fields and property setters. Fixtures and Patches Ship records with an app through the fixtures hook, change data on existing sites with patches, and understand the order of bench migrate. Translations Mark strings with _() in Python and __() in JS, use context and lazy strings, keep PO/POT files in an app, and run the bench translation commands.

docs.title: Apps
docs.text: An app is a Python package that adds DocTypes, pages, hooks, APIs and assets to a site. All your code goes in an app. Do not edit frappe or other apps that you do not own. Use an app when you need code-level changes. Use Customize Form or Server and Client Scripts for small changes that a site admin can make.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
• A bench holds many apps in apps/. The file sites/apps.txt lists the apps on the bench.
  • A site uses only the apps that are installed on it. The list is stored in the installed_apps global default.
  • An app has one or more modules. Each module is a folder in the app package. DocTypes, reports and pages belong to a module.
  • frappe is always the first app. Other apps follow in the order of installation.

See Architecture for the bench, site and app model.

docs.title: Create an app
docs.text:
1. Go to the bench root.
  2. Run bench new-app.
cd ~/frappe-bench
bench new-app sample_app

bench new-app is a command of the bench CLI. It calls the Frappe command bench make-app apps sample_app. Then it installs the package into the bench virtual environment, adds the app to sites/apps.txt and builds assets.

bench make-app DESTINATION APP_NAME writes only the files. Use --no-git to skip git init. The app name is converted to snake case with frappe.scrub. The command stops if a site has the same name as the app.

The command asks these questions:

Prompt Default Notes App Title App name in title case Must start with a letter. Letters, numbers, spaces and underscores only. App Description none App Publisher none App Email none Must be a valid email address. App License mit Choices come from the GitHub licenses API. If the API is not reachable, the choices are agpl-3.0, gpl-3.0, mit and custom. Create GitHub Workflow action for unittests False Adds .github/workflows/ci.yml and linter.yml.

Without --no-git, the command runs git init with the branch develop and makes a first commit "feat: Initialize App".

docs.title: Files and folders
docs.text:
bench make-app makes this tree (frappe/utils/boilerplate.py):

apps/sample_app/                  # git repository
├── pyproject.toml
├── README.md
├── license.txt
├── .gitignore                    # not written with --no-git
├── .pre-commit-config.yaml
├── .editorconfig
├── .eslintrc
├── .github/workflows/            # only if you answer yes to the workflow prompt
└── sample_app/                   # Python package
    ├── __init__.py               # __version__ = "0.0.1"
    ├── hooks.py
    ├── modules.txt               # contains the App Title
    ├── patches.txt
    ├── config/__init__.py
    ├── patches/__init__.py
    ├── public/
    │   ├── .gitkeep
    │   ├── css/
    │   └── js/
    ├── templates/
    │   ├── __init__.py
    │   ├── includes/
    │   └── pages/__init__.py
    ├── www/
    └── sample_app/               # first module, named from the App Title
        └── __init__.py
Path Purpose pyproject.toml Package metadata. Build backend is flit_core. The version is read from __init__.py. sample_app/__init__.py Holds __version__. sample_app/hooks.py App metadata and hooks. See Hooks. sample_app/modules.txt One module name per line. frappe.get_module_list(app) reads the modules of an app from this file. sample_app/patches.txt Patches that bench migrate runs. See Fixtures and Patches. sample_app/public/ Static assets. Served at /assets/sample_app/. sample_app/templates/ Jinja templates for web pages and includes. sample_app/www/ Web pages that map to URL paths. See Website. sample_app/<module>/ A module folder with an __init__.py.

The first module is the App Title. Its folder name is the scrubbed App Title. For the title "Sample App" it is sample_app. This is the same as the package name, so the path is sample_app/sample_app/sample_app/.

docs.title: pyproject.toml
docs.text:
The generated file sets requires-python = ">=3.10" and ruff settings with target-version = "py310". Two bench-specific tables are present:

Table Use [tool.bench.dev-dependencies] Python packages that bench installs only when developer mode is on. [deploy.dependencies.apt] packages list of apt packages for Frappe Cloud.

Do not add frappe to dependencies. Bench installs and manages it. The template has the line # "frappe~=15.0.0" as a comment only.

docs.title: Module folders
docs.text:
When you save a standard DocType in developer mode, Frappe writes its files into the module folder:

sample_app/selling/                 # module "Selling"
└── doctype/
    └── sample_order/
        ├── __init__.py
        ├── sample_order.json       # the DocType definition
        ├── sample_order.py         # the controller
        ├── sample_order.js         # the form script
        └── test_sample_order.py    # the test file

Folder and file names are the scrubbed names (lowercase, spaces become underscores). See DocTypes for the JSON and Controllers for the Python class.

To add a module, create a Module Def record in developer mode and set App Name to your app. On save, ModuleDef.on_update makes the module folder with an __init__.py and adds the name to modules.txt. Without developer mode, it does neither.

If you add a name to modules.txt by hand, bench migrate does not create the Module Def record. install-app adds Module Def records only when it installs the app. Saving a DocType of the module also creates a missing Module Def.

docs.title: Install an app on a site
docs.text:
1. Get the app into the bench. Use bench new-app or bench get-app <git-url>.
  2. Install it on the site.
bench --site frappe.localhost install-app sample_app

install-app accepts more than one app. Use --force to install again over an existing install.

frappe.installer.install_app runs these steps in this order:

  1. Install each app in required_apps first.
  2. Stop with an error if the app is not in sites/apps.txt.
  3. If the app is already installed and --force is not set, print a message and stop.
  4. Check that the user has the System Manager role (not for frappe).
  5. Run the before_install hooks of the app. If one returns False, stop.
  6. Run the before_app_install hooks of the installed apps. Each gets the app name.
  7. Add a Module Def for each module in modules.txt.
  8. Sync all DocTypes of the app from their JSON files.
  9. Add the app to installed_apps and commit.
  10. Sync the Portal Settings menu.
  11. Mark all patches in patches.txt as done. A new install does not run old patches.
  12. Run the after_install hooks of the app.
  13. Run the after_app_install hooks of the installed apps.
  14. Sync scheduled jobs, fixtures, customizations and dashboards.
  15. Run the after_sync hooks of the app.

install_app does not roll back on an error after step 9. The app stays in installed_apps.

To remove an app from a site, use bench --site <site> uninstall-app sample_app. Add --dry-run to list the DocTypes that it deletes. Other options are --no-backup and --force.

docs.title: Required apps
docs.text:
Declare other apps that your app needs in hooks.py:

# sample_app/hooks.py
required_apps = ["frappe/erpnext"]

An entry can be an app name (erpnext), an org/repo (frappe/erpnext) or a git URL. Each can end with @branch. install-app installs the required apps first. bench get-app --resolve-deps also fetches them.

docs.title: Build assets
docs.text:
Frappe bundles files whose name matches *.bundle.{js,ts,css,sass,scss,less,styl,jsx} under public/. Other files in public/ are served as they are.

bench build --app sample_app
Option Description --app TEXT Build assets for one app. --apps TEXT Build assets for some apps. --production Build in production mode. Without it, the mode is development when developer_mode is on. --hard-link Copy the files instead of making symlinks. Also set by the env var FRAPPE_HARD_LINK_ASSETS. --force Build the frappe assets instead of downloading them. --verbose Print more output. --save-metafiles Save esbuild metafiles to analyze bundle size.

Without --force, --app, --apps or the env var CI, bench build tries to download prebuilt frappe assets and skips the frappe build if that works.

sites/assets/sample_app is a symlink to apps/sample_app/sample_app/public. Built bundles go into public/dist/. Include a bundle in the desk with the app_include_js or app_include_css hook:

# sample_app/hooks.py
app_include_js = "sample_app.bundle.js"     # built from public/js/sample_app.bundle.js
app_include_css = "sample_app.bundle.css"

During development, bench watch rebuilds bundles when files change. Use --apps to watch some apps only. The watch process in the bench Procfile runs it.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not delete public/.gitkeep. Without the public folder, bench build does not link the assets of the app.
  • bench make-app does not install the app into the environment. Use bench new-app, or run bench get-app on the folder.
  • A module that you add to modules.txt by hand has no Module Def until you save a DocType in it. Create the Module Def record instead.
  • You can save standard DocTypes only in developer mode. Set developer_mode to 1 in site_config.json on your development site. See Configuration.

docs.title: Extending Other Apps
docs.text: Use the hooks on this page when your app must change a DocType or a method that another app owns. Do not edit the other app. Your changes stay in your app and survive updates of the other app. Each hook goes in your app's hooks.py. Frappe merges the hook values of all installed apps. For how merging works, see Hooks.

docs.title: Choose a mechanism
docs.text: Need Use Run code when a document of another app is saved, submitted, deleted doc_events Add or change methods of another app's controller, or replace it override_doctype_class Replace a whitelisted method override_whitelisted_methods Add form, list, tree or calendar JavaScript to another app's DocType doctype_js, doctype_list_js, doctype_tree_js, doctype_calendar_js Add fields to another app's DocType Custom Field (create_custom_fields or exported customizations) Change a property of a field or DocType (label, hidden, reqd, options) Property Setter (make_property_setter) Replace the link search query of a DocType standard_queries Change the dashboard (connections) of a DocType override_doctype_dashboards Send extra data to the desk on page load boot_session

docs.title: doc_events
docs.text:
doc_events maps a DocType name (or "*" for all DocTypes) to controller events. Each event has a dotted path or a list of dotted paths.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doc_events = {
    "ToDo": {
        "validate": "sample_app.events.todo.validate",
        "on_update": ["sample_app.events.todo.notify_owner"],
    },
    "*": {
        "on_trash": "sample_app.events.common.log_delete",
    },
}

# sample_app/events/todo.py
import frappe
from frappe import _


def validate(doc, method=None):
    if doc.priority == "High" and not doc.date:
        frappe.throw(_("Set a due date for high priority tasks"))
  • Frappe calls the handler with two arguments: the document and the event name. Always accept both: def validate(doc, method=None).
  • Handlers run after the controller method of the same name (Document.hook in frappe/model/document.py). Handlers of the DocType run before the handlers of "*".
  • Do not call frappe.db.commit() inside a handler. In v15 it commits the half-saved document. Use frappe.db.after_commit.add(fn) for side effects that must happen after the commit.
  • Any event that run_method calls works: before_insert, validate, on_update, on_submit, on_cancel, on_trash, after_insert and others. See Controllers for the order.

docs.title: override_doctype_class
docs.text:
override_doctype_class replaces the controller class. Only the last value is used, so only one app can override a DocType. v15 has no hook to add a mixin to a controller.

Version

v16 adds extend_doctype_class, which adds mixin classes to a controller so that several apps can extend one DocType.

# sample_app/hooks.py
override_doctype_class = {
    "ToDo": "sample_app.overrides.todo.CustomToDo",
}

# sample_app/overrides/todo.py
from frappe.desk.doctype.todo.todo import ToDo


class CustomToDo(ToDo):
    def on_update(self):
        super().on_update()
        # your code
  • Subclass the original controller and call super(), so the original logic still runs. Frappe only checks that the class is a subclass of Document. If it is not, get_controller raises ImportError.
  • Frappe does not warn when two apps override the same DocType. The app that comes last in the hook order wins.
  • The hook has no effect on custom DocTypes (custom = 1). They always use Document.

docs.title: override_whitelisted_methods
docs.text:
override_whitelisted_methods maps the dotted path of a whitelisted method to your replacement. The last app in the hook list wins.

# sample_app/hooks.py
override_whitelisted_methods = {
    "frappe.desk.doctype.event.event.get_events": "sample_app.overrides.event.get_events",
}
  • The override applies to /api/method/<path> and /api/v2/method/<path> (frappe/handler.py, frappe/api/v2.py).
  • The replacement must also have @frappe.whitelist(). Frappe checks the replacement, not the original.
  • Keep the same parameters as the original. Callers do not know about the override.
  • The hook does not change Python calls to the original function. It changes only HTTP calls.

docs.title: doctype_js and related hooks
docs.text:
These hooks add JavaScript files from your app to the views of another app's DocType. The path is relative to your app package.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doctype_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo.js"}
doctype_list_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo_list.js"}

// sample_app/public/js/todo.js
frappe.ui.form.on("ToDo", {
    refresh(frm) {
        frm.add_custom_button(__("Mark Urgent"), () => {
            frm.set_value("priority", "High").then(() => frm.save());
        });
    },
});

Frappe reads the file on each meta load and appends it to the form script (frappe/desk/form/meta.py). You do not need to build assets for these files. The value can be a list of paths. The hooks have no effect on custom DocTypes. See Form Scripts for the form API.

docs.title: Custom fields from code
docs.text:
Use create_custom_fields to add fields to another app's DocType. Call it from after_install and from after_migrate, so that the fields also exist on sites that update.

# sample_app/hooks.py
after_install = "sample_app.setup.make_custom_fields"
after_migrate = "sample_app.setup.make_custom_fields"

# sample_app/setup.py
from frappe.custom.doctype.custom_field.custom_field import create_custom_fields


def make_custom_fields():
    create_custom_fields(
        {
            "ToDo": [
                {
                    "fieldname": "sample_code",
                    "label": "Sample Code",
                    "fieldtype": "Data",
                    "insert_after": "description",
                },
            ],
        }
    )

create_custom_fields(custom_fields, ignore_validate=False, update=True):

Name Type Default Description custom_fields dict Key: a DocType name or a tuple of names. Value: one field dict or a list of field dicts. ignore_validate bool False Skip field validation. update bool True Update fields that exist. If False, only missing fields are inserted.
  • Fields are created with owner Administrator and is_system_generated set. Only Administrator can delete them.
  • The function clears the DocType cache and adds the columns with frappe.db.updatedb.
  • delete_custom_fields({"ToDo": ["sample_code"]}) removes fields. It does not drop the database column.

docs.title: Exported customizations
docs.text: In developer mode, Customize Form has an Export Customizations action. It writes Custom Fields and Property Setters of a DocType to <app>/<module>/custom/<doctype>.json (export_customizations in frappe/modules/utils.py). If the file has "sync_on_migrate": 1, bench migrate syncs it on every site. Use this when you build the fields in the desk. Use create_custom_fields when you prefer to keep fields in Python.

docs.title: Property setters from code
docs.text:
A Property Setter changes one property of a DocType or of a field, without changing the DocType JSON.

from frappe.custom.doctype.property_setter.property_setter import make_property_setter

make_property_setter("ToDo", "priority", "default", "High", "Data")
make_property_setter("ToDo", None, "sort_field", "date", "Data", for_doctype=True)

make_property_setter(doctype, fieldname, property, value, property_type, for_doctype=False, validate_fields_for_doctype=True, is_system_generated=True):

  • Ignores permissions.
  • Deletes the old Property Setter for the same DocType, field and property, then inserts the new one. The name is <doctype>-<field or "main">-<property>.
  • Clears the DocType cache.

frappe.make_property_setter(args, ...) is a second form. It takes a dict with doctype, fieldname, property, value and optional property_type. If doctype is not set, it applies to every DocType that has a field with that fieldname.

docs.title: standard_queries
docs.text:
standard_queries replaces the search query that Link fields use for a DocType. Frappe uses the last value. The method must be whitelisted.

# sample_app/hooks.py
standard_queries = {"Sample Item": "sample_app.queries.sample_item_query"}

# sample_app/queries.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
@frappe.validate_and_sanitize_search_inputs
def sample_item_query(doctype, txt, searchfield, start, page_len, filters):
    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Item",
        filters={"disabled": 0, "item_name": ["like", f"%{txt}%"]},
        fields=["name", "item_name"],
        limit_start=start,
        limit_page_length=page_len,
        as_list=True,
    )

Frappe calls the method with doctype, txt, searchfield, start, page_len, filters (frappe/desk/search.py). A query set by a form script with frm.set_query takes priority over this hook.

docs.title: override_doctype_dashboards
docs.text:
Each method gets the dashboard data as data and returns the changed data. Frappe calls all methods in order (frappe/model/meta.py).

# sample_app/hooks.py
override_doctype_dashboards = {"ToDo": "sample_app.overrides.todo.get_dashboard_data"}

# sample_app/overrides/todo.py
def get_dashboard_data(data):
    data.setdefault("transactions", []).append({"label": "Sample", "items": ["Sample Order"]})
    return data

The data dict can be empty when the DocType has no <doctype>_dashboard.py file. Use setdefault for keys that can be missing.

docs.title: boot_session
docs.text:
Each method gets the bootinfo dict before the desk loads (frappe/boot.py). Add keys to it. The client reads them from frappe.boot.

# sample_app/hooks.py
boot_session = "sample_app.boot.boot_session"

# sample_app/boot.py
def boot_session(bootinfo):
    bootinfo.sample_app_settings = {"show_banner": True}

The method runs on every desk load. Keep it fast. Do not run queries per DocType or per record.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• override_doctype_class allows one winner. Two apps that override the same DocType break each other. Use doc_events when you only need to run code on an event.
  • A doc_events handler runs for every save, also for imports and API calls. Check doc.flags or field changes with doc.has_value_changed("field") before you do heavy work.
  • Do not call frappe.db.commit() in a doc_events handler. It commits a document that has not finished saving.
  • create_custom_fields only runs where you call it. Call it from after_migrate too, or sites that update do not get new fields.
  • doctype_js files are not bundled. Do not use import statements in them.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Hooks
  • Controllers
  • Fixtures and Patches
  • Customize Form
  • Whitelisted Methods
  • Hooks reference

docs.title: Fixtures and Patches
docs.text: Fixtures and patches move data with your app. Use fixtures for records that must be the same on every site, such as Custom Fields, Property Setters, Roles or Workflows. Use patches for one-time changes to the data of sites that already exist, such as a field rename or a backfill. Both run during bench migrate.

docs.title: Declare fixtures
docs.text:
Add the fixtures hook to hooks.py. Each item is a DocType name or a dict with filters.

# sample_app/hooks.py
fixtures = [
    "Sample Role",
    {"dt": "Custom Field", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]},
    {"dt": "Property Setter", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]},
    {"doctype": "Workflow", "or_filters": [["name", "=", "Sample Order Approval"]]},
]
Key Type Description dt or doctype str The DocType to export. filters list or dict Filters for frappe.get_all. Exports only matching records. or_filters list or dict OR filters for frappe.get_all.

Without filters, every record of the DocType is exported. Filter Custom Fields and Property Setters by module, or you export the customizations of all apps.

Each fixture writes one file named after the DocType. You cannot export one DocType into more than one file. If you list the same DocType two times, the second export replaces the first file.

docs.title: Export fixtures
docs.text:
Run this on a site that has the records:

bench --site frappe.localhost export-fixtures --app sample_app

Frappe writes one JSON file per fixture to sample_app/fixtures/<scrubbed_doctype>.json (for example custom_field.json). It removes owner, creation, modified_by, idx, lft and rgt from each record. Records are sorted by idx and creation. Without --app, Frappe exports the fixtures of all installed apps.

docs.title: Import fixtures
docs.text:
bench migrate and bench install-app call sync_fixtures. It imports every .json file in <app>/fixtures/, sorted by file name. To control the import order, give the files names that sort in the order you need.

  • An existing record with the same name is deleted and inserted again. Changes made on the site to a fixture record are lost on the next migrate.
  • A record that you remove from the JSON file is not deleted from sites.
  • If the DocType of a file does not exist, Frappe prints "Skipping fixture syncing" and goes on.
  • Emails are muted during the import. Each file is committed.
  • frappe.flags.in_fixtures is set during the import.

Warning

<app>/fixtures/custom_scripts/*.js files are not imported. Frappe prints an error for each one. Export Client Scripts as a Client Script fixture instead.

docs.title: Fixtures or exported customizations
docs.text: For Custom Fields and Property Setters you can also use Export Customizations in Customize Form. That writes <app>/<module>/custom/<doctype>.json. Files with "sync_on_migrate": 1 sync on every migrate. See Extending Other Apps.

docs.title: Patches
docs.text: A patch is a Python module with an execute() function. Frappe runs each patch once per site and records it in Patch Log.

docs.title: Write a patch
docs.text:
# sample_app/patches/v1_0/set_default_category.py
import frappe


def execute():
    """Set category of old Sample Items to Hardware."""
    frappe.db.set_value(
        "Sample Item",
        {"category": ("is", "not set")},
        "category",
        "Hardware",
        update_modified=False,
    )
  • Frappe prints the docstring when the patch runs.
  • Frappe commits before and after the patch. If the patch raises an error, Frappe rolls back and stops the migrate.
  • During a patch frappe.flags.in_patch is set and developer_mode is off. Files are not written back to the app.
  • Server Script DocType events do not run during a migrate.

docs.title: Register the patch
docs.text:
Add the dotted path to <app>/patches.txt. Use the INI format with two sections:

# sample_app/patches.txt
[pre_model_sync]
sample_app.patches.v1_0.rename_old_field

[post_model_sync]
sample_app.patches.v1_0.set_default_category
execute:frappe.db.set_single_value("System Settings", "enable_onboarding", 0)
Section Runs Use for [pre_model_sync] Before DocType JSON is synced Patches that need the old schema, for example to copy data out of a column that the new JSON removes. [post_model_sync] After DocType JSON is synced Most patches. New fields and DocTypes exist.
  • Both sections are required in INI format. If one is missing, the migrate stops with "Patch type ... not found in patches.txt".
  • A file without section headers is read in the old format. All lines are pre_model_sync patches.
  • A line that starts with execute: runs the Python code after the prefix.
  • A line that starts with finally: runs after all other patches of the same pass.
  • To run a patch again on all sites, change its line, for example add a comment: sample_app.patches.v1_0.set_default_category #2. Patch Log stores the full line.

docs.title: Run patches
docs.text:
bench --site frappe.localhost migrate
bench --site frappe.localhost run-patch sample_app.patches.v1_0.set_default_category
bench --site frappe.localhost run-patch --force sample_app.patches.v1_0.set_default_category

run-patch runs one patch if it is not in Patch Log. --force runs it again.

bench migrate --skip-failing writes a failing patch to Patch Log with skipped set and goes on. Frappe tries the patch again on the next migrate. To stop the migrate for a patch even with --skip-failing, list it in the never_skip_patches hook:

# sample_app/hooks.py
never_skip_patches = ["sample_app.patches.v1_0.critical_data_fix"]

docs.title: Order of bench migrate
docs.text:
SiteMigration in frappe/migrate.py runs these steps for each site. It takes a file lock, so only one migrate runs at a time.

  1. Check that Redis cache is running. If not, stop.
  2. Clear the cache and set frappe.flags.in_migrate.
  3. Run before_migrate hooks of each app.
  4. Run [pre_model_sync] patches.
  5. Sync DocType JSON and other standard files of all apps (frappe.model.sync.sync_all).
  6. Run [post_model_sync] patches.
  7. Sync Scheduled Job Types from scheduler_events.
  8. Sync fixtures.
  9. Sync dashboards and exported customizations.
  10. Sync languages, flush deferred inserts, remove orphan DocTypes.
  11. Sync the Portal Settings menu and update Installed Applications.
  12. Run after_migrate hooks of each app.

Step 3, steps 4 to 6 and steps 7 to 12 each commit at the end, or roll back on error. After the migrate, Frappe clears the translation, website and notification caches. It queues a rebuild of the website search index on the long queue (skip it with --skip-search-index). It also sends a version-update realtime event to open desks.

# sample_app/hooks.py
before_migrate = "sample_app.migrate.before_migrate"
after_migrate = ["sample_app.setup.make_custom_fields"]

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not call frappe.get_doc and doc.save() on many records in a patch. Use frappe.db.set_value with filters, frappe.qb.update or frappe.db.bulk_update.
  • A patch in [pre_model_sync] cannot use new fields. Put patches that read old data there, and check the column with frappe.db.has_column first, because new sites never had it.
  • A patch that needs Custom Fields or records from fixtures cannot run in patches.txt before step 8. Run that code in an after_migrate hook and make it safe to run more than one time.
  • Fixture records are replaced on every migrate. Do not use fixtures for records that users edit.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: hooks.py is the file where an app tells Frappe what to add or change. Each hook is a module-level variable. Frappe reads the hooks of all installed apps and merges them. Use hooks to run code on document events, add assets, add scheduled jobs, override classes and methods, and react to install and migrate. This page explains how hooks work and shows the hooks that apps use most. For every hook key, see the Hooks reference.

docs.title: How Frappe reads hooks
docs.text:
frappe.get_hooks loads <app>.hooks for each installed app (frappe/__init__.py, _load_app_hooks):

  • Apps are read in the order of installed_apps. frappe is first.
  • Apps in installed_apps that are not in the bench are skipped.
  • Every module-level name that does not start with _ is a hook. Imported modules, functions and classes are skipped.
# sample_app/hooks.py
app_name = "sample_app"
app_title = "Sample App"

doc_events = {
    "Sample Order": {
        "on_submit": "sample_app.events.notify_customer",
    },
}

docs.title: How values merge
docs.text:
frappe.append_hook merges the value of each app into one dict:

Value in hooks.py Merged result A string or number A list. Each app appends its value. A list One list. Each app extends it. A dict A dict. Keys merge across apps, and each leaf becomes a list.

So frappe.get_hooks("app_name") returns a list, even though each app sets a string:

frappe.get_hooks("app_name")
# ['frappe', 'sample_app']

frappe.get_hooks("doc_events")["*"]["on_update"]
# ['frappe.desk.notifications.clear_doctype_notifications', ...]   one list for all apps

Most hooks call every value in the list, in app order. Some hooks use only the last value:

Hook Which value wins override_whitelisted_methods The last app in installed_apps that overrides the method. override_doctype_class The last app that overrides the DocType.

docs.title: Read hooks in your code
docs.text:
# all apps
for method in frappe.get_hooks("after_migrate"):
    frappe.get_attr(method)()

# one app only
frappe.get_hooks("fixtures", app_name="sample_app")

# a default when the hook is not set
frappe.get_hooks("my_hook", default={})
Parameter Type Default Description hook str None Hook name. If None, return all hooks as a dict. default any [] Value to return when no app sets the hook. app_name str None Read the hooks of this app only.

Hooks are cached:

  • Developer mode off: in the Redis cache (frappe.cache), key app_hooks.
  • Developer mode on: not cached between requests. Frappe reloads them per request.
  • In both modes, the result is cached for the length of one request (request_cache).

bench --site <site> clear-cache clears the Redis cache. Run it after you change hooks.py on a site that is not in developer mode. Also restart the bench processes, because workers keep loaded Python modules.

docs.title: App metadata
docs.text:
bench make-app writes these values. They are also read as hooks.

# sample_app/hooks.py
app_name = "sample_app"
app_title = "Sample App"
app_publisher = "Example Corp"
app_description = "Sample app"
app_email = "admin@example.com"
app_license = "mit"

All other hooks in the generated hooks.py are comments. One of them is export_python_type_annotations = True. Uncomment it to make Frappe write field type hints into the controllers of the app when you save a DocType in developer mode.

docs.title: Install, uninstall and migrate
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
required_apps = ["frappe/erpnext"]

before_install = "sample_app.install.before_install"
after_install = "sample_app.install.after_install"
after_sync = "sample_app.install.after_sync"

before_uninstall = "sample_app.uninstall.before_uninstall"
after_uninstall = "sample_app.uninstall.after_uninstall"

# called with the name of the app that is installed or uninstalled
after_app_install = "sample_app.utils.after_app_install"
before_app_uninstall = "sample_app.utils.before_app_uninstall"

before_migrate = "sample_app.migrate.before_migrate"
after_migrate = "sample_app.migrate.after_migrate"
Hook When it runs required_apps install-app installs these apps first. before_install Before the DocTypes of this app are synced. Return False to stop the install. after_install After the app is added to installed_apps and its patches are marked as done. after_sync At the end of install, after fixtures and customizations are synced. before_app_install, after_app_install When any app is installed. The function gets the app name. before_uninstall, after_uninstall When this app is uninstalled. before_app_uninstall, after_app_uninstall When any app is uninstalled. The function gets the app name. before_migrate, after_migrate At the start and end of bench migrate.

See Apps for the full install order.

docs.title: Document events
docs.text:
doc_events runs functions on controller events of any DocType. The key is a DocType name, a tuple of names, or "*" for all DocTypes.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doc_events = {
    "Sample Order": {
        "validate": "sample_app.events.check_credit_limit",
        "on_submit": [
            "sample_app.events.notify_customer",
            "sample_app.events.update_stock",
        ],
    },
    ("Sample Item", "Sample Order"): {
        "on_trash": "sample_app.events.log_delete",
    },
    "*": {
        "on_update": "sample_app.events.audit",
    },
}

# sample_app/events.py
import frappe


def check_credit_limit(doc, method):
    if doc.total > 100000:
        frappe.throw(frappe._("Total is over the credit limit"))


def audit(doc, method):
    frappe.logger().info(f"{doc.doctype} {doc.name} updated")

The handler gets two positional arguments: the document and the event name. Every handler must accept both. Handlers run after the controller method. See Controllers for the event order.

Warning

Do not call frappe.db.commit() in a doc_events handler. In v15 the call commits the open transaction. A later error in the same save cannot roll back the work that was committed.

docs.title: Override controllers and methods
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
override_doctype_class = {
    "ToDo": "sample_app.overrides.todo.CustomToDo",
}

override_whitelisted_methods = {
    "frappe.desk.doctype.event.event.get_events": "sample_app.event.get_events",
}
Hook Rule override_doctype_class The class must be a subclass of Document. Frappe raises ImportError if it is not. Subclass the original controller to keep its logic. override_whitelisted_methods Requests to the original dotted path call the new function.

override_doctype_class has no effect on custom DocTypes (custom = 1). Custom DocTypes always use Document or NestedSet. See Extending Apps.

docs.title: Desk and web assets
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
app_include_js = "sample_app.bundle.js"
app_include_css = "sample_app.bundle.css"
web_include_js = "sample_app_web.bundle.js"
web_include_css = "sample_app_web.bundle.css"

doctype_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo.js"}
doctype_list_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo_list.js"}
Hook Effect app_include_js, app_include_css Load in every desk page. web_include_js, web_include_css Load in every website page. doctype_js Add a form script to a DocType of another app. Path is relative to the app package. doctype_list_js, doctype_tree_js, doctype_calendar_js Add view scripts the same way.

See Form Scripts and List View Settings.

docs.title: Scheduled jobs
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
scheduler_events = {
    "daily": ["sample_app.tasks.send_reminders"],
    "cron": {
        "0/15 * * * *": ["sample_app.tasks.sync_orders"],
    },
}

See Scheduler.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
permission_query_conditions = {
    "Sample Order": "sample_app.permissions.sample_order_query",
}
has_permission = {
    "Sample Order": "sample_app.permissions.sample_order_has_permission",
}

See Permissions.

docs.title: Fixtures
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
fixtures = [
    "Sample Role",
    {"dt": "Custom Field", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]},
]

An entry is a DocType name or a dict with dt (or doctype), filters and or_filters. See Fixtures and Patches.

docs.title: Requests, sessions and templates
docs.text: Hook Shape Effect before_request, after_request list of dotted paths Run before and after each HTTP request. after_request functions get response and request. boot_session list of dotted paths Each function gets bootinfo and can add keys for the desk. extend_bootinfo list of dotted paths Each function gets bootinfo= as a keyword argument. jinja dict with methods and filters Add functions and filters to the Jinja environment. website_route_rules list of {"from_route", "to_route"} Map URL patterns to pages. See Website.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A hook value that is a function object, class or module is ignored. Always use a dotted path string.
  • Names that start with _ are not hooks. Use them for private helpers in hooks.py.
  • A typo in a hook key fails without an error. Frappe reads only the keys it knows.
  • Two apps that override the same DocType class do not both apply. Only the last one wins, without a warning.
  • A doc_events handler with one parameter fails with TypeError. Accept doc and method.
  • After you edit hooks.py, clear the cache and restart the bench processes.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text: Frappe translates user-facing strings at run time. You mark a string in code, and Frappe looks it up in the translations of the user's language. In v15, translations come from CSV files and PO files in each app, and from Translation documents that users add in the desk. Mark every string that a user sees.

docs.title: Mark strings in Python
docs.text:
import frappe
from frappe import _

frappe.throw(_("Rate must be more than zero"), title=_("Invalid Rate"))
frappe.msgprint(_("{0} is mandatory").format(_("Rate")))
_("Change", context="Coins")

_(msg, lang=None, context=None) returns the translation in lang, or in frappe.local.lang when lang is empty. When no translation exists, it returns msg.

_("Save", lang="de")                           # 'Speichern'
_("{0} is mandatory", lang="de").format("Rate")  # 'Rate ist zwingend erforderlich'
_("Unknown sample string", lang="de")          # 'Unknown sample string'

Rules for the message:

  • Pass a literal string. The extractor reads the source code, so _(variable) and f-strings are not extracted.
  • Use {0}, {1} placeholders and call .format() on the result. Do not format before you translate.
  • Use context when one English word has more than one meaning. Frappe looks up "<msg>:<context>" first, then msg.

docs.title: Lazy strings
docs.text:
At import time, the language is not known. Use _lt() for strings in module scope, for example in class attributes or constants. It returns a _LazyTranslate object that translates when it is turned into a string.

from frappe import _lt

STATUS_LABELS = {"Open": _lt("Open"), "Completed": _lt("Completed")}

str(STATUS_LABELS["Open"])  # translated in the current language

N_(msg) marks a string for extraction and returns it unchanged. Use it when you translate the value later with _().

docs.title: Print in another language
docs.text:
frappe.translate.print_language(lang) is a context manager. Inside it, _() and Jinja templates use lang.

from frappe.translate import print_language

with print_language("de"):
    pdf = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001", as_pdf=True)

docs.title: Mark strings in JavaScript
docs.text:
__(txt, replace, context) is the client function (frappe/public/js/frappe/translate.js). replace is a list of values for {0}, {1}.

frappe.msgprint(__("Rate must be more than zero"));
frappe.show_alert(__("{0} items added", [count]));
__("Change", null, "Coins");

The desk loads all translations of the user's language at boot. frappe.boot.load_translations puts them in bootinfo.__messages (from frappe.translate.get_messages_for_boot), and the client keeps them in frappe._messages.

docs.title: Strings in Jinja, DocTypes and JSON
docs.text:
• In Jinja templates, use {{ _("Total") }}. _ is a template global.
  • DocType labels, descriptions, Select options, workspace labels, report names and Web Form labels are extracted from the JSON files. The desk translates them with __().
  • Field values are not translated. To show translated values of a Link field, set translated_doctype on the target DocType. The desk then translates link titles, and link search matches the translated text (frappe/desk/search.py).
  • translatable on a DocField adds a translate button next to the field in the form. Users with write access to Translation can add a translation of the field value there.

docs.title: Where translations come from
docs.text:
get_all_translations(lang) merges these sources and caches the result in Redis:

  1. CSV files: <app>/translations/<lang>.csv. Frappe v15 still ships these files.
  2. MO files: sites/assets/locale/<lang>/LC_MESSAGES/<app>.mo, compiled from <app>/locale/<lang>.po. For each app, MO values win over CSV values.
  3. Translation documents for the language (made in the desk).
  4. Translated country names.

A child language (for example es-GT) first gets the parent language (es), then its own values. Later sources win.

docs.title: CSV or PO files
docs.text: v15 reads both formats. New apps should use PO files. Frappe itself has both frappe/translations/*.csv and frappe/locale/*.po. Use bench update-csv-from-po to copy PO translations into CSV files, and bench migrate-csv-to-po for the other way.

docs.title: PO files in an app
docs.text:
sample_app/sample_app/locale/
├── main.pot     # all strings of the app, made by generate-pot-file
├── de.po        # German translations
└── fr.po
  1. Run bench generate-pot-file --app sample_app to extract strings into main.pot.
  2. Run bench create-po-file de --app sample_app to start a new language.
  3. Run bench update-po-files --app sample_app to sync existing PO files with the POT file.
  4. Translate the msgstr entries in the PO file.
  5. Run bench compile-po-to-mo --app sample_app to build the MO files.
  6. Run bench --site <site> clear-cache so the site loads the new translations.

bench build also compiles PO files when they changed. Use bench build --force to compile all.

The extractor (Babel with frappe/gettext/extractors) finds _(), _lt() and N_() in Python, __() in JS, HTML and Vue files, labels in DocType, report, workspace, Web Form, onboarding JSON files, and navbar items in hooks.py. The mapping of file patterns to extractors is in babel_extractors.csv at the repository root. An app can add its own babel_extractors.csv next to its package. Its rules run before the Frappe rules. Folders that start with . or _, and files ignored by git, are skipped.

To keep strings that another app already has out of your POT file, set this hook:

# sample_app/hooks.py
ignore_translatable_strings_from = ["frappe"]

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Description bench generate-pot-file [--app APP] Extract strings into <app>/locale/main.pot. bench create-po-file LOCALE [--app APP] Create <app>/locale/<locale>.po. bench update-po-files [--app APP] [--locale LOCALE] Sync PO files with the POT file. bench compile-po-to-mo [--app APP] [--locale LOCALE] [--force] Compile PO files to MO files. bench migrate-csv-to-po [--app APP] [--locale LOCALE] Move CSV translations into PO files. bench update-csv-from-po APP [--locale LOCALE] Add translations from PO files that the CSV file does not have. bench --site SITE get-untranslated LANG FILE [--app APP] [--all] Write untranslated strings (CSV workflow). bench --site SITE update-translations LANG UNTRANSLATED TRANSLATED [--app APP] Merge a translated file (CSV workflow). bench --site SITE import-translations LANG PATH Import a CSV file of translations. bench --site SITE migrate-translations SOURCE_APP TARGET_APP Move app-specific translations between apps. bench --site SITE build-message-files Rebuild the translation message files. bench --site SITE new-language LANG_CODE APP Create a CSV file for a language.

Without --app, the gettext commands work on all apps and need a site (bench --site <site> ...).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Translate the template, then format: _("{0} saved").format(name), not _(f"{name} saved").
  • Do not join translated pieces into a sentence. Word order changes between languages. Translate the full sentence with placeholders.
  • _() at module level runs before a request sets the language. Use _lt() there.
  • After you change translations, clear the cache. Translations are cached per language.
