docs.title: Desk Pages
docs.text: A desk page is a custom screen in the desk that is not a form, list or report. Examples in Frappe are backups (Download Backups), leaderboard and user-profile. Use a page for a dashboard, a tool or a board that needs its own layout. A page is a record of the Page DocType plus files in your app.

docs.title: Page files
docs.text:
A standard page lives in the page folder of a module:

sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/
├── __init__.py
├── order_board.json     # the Page record
├── order_board.js       # page script
├── order_board.css      # optional styles
├── order_board.html     # optional templates
└── order_board.py       # optional whitelisted methods

The folder and file names are the scrubbed page name (order-board becomes order_board). bench migrate imports the JSON into the Page table.

docs.title: Create a page
docs.text:
1. Turn on developer mode for the site. A new Page needs it.
  2. Log in as Administrator. Only Administrator can create or edit a Page.
  3. Go to /app/page/new.
  4. Set Page Name, Title and Module. Keep Standard = Yes.
  5. Add the roles that can open the page in Roles. With no roles, all desk users can open it.
  6. Save.

On save, Frappe writes <page_name>.json and a starter <page_name>.js into the module folder. The record name comes from Page Name: lowercase, spaces become hyphens, and it is cut to 20 characters. The page opens at /app/<name>. If another name already has that prefix, Frappe adds -1, -2 and so on.

docs.title: The page script
docs.text:
The starter script runs when the page loads for the first time:

// sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/order_board.js
frappe.pages["order-board"].on_page_load = function (wrapper) {
    const page = frappe.ui.make_app_page({
        parent: wrapper,
        title: __("Order Board"),
        single_column: true,
    });

    page.set_primary_action(__("New Order"), () => frappe.new_doc("Sample Order"), "add");
    page.add_inner_button(__("Refresh"), () => load_orders(page));

    page.status_field = page.add_field({
        label: __("Status"),
        fieldname: "status",
        fieldtype: "Select",
        options: ["", "Draft", "Open", "Completed"],
        change: () => load_orders(page),
    });

    $(page.body).html(`<div class="order-board"></div>`);
    load_orders(page);
};

frappe.pages["order-board"].on_page_show = function (wrapper) {
    load_orders(wrapper.page);
};

function load_orders(page) {
    frappe
        .xcall("sample_app.sample_module.page.order_board.order_board.get_orders", {
            status: page.status_field.get_value(),
        })
        .then((orders) => {
            $(page.body).find(".order-board").html(
                frappe.render_template("order_board", { orders })
            );
        });
}

frappe.pages[name] is the page wrapper element. The desk calls these functions on it:

Function When it runs on_page_load(wrapper) Once, after the page script is loaded. on_page_show(wrapper) Each time the page is shown, also the first time. refresh(wrapper) Each time the page is shown, after on_page_show.

frappe.ui.make_app_page(opts) makes a frappe.ui.Page and stores it as wrapper.page. Options: parent (required), title, single_column. A frappe.ui.Page has these parts and methods:

Member Description page.body, page.main The main content area (a jQuery object). page.sidebar The side section, used when single_column is not set. set_title(title), set_indicator(label, color), clear_indicator() Title and status indicator. set_primary_action(label, fn, icon), set_secondary_action(label, fn, icon) The main buttons. add_inner_button(label, fn, group) A toolbar button, or a dropdown item if group is set. add_menu_item(label, fn) An item in the "..." menu. add_action_item(label, fn) An item in the Actions menu. add_field(df) A filter control in the page form bar. Returns the control. page.fields_dict holds them. clear_primary_action(), clear_inner_toolbar(), clear_menu() Remove buttons.

docs.title: Server methods
docs.text:
Put whitelisted functions in <page_name>.py and call them by dotted path:

# sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/order_board.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_orders(status: str | None = None):
    filters = {"status": status} if status else {}
    return frappe.get_list("Sample Order", filters=filters, fields=["name", "customer_name", "status"])

The Page Roles control only who can open the page. They do not protect these methods. Use frappe.get_list or an explicit permission check in each method. See Whitelisted Methods.

docs.title: CSS and HTML templates
docs.text:
• <page_name>.css is loaded with the page.
  • Each .html file in the folder becomes frappe.templates["<file name>"]. Render it with frappe.render_template("<file name>", data). The syntax is the desk micro-template: {{ value }}, {% if %}, {% for item in list %} and {% endfor %}, or plain JavaScript inside {% %}.
  • If an .html file contains <!-- jinja -->, the server renders it with Jinja first. The context comes from get_context(context) in <page_name>.py. Such a page is not cached in the browser.
<!-- sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/order_board.html -->
{% for order in orders %}
    <div class="order-row">{{ order.customer_name }}: {{ order.status }}</div>
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Add code to another app's page
docs.text:
The page_js hook adds a script to a page that another app owns. The script runs after the page script.

# sample_app/hooks.py
page_js = {"backups": "public/js/backups_extra.js"}

docs.title: Page fields
docs.text: Field Type Description page_name Data Name used for the record name and route. title Data Title in the breadcrumb and browser tab. icon Data Icon name. module Link Module that holds the page folder. restrict_to_domain Link (Domain) Show the page only when this domain is active. standard Select Yes for a page shipped in an app, No otherwise. roles Table (Has Role) Roles that can open the page. Empty means all desk users. Role Permission for Page and Report can add custom roles. system_page Check Stored on the record. The v15 desk does not read it.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Outside developer mode, the browser caches the page script in localStorage. Reload after a change. Run bench --site <site> clear-cache if it does not update.
  • Deleting a Page record does not delete its folder in the app.
  • The frappe.pages[...] key is the record name with hyphens, not the scrubbed folder name.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Client API
  • Workspaces
  • Whitelisted Methods
  • Apps

docs.title: Form Scripts
docs.text: A form script is JavaScript that runs in the desk form of a DocType. Use it to react to form events, change field properties, add buttons, filter Link fields and call the server. Keep business rules and validation on the server, in the controller. A form script only improves the user interface. A user can skip it with a direct API call.

docs.title: Where form scripts come from
docs.text:
When the desk loads a DocType, frappe/desk/form/meta.py collects all form code into the __js and __custom_js keys of the DocType meta. The browser runs them in this order:

  1. <doctype>.js in the DocType folder of the app that owns the DocType, for example sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.js.
  2. regional/<country>.js in the same folder, if System Settings has a country and the file exists.
  3. The files that other apps add with the doctype_js hook, in app order.
  4. The client script of the active DocType Layout, if the form opens with one.
  5. All enabled Client Script records with view = Form for the DocType, oldest first. These do not run when a DocType Layout is active.

Steps 1 to 3 apply only to standard DocTypes. A DocType with custom = 1 gets no file-based code, so use a Client Script record for it. Client Script records are described in Server and Client Scripts.

To add code to a DocType that another app owns, use the doctype_js hook. The path is relative to the app package.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doctype_js = {
    "ToDo": "public/js/todo.js",
    "User": ["public/js/user.js", "public/js/user_extra.js"],
}

The value can be a string or a list of strings. See Extending Apps for the other extension hooks.

docs.title: Register event handlers
docs.text:
Use frappe.ui.form.on(doctype, handlers). Each key is a form event or a fieldname. Each handler gets frm, and for child rows also cdt (child DocType) and cdn (child row name).

// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    setup(frm) {
        frm.set_query("item", "items", () => ({ filters: { disabled: 0 } }));
    },
    refresh(frm) {
        if (!frm.is_new()) {
            frm.add_custom_button(__("Mark as Completed"), () => {
                frm.set_value("status", "Completed").then(() => frm.save());
            }, __("Actions"));
            frm.add_custom_button(__("Open Customer Orders"), () => {
                frappe.set_route("List", "Sample Order", { customer_name: frm.doc.customer_name });
            });
        }
    },
    customer_name(frm) {
        frm.set_intro(__("Customer changed. Check the items."), "orange");
    },
});

You can call frappe.ui.form.on many times for the same DocType. All handlers for an event run, one after the other, in the order they were registered. If a handler returns a promise, the next handler waits for it. frappe.ui.form.off(doctype, event) removes all handlers for that event.

To run another handler from your code, use frm.trigger("event_name"). It returns a promise.

docs.title: Form events
docs.text:
The event order below was checked in the v15 desk (/app) on a Sample Order form. v15 has no after_delete, before_discard or after_discard form event.

Action Events, in order Open a form for the first time (new or existing document) setup, before_load, onload, refresh, onload_post_render Open a document that is already loaded in this session refresh Change a field value <fieldname> Save validate, before_save, (server save), after_save, refresh Submit before_submit, validate, before_save, (server submit), after_save, on_submit, refresh Cancel before_cancel, (server cancel), after_cancel, refresh

setup runs once for each form instance, that is once for each DocType in a browser session. Put set_query and other one-time setup there. Put buttons and anything that depends on the document in refresh.

All form events:

Event When it runs setup Once, when the form object for the DocType is made. before_load Before onload, the first time a document opens. onload The first time a document opens in this session. refresh Every time the form renders: after load, after save, submit or cancel, and when you go back to the form. onload_post_render After the first refresh of a document. <fieldname> After the value of that field changes. validate Before save. Stop the save with frappe.throw() or frappe.validated = false. before_save After validate, before the request to the server. after_save After the server saved the document. before_submit Before submit. Stop it with frappe.validated = false. on_submit After the server submitted the document. before_cancel Before cancel. Stop it with frappe.validated = false. after_cancel After the server cancelled the document. before_workflow_action, after_workflow_action Before and after a workflow action. frm.selected_workflow_action holds the action name. timeline_refresh After the timeline renders. dashboard_update After the connections dashboard loads its counts. on_tab_change After the user changes the form tab. on_hide When the user leaves the form page. <button fieldname> When the user clicks a Button field.

docs.title: Child table events
docs.text:
Register child table events on the child DocType, not on the parent. The handler gets (frm, cdt, cdn). Use locals[cdt][cdn] or frappe.get_doc(cdt, cdn) to read the row.

// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order Item", {
    qty(frm, cdt, cdn) {
        const row = locals[cdt][cdn];
        frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, "amount", flt(row.qty) * flt(row.rate));
    },
    items_add(frm, cdt, cdn) {
        frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, "qty", 1);
    },
    items_remove(frm) {
        frm.set_value("total", frm.get_sum("items", "amount"));
    },
});
Event When it runs <child fieldname> After a field in a row changes. <table fieldname>_add After the user adds a row in the grid. frm.add_child() does not trigger it. before_<table fieldname>_remove Before a row is removed. <table fieldname>_remove After a row is removed. <table fieldname>_move After the user drags a row to a new position. <table fieldname>_delete After the user deletes selected rows or all rows. form_render When the row editor of a row opens.

docs.title: The frm object
docs.text:
frm is the frappe.ui.form.Form instance (frappe/public/js/frappe/form/form.js). The global cur_frm points to the form on screen, but use the frm argument in handlers.

Common properties:

Property Description frm.doc The document as a plain object. Child tables are arrays of row objects. frm.doctype, frm.docname The DocType and the document name. frm.meta The DocType meta. frm.fields_dict Field controls by fieldname. frm.fields_dict.items.grid is the grid of a table field. frm.page The frappe.ui.Page of the form. frm.custom_buttons Buttons added with add_custom_button, by label.

Methods:

Method Description set_value(fieldname, value) or set_value({field: value, ...}) Set values and run the change events. Returns a promise. Pass an array to replace a child table. refresh_field(fieldname) Render one field again after you change frm.doc directly. refresh_fields() / refresh() Render all fields again / render the whole form again. set_df_property(fieldname, property, value) Change a field property, for example read_only, hidden, reqd, options, label, description. set_df_property(table, property, value, docname, child_field, row_name) Change a property of a child field for one row. toggle_display(fieldnames, show) Show or hide one field or a list of fields. toggle_reqd(fieldnames, mandatory) Make fields mandatory or not. toggle_enable(fieldnames, enable) Make fields editable or read-only. set_query(fieldname, fn) / set_query(child_field, table, fn) Set the filters of a Link field. fn returns { filters } or { query, filters }. add_custom_button(label, fn, group) Add a toolbar button. A group puts it in a dropdown. Returns the button. remove_custom_button(label, group), clear_custom_buttons() Remove one button or all custom buttons. change_custom_button_type(label, group, type) Change the button style, for example "primary". add_child(table_fieldname, values) Add a row to a child table. Call refresh_field(table) after it. Returns the row. clear_table(table_fieldname) Remove all rows of a child table. get_sum(table_fieldname, fieldname) Sum a column of a child table. update_in_all_rows(table_fieldname, fieldname, value) Set a value in all rows. get_selected() Selected rows of each grid, as {table_fieldname: [row names]}. call(method, args) Call a whitelisted method of the document controller. See below. save(action), savesubmit(), savecancel(), savetrash() Save, submit, cancel or delete with the standard confirm dialogs. save() returns a promise. reload_doc() Load the document again from the server. is_new(), is_dirty(), dirty() Check if the document is unsaved or changed, or mark it as changed. has_perm(ptype) Check a permission on the document, for example "write". set_intro(text, color) Show a message at the top of the form. Call with no text to clear it. set_indicator_formatter(fieldname, get_color, get_text) Show a colored indicator in a Link column of a grid. disable_save(), enable_save(), disable_form() Hide the save button, show it again, or make the whole form read-only. scroll_to_field(fieldname) Scroll to a field and focus it. set_active_tab(tab_fieldname) Open a form tab. add_fetch(link_field, source_field, target_field) Copy a field of the linked document into the form when the link changes. Prefer fetch_from in the DocType. trigger(event) Run the handlers of an event. copy_doc(), amend_doc(), print_doc(), email_doc(), rename_doc() Open the standard actions.

The helpers in frappe/public/js/frappe/form/script_helpers.js (refresh_field, hide_field, unhide_field, set_field_options) are older globals that act on cur_frm. Use the frm methods in new code.

docs.title: Call the server
docs.text:
frm.call(method, args) runs a whitelisted method of the controller class of the document. The current document is sent with the request. If the method changes the document, the form updates its fields.

# sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
class SampleOrder(Document):
    @frappe.whitelist()
    def get_open_count(self):
        return frappe.db.count("Sample Order", {"customer_name": self.customer_name, "docstatus": 0})

// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    refresh(frm) {
        frm.call("get_open_count").then((r) => {
            frm.set_intro(__("{0} draft orders for this customer", [r.message]));
        });
    },
});

If you pass an object with method and no doc, and the method has no dot, frm.call prefixes it with the Python module of the DocType. For other server calls, use frappe.call or frappe.xcall. See Client API.

docs.title: Class-based controllers
docs.text: Older code puts methods on frm.cscript, the form controller object. A method named after an event, or custom_<event>, runs for that event. These methods get (doc, cdt, cdn), not frm. They run after the frappe.ui.form.on handlers for the same event. To bind a class, older code calls frm.script_manager.make(MyController) or extend_cscript(frm.cscript, new MyController({ frm })). Use frappe.ui.form.on in new code.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not trust form scripts for validation. Repeat each rule in the controller validate.
  • Add buttons in refresh, not in onload. The toolbar is rebuilt on every refresh.
  • frm.add_child() and direct changes to frm.doc do not render. Call frm.refresh_field() after them.
  • frm.set_value() is asynchronous. Use await or .then() before you read dependent values or save.
  • A handler that returns a promise delays the next handler and the save. A promise that never settles blocks the form.
  • frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, ...) sets a child row value. frm.set_value sets parent fields only.
  • If a form uses a DocType Layout, Client Script records with view = Form do not run. Put the code in the client script of the layout.

docs.title: List View Settings
docs.text: Each desk view of a DocType reads a settings object from a global registry. An app fills the registry in a JavaScript file next to the DocType, for example sample_order_list.js for the list view. Use these files to add indicators, row buttons, column formatters, default filters and view-specific options. To change columns or the page size without code, users have List Settings in the desk. See List View.

docs.title: Files and registries
docs.text:
frappe/desk/form/meta.py reads these files from the DocType folder and from hooks. The browser runs them when it loads the DocType meta, in this order: list, calendar, tree, then Client Script records with view = List. A Client Script can therefore override the file-based settings.

File in the DocType folder Hook for other apps Registry it fills <doctype>_list.js doctype_list_js frappe.listview_settings["<DocType>"] (list, report, kanban and image views) <doctype>_calendar.js doctype_calendar_js frappe.views.calendar["<DocType>"] (calendar and gantt views) <doctype>_tree.js doctype_tree_js frappe.treeview_settings["<DocType>"] (tree view)

The <doctype> part is the scrubbed DocType name, for example sample_order. A file <doctype>_list.html in the DocType folder is loaded as the list view template (__listview_template). A file regional/<country>_list.js is also added to the list code when System Settings has that country. A custom DocType (custom = 1) loads no files. Use a Client Script with view = List for it.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doctype_list_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo_list.js"}
doctype_calendar_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo_calendar.js"}

A hook file runs after the file of the owning app. Assigning a new object replaces the settings of the owning app. Change single keys instead:

// sample_app/public/js/todo_list.js
frappe.listview_settings["ToDo"] = frappe.listview_settings["ToDo"] || {};
frappe.listview_settings["ToDo"].add_fields = ["priority"];

docs.title: List view settings
docs.text:
// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order_list.js
frappe.listview_settings["Sample Order"] = {
    add_fields: ["status", "total"],
    has_indicator_for_draft: 1,
    get_indicator(doc) {
        const colors = { Draft: "gray", Open: "orange", Completed: "green", Cancelled: "red" };
        return [__(doc.status), colors[doc.status] || "gray", "status,=," + doc.status];
    },
    button: {
        show: (doc) => doc.status === "Open",
        get_label: () => __("Complete"),
        get_description: (doc) => __("Mark {0} as Completed", [doc.name]),
        action: (doc) =>
            frappe.db.set_value("Sample Order", doc.name, "status", "Completed")
                .then(() => cur_list.refresh()),
    },
    formatters: {
        order_date: (value) => `<span class="text-muted">${frappe.datetime.prettyDate(value)}</span>`,
    },
    onload(listview) {
        listview.page.add_inner_button(__("Open Orders"), () =>
            listview.filter_area.add([["Sample Order", "status", "=", "Open"]])
        );
    },
};

If the DocType has an active Workflow, the workflow state takes priority over get_indicator.

Key Type Description add_fields list Extra fields to fetch for each row. Add every field that get_indicator, button or formatters reads. filters list Default filters, as [fieldname, operator, value]. Used only when the user has no saved filters. hide_name_column bool Hide the name (ID) column. hide_name_filter bool Hide the ID filter in the standard filter bar. get_indicator(doc) function Return [label, color, filter] for the status indicator. filter is "field,operator,value" and is applied when the user clicks the indicator. has_indicator_for_draft bool For a submittable DocType, use get_indicator for drafts instead of the "Draft" indicator. has_indicator_for_cancelled bool The same for cancelled documents. formatters object {fieldname: (value, df, doc) => html}. Formats a column. button object One button per row: show(doc), get_label(doc), get_description(doc), action(doc). onload(listview) function Runs once after the view is set up. Add page buttons and menu items here. before_render() function Runs before each render of the rows. refresh(listview) function Runs after each data refresh. primary_action() function Replaces the action of the "Add" button. get_form_link(doc) function Return the URL a row opens.

listview is the frappe.views.ListView instance. Useful members: listview.page (a frappe.ui.Page), listview.filter_area, listview.data, listview.get_checked_items(), listview.refresh(). To add an item to the Actions menu of selected rows, call listview.page.add_actions_menu_item(label, fn).

The indicator rules in frappe/public/js/frappe/model/indicator.js run in this order: unsaved, workflow state, draft and cancelled (for submittable DocTypes), DocType states that match doc.status, get_indicator, submitted, status, enabled, disabled.

docs.title: Calendar and gantt settings
docs.text:
// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_event/sample_event_calendar.js
frappe.views.calendar["Sample Event"] = {
    field_map: {
        start: "starts_on",
        end: "ends_on",
        id: "name",
        title: "subject",
        allDay: "all_day",
    },
    gantt: true,
    get_events_method: "frappe.desk.calendar.get_events",
};
Key Description field_map Maps start, end, id, title, allDay and convertToUserTz to fieldnames. The gantt view also reads field_map.progress (a fieldname or a function). It reads color, is_milestone and depends_on_tasks from the row. get_events_method Dotted path of a whitelisted method. Default frappe.desk.calendar.get_events, which takes doctype, start, end, field_map, filters and fields. get_css_class(event) Return danger, success, warning or default to color an event. fields Extra fields to fetch for each event. The calendar sends the current list filters with the request. options Extra FullCalendar options. gantt true, or an object of keys that override this object in the gantt view. order_by Sort order of the gantt view.

docs.title: Tree view settings
docs.text:
A tree view needs a DocType with is_tree = 1. See DocTypes. Common keys of frappe.treeview_settings["<DocType>"]:

Key Description get_tree_nodes Method that returns child nodes. Default frappe.desk.treeview.get_children. add_tree_node Method that adds a node. Default frappe.desk.treeview.add_node. root_label Label of the root node. get_tree_root Set false to skip the root node lookup. title Page title. filters Filter fields shown above the tree. fields, ignore_fields Fields of the "Add Child" dialog. onload(treeview), post_render(treeview) Run after load and after render. onrender(node), on_get_node(nodes, deep), click(node) Node hooks. get_label(node) Return the label of a node. toolbar, extend_toolbar Node buttons. With extend_toolbar: true your buttons are added to the standard ones. menu_items Extra page menu items. disable_add_node Hide "Add Child".

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A field that get_indicator or button.show reads is undefined unless it is a list column or in add_fields.
  • For submittable DocTypes, get_indicator is ignored for drafts and cancelled documents unless you set has_indicator_for_draft or has_indicator_for_cancelled.
  • A Calendar View record uses only its own field map. It does not read frappe.views.calendar settings.
  • The settings code comes with the DocType meta, which the browser caches. After you change a settings file, reload the page. Outside developer mode, also run bench --site <site> clear-cache.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text:
In v15, desk navigation is made of workspaces. The left sidebar of the desk at /app lists the workspaces that the user can see. Each workspace is a page with shortcuts, cards of links, charts, number cards and quick lists. An app ships its workspaces as JSON files, and bench migrate imports them. The apps screen at /apps lists installed apps, and an app joins it with the add_to_apps_screen hook. For the user view, see Desk.

Version

v15 has no Sidebar or Dock DocTypes. They were added in later versions.

docs.title: Workspace files
docs.text:
A standard workspace lives in the workspace folder of a module:

sample_app/sample_module/workspace/sample_orders/sample_orders.json

The folder and file names are the scrubbed workspace title. bench migrate imports the JSON into the Workspace table. On import, Frappe keeps the site value of is_hidden. Migrate does not delete a workspace whose file is gone from the app.

docs.title: Workspace fields
Make or change a standard workspace
docs.text:
1. Turn on developer mode for the site.
  2. Log in as a user with the Workspace Manager role.
  3. Open the workspace at /app/<workspace> and select Edit.
  4. Make sure the workspace is public and has a module of your app.
  5. Save. Frappe writes the JSON file into the module folder.
  6. Commit the file in your app.

Only a Workspace Manager can save, rename or delete a public workspace. If you change the title or module in developer mode, Frappe deletes the old folder. Deleting a public workspace in developer mode deletes its folder.

During install, uninstall, migrate, patches, tests and fixture import, a workspace save does not export files and skips the Workspace Manager check.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
The desk builds a map of workspaces at boot. The route of a public workspace is /app/<slug of the name>, for example /app/tools. A private workspace is at /app/private/<slug of the title>. A route that matches no workspace falls through to a DocType or Page route.

The sidebar data comes from frappe.desk.desktop.get_workspace_sidebar_items. It returns the public workspaces that the user may see and the user's own private workspaces. Boot sends them as frappe.boot.allowed_workspaces.

docs.title: Apps screen: add_to_apps_screen
docs.text:
The add_to_apps_screen hook puts an app on the apps screen at /apps. It is a list with one dict per entry.

# sample_app/hooks.py
add_to_apps_screen = [
    {
        "name": "sample_app",
        "logo": "/assets/sample_app/images/logo.svg",
        "title": "Sample App",
        "route": "/app/sample-orders",
        "has_permission": "sample_app.api.has_app_permission",
    }
]
Key Description name App name. Frappe uses it only to find a workspace of the app's modules when the user cannot open route. The tile always shows the app that sets the hook. title Label on the apps screen. It is translated. logo Logo URL. route Where the icon goes. Default /apps. has_permission Dotted path of a function with no arguments. Return True if the session user may see the app.

frappe.apps.get_apps builds the list. It skips frappe itself. It also skips apps whose setup wizard is not complete, unless the user is a System Manager. If the route starts with /app/ and the user cannot open that workspace, Frappe uses the first allowed workspace of the app's modules, or else the first allowed workspace.

If no app is on the list, /apps redirects to /app. With only frappe installed, this is always the case.

docs.title: Default app
docs.text:
System Settings > Default App and User > Default App pick the app to open after login. The user value wins. Without a default:

  • With one app on the apps screen, login opens its route.
  • With more apps whose routes are all under /app, login opens /app.
  • Otherwise login opens /apps.

The whitelisted method frappe.apps.set_app_as_default(app_name) toggles the user's default app.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Export works only in developer mode and only for public workspaces. On other sites, desk changes stay in the database and are lost when a migrate imports the file again.
  • A workspace file that you delete from the app stays on sites as a record. Delete the record too, or ship a patch.
  • has_permission errors are logged to Error Log and the app is left out of the list.

docs.title: Server and Client Scripts
docs.text:
Use server scripts and client scripts, and decide when to write app code instead.

Page What it covers Server Scripts and Client Scripts Write Python Server Scripts and JavaScript Client Scripts in the desk, enable server scripts, and know the restricted API that safe_exec allows.

docs.title: Server Scripts and Client Scripts
docs.text:
Server Script and Client Script are DocTypes that store code in the database. You write them in the desk, without an app. Use them for small, site-specific changes. Use app code (controllers, hooks, form scripts) for logic that must be versioned, reviewed, tested, or shipped to more than one site.

Server Script Client Script Language Restricted Python (RestrictedPython) JavaScript Runs On the server In the browser of the user Role to create Script Manager System Manager Must be enabled Yes, server_script_enabled in common_site_config.json No, but each script has enabled (default off) Turn one script off Set disabled Clear enabled

docs.title: Enable server scripts
docs.text:
Server scripts are off by default. Frappe reads the key only from sites/common_site_config.json, not from site_config.json (is_safe_exec_enabled in frappe/utils/safe_exec.py). The setting applies to all sites of the bench.

bench set-config -g server_script_enabled 1

When the key is off, every Server Script raises ServerScriptNotEnabled with the message "Server Scripts are disabled. Please enable server scripts from bench configuration." This also applies to other features that use safe_exec, such as Script Reports written in the desk. You can still save a Server Script while the key is off.

docs.title: Server Script types
docs.text:
Set Script Type (script_type):

Type Extra fields Runs when Variables in scope DocType Event reference_doctype, doctype_event The document event fires doc API api_method, allow_guest, rate limit fields A request to /api/method/<api_method> frappe.form_dict Scheduler Event event_frequency, cron_format The scheduler runs the job none Permission Query reference_doctype frappe.get_list builds the query user, set conditions

docs.title: DocType Event
docs.text:
doctype_event maps to controller events (EVENT_MAP in frappe/core/doctype/server_script/server_script_utils.py):

doctype_event Controller event Before Insert before_insert Before Validate before_validate Before Save validate After Insert after_insert After Save on_update Before Rename / After Rename before_rename / after_rename Before Submit / After Submit before_submit / on_submit Before Cancel / After Cancel before_cancel / on_cancel Before Delete / After Delete on_trash / after_delete Before Save (Submitted Document) / After Save (Submitted Document) before_update_after_submit / on_update_after_submit Before Print before_print On Payment Authorization on_payment_authorized

Scripts run after the controller and doc_events handlers for the same event. They do not run during bench install-app or bench migrate.

# Server Script: DocType Event, Sample Order, Before Save
total = 0
for row in doc.items:
    row.amount = frappe.utils.flt(row.qty) * frappe.utils.flt(row.rate)
    total += row.amount
doc.total = total

if doc.total <= 0:
    frappe.throw(_("Total must be more than zero"))

frappe.db.commit, frappe.db.rollback and frappe.db.add_index are removed in DocType Event scripts.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
The script runs at /api/method/<api_method> and /api/v2/method/<api_method>. Set the response in frappe.response["message"]. If you set values on frappe.flags, Frappe returns the flags as the message instead.

# Server Script: API, api_method = sample_item_count
category = frappe.form_dict.get("category")
frappe.response["message"] = frappe.db.count("Sample Item", {"category": category})

curl -b jar "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/sample_item_count?category=Hardware"

{"message": 3}
  • With allow_guest off, a Guest gets PermissionError.
  • With enable_rate_limit on, rate_limit_count defaults to 5 and rate_limit_seconds to 86400 when they are empty.
  • An API script with allow_guest on and no rate limit can be called without limit by anyone. Turn on enable_rate_limit for guest scripts.
  • The script has priority: an API script with the same path as a Python method replaces it.

docs.title: Scheduler Event
docs.text: Saving the script creates or updates a Scheduled Job Type that points to it. event_frequency takes All, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly, the Long variants, or Cron with cron_format. Setting disabled stops the job.

docs.title: Permission Query
docs.text:
Set conditions to a SQL condition string. Frappe adds it to the WHERE clause of frappe.get_list for reference_doctype.

# Server Script: Permission Query, Sample Order
conditions = f"`tabSample Order`.owner_user = {frappe.db.escape(user)}"

docs.title: The restricted environment
docs.text:
safe_exec compiles the script with RestrictedPython and runs it with the globals from get_safe_globals().

  • import is not allowed. Use the names below.
  • Attributes and keys that start with _ are not allowed.
  • print() writes to frappe.log, not to the console.
  • frappe.db.sql allows only queries that start with SELECT or EXPLAIN, and WITH on MariaDB. It rejects INTO OUTFILE, DUMPFILE and queries on __Auth.

docs.title: Allowed API
docs.text:
Top-level names:

frappe, json (loads, dumps), as_json, _, _dict, dict, log, args (the form dict), scrub, guess_mimetype, html2text, get_toc, get_next_link, get_visible_columns, run_script, FrappeClient, style, dev_server, and the builtins abs, all, any, bool, dict, enumerate, isinstance, issubclass, list, max, min, range, set, sorted, sum, tuple.

frappe.*:

Group Names Documents get_doc, new_doc, copy_doc, get_cached_doc, get_last_doc, get_mapped_doc, rename_doc, delete_doc, get_meta Lists get_list, get_all, qb Database (frappe.db.*) get_list, get_all, get_value, get_single_value, set_value, exists, count, escape, get_default, sql (read-only), commit, rollback, add_index, after_commit, before_commit, after_rollback, before_rollback Messages and errors msgprint, throw, log_error, errprint, log, and all exception classes of frappe.exceptions (for example frappe.ValidationError) Calls and jobs call (calls a whitelisted method or API script), enqueue (enqueues a whitelisted method or API script), is_job_queued HTTP make_get_request, make_post_request, make_put_request, make_patch_request, make_delete_request Email and print sendmail, get_print, attach_print, render_template Formatting format, format_value, format_date, bold, date_format, time_format, sanitize_html Session and request session (user, csrf_token), user, full_name, form_dict, request (path), response, flags, lang Users get_fullname, get_gravatar, get_identicon Other get_hooks, get_system_settings, get_url, website (abs_url, extract_title, get_boot_data, get_home_page, get_html_content_based_on_type), socketio_port, json_handler

frappe.utils contains a fixed list of helpers from frappe/utils/data.py (VALID_UTILS in frappe/utils/safe_exec.py). Examples: flt, cint, cstr, getdate, get_datetime, nowdate, now, today, add_days, add_months, date_diff, fmt_money, money_in_words, strip_html, escape_html, get_url_to_form, generate_hash. Other functions of frappe.utils are not available.

In Server Scripts, frappe.get_doc, frappe.get_list, frappe.get_all and the other document functions are the normal functions. They behave as in app code: get_list checks permissions of the session user, get_all does not, and doc.save() checks write permission.

Version

In v15 Server Scripts, the HTTP helpers are the normal functions of frappe.integrations.utils. They do not block requests to private or local addresses. Give the Script Manager role only to trusted users.

docs.title: Client Script
docs.text:
A Client Script adds JavaScript to the form or list of a DocType. Set:

Field Description dt The DocType. view Form (default) or List. enabled Default off. Turn it on, or the script does not load. module Optional. Use it to filter the script in a fixture. Frappe does not check it when it loads scripts. script The code. 
// Client Script: Sample Order, Form
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    refresh(frm) {
        if (frm.doc.docstatus === 0) {
            frm.add_custom_button(__("Recalculate"), () => frm.trigger("recalculate"));
        }
    },
});

Frappe appends all enabled scripts of the DocType, ordered by creation, to the form script or the list script (add_custom_script in frappe/desk/form/meta.py). For a List script, set frappe.listview_settings["<DocType>"]. See Form Scripts and List View Settings for the API.

A Client Script runs only in the desk. Validation in a Client Script does not protect the data. The REST API, Data Import and server code skip it. Put rules that must hold on the server.

docs.title: Ship scripts with an app
docs.text:
Server Scripts and Client Scripts can be fixtures:

# sample_app/hooks.py
fixtures = [
    {"dt": "Server Script", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]},
    {"dt": "Client Script", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]},
]

For code that you own, prefer controllers, doc_events and doctype_js in the app. They do not need server_script_enabled, and they run under your tests.

docs.title: Test with server scripts
docs.text:
Call the enable_safe_exec class method of FrappeTestCase in setUpClass. It sets server_script_enabled to 1 in common_site_config.json. A class cleanup sets it to 0 after the tests of the class, even if it was 1 before.

# sample_app/sample_app/tests/test_sample_script.py
from frappe.tests.utils import FrappeTestCase


class TestSampleScript(FrappeTestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        super().setUpClass()
        cls.enable_safe_exec()

    def test_api_script(self):
        ...

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• server_script_enabled in site_config.json has no effect. Use bench set-config -g.
  • Only one Permission Query script per DocType is used.
  • A Server Script with an error in a Before Save event blocks all saves of the DocType. Test on a copy of the site first.
  • Server Scripts are cached in server_script_map. Saving or deleting a script clears the cache.
  • Do not build SQL from user input. Use frappe.db.escape or frappe.qb.

docs.title: Configuration and Operations
docs.text:
Configure sites, deploy to production and upgrade between versions.

Page What it covers Configuration Configure a site with site_config.json and common_site_config.json, read values with frappe.conf, change them with bench set-config, and override them with environment variables. Deployment Run Frappe in production with the bench CLI - processes, Procfile, supervisor or systemd, nginx, workers and queues, socketio, maintenance mode and DNS multitenancy. Upgrading Upgrade a bench to Frappe v15 from v14, what the v15 patches change on a site, deprecation warnings in v15, and what to prepare for v16.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Frappe reads its configuration from two JSON files in the sites folder. sites/common_site_config.json holds values for every site on the bench. sites/<site>/site_config.json holds values for one site and overrides the common file. Use configuration for things that differ per server or site: credentials, Redis URLs, ports, feature flags. Use a Single DocType such as System Settings for things that a user changes in the desk.

docs.title: How the values merge
docs.text:
frappe.get_site_config() builds the configuration in this order. A later step wins.

  1. common_site_config.json.
  2. site_config.json of the site.
  3. Environment variables and defaults for a few keys: redis_queue (default redis://127.0.0.1:11311), redis_cache (default redis://127.0.0.1:13311), db_type (default mariadb), db_socket, db_host (default 127.0.0.1) and db_port (default 3306 for MariaDB, 5432 for Postgres). See Environment variables.
  4. extra_config hooks: if the config has extra_config (a dotted path or a list of paths), Frappe calls each function and merges the dict it returns.

docs.title: Read configuration in code
docs.text:
import frappe

frappe.conf.developer_mode           # current site, merged config. A missing key returns None.
frappe.conf.get("max_file_size", 0)  # with a default

frappe.get_site_config()             # merged config of the current site, read from disk
frappe.get_common_site_config()      # common_site_config.json only
frappe.get_conf("frappe.localhost")  # config of another site
frappe.get_conf()                    # current site, or common config when no site is set

frappe.conf is frappe.local.conf. It is loaded once per request or job by frappe.init. The result is a frappe._dict, so attribute access returns None for a missing key.

Some keys are read with frappe.get_common_site_config() or before a site is set. These keys work only in common_site_config.json. They are marked common in the tables below.

Warning

Site config holds secrets: db_password, encryption_key, mail and Redis passwords. Never send frappe.conf to the browser. frappe.boot gets only developer_mode, socketio_port, file_watcher_port, disable_async and max_file_size from it.

docs.title: Change configuration
docs.text:
bench --site frappe.localhost set-config developer_mode 1
bench --site frappe.localhost set-config allow_cors '["https://app.example.com"]' --parse
bench set-config -g scheduler_tick_interval 60        # common_site_config.json
bench --site frappe.localhost set-config pause_scheduler None   # remove the key
bench --site frappe.localhost show-config                       # print the merged config
  • -g, --global: write to common_site_config.json.
  • -p, --parse: read the value as a Python literal (True, False, numbers, lists, dicts).
  • Without --parse, "0" and "1" are saved as integers, and "true" and "false" as booleans. The value None removes the key.

From code, use frappe.installer.update_site_config(key, value). It locks the file, writes it, and updates frappe.local.conf of the current process. Other processes read the new value on their next request. Restart workers and the Socket.IO server for keys they read at startup (workers, socketio_*, redis_*).

docs.title: Keys by purpose
docs.text: This is the list of keys that you are most likely to set. For every key read by the framework, see the site config reference.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Key Default Description db_type mariadb mariadb or postgres. db_name none Database name. Also the database user and the Redis key prefix of the site. db_password none Password of the database user. db_host, db_port, db_socket 127.0.0.1, default port, none Where the database server is. db_ssl_ca, db_ssl_cert, db_ssl_key, db_ssl_check_hostname none TLS for MariaDB. db_schema none Schema for Postgres. read_from_replica off Send read-only requests to a replica. Needs replica_host. replica_host, replica_db_port none Replica server. different_credentials_for_replica, replica_db_name, replica_db_password off Use other credentials for the replica. max_writes_per_transaction framework limit Raise the limit of writes in one transaction. enable_db_statement_timeout off Stop queries after 1.5 times the request timeout (http_timeout, default 300 s) or the job timeout. rds_db off Grant a reduced set of privileges when making the site database, for managed databases.

v15 has no db_user key. The database user is always db_name.

docs.title: Redis, queues and workers
docs.text:
Key Default Description redis_cache redis://127.0.0.1:13311 Redis for frappe.cache. redis_queue redis://127.0.0.1:11311 Redis for job queues and realtime events. common redis_cache_sentinel_enabled, redis_cache_sentinels, redis_cache_master_service, ... off Connect to the cache through Redis Sentinel. The same keys exist with the redis_queue_ prefix. workers none Extra queues: {"<queue>": {"timeout": <seconds>}}. common use_rq_auth, rq_username, rq_password off Redis ACL user for the queue. common max_queued_jobs unset (no limit) Queue size at which frappe.enqueue fails. rq_job_failure_ttl, rq_results_ttl, rq_failed_jobs_limit 7 days, 600 s, 1000 How long RQ keeps job data. background_process_niceness 10 CPU niceness increment for workers and the scheduler. common

See Background Jobs.

docs.title: Scheduler and maintenance
docs.text:
Key Default Description scheduler_tick_interval 60 Seconds between scheduler checks. common scheduler_interval 240 Interval of all scheduler events, in seconds. pause_scheduler off Pause scheduled jobs. disable_scheduler off Disable scheduled jobs. maintenance_mode off Block writes and stop the scheduler. allow_reads_during_maintenance off In maintenance mode, keep the site open for reads.

See Scheduler.

docs.title: Web server, URLs and realtime
docs.text:
Key Default Description webserver_port none Port of bench serve. Used in URLs when host_name is not set. common host_name (or hostname) none Full site URL, such as https://erp.example.com. Used by frappe.utils.get_url. http_port none Port added to URLs made from the request host. default_site none Site used when no --site is given. common socketio_port 9000 Port of the Node Socket.IO server. common socketio_uds none Unix socket for the Socket.IO server instead of the port. common live_reload, file_watcher_port off Development asset watcher. common restart_supervisor_on_update, restart_systemd_on_update off Restart services after bench update.

See Realtime and Deployment.

docs.title: Security and requests
docs.text:
Key Default Description encryption_key made at site creation Key for encrypted Password fields and backups. Keep a copy. Without it, encrypted data cannot be read. allow_cors none "*", one origin, or a list of origins allowed to call the API from a browser. ignore_csrf off Turn off the CSRF check. Only for development. deny_multiple_sessions off Log out other sessions of a user at login. Also in System Settings. rate_limit none {"limit": <seconds>, "window": <seconds>}. Total request time the site may use in each window. Over the limit, requests get HTTP 429. throttle_user_limit 60 Maximum users created in 60 seconds. server_script_enabled off Allow Server Scripts and safe exec. common notify_admin_access_to_system_manager off Email System Managers when Administrator logs in.

See Security.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Key Default Description max_file_size 25 MB Maximum upload size in bytes. System Settings max_file_size (in MB) wins when set. max_zip_extract_size, max_zip_extract_members 25 MB, 1000 Limits for unzipping a File. System Settings max_zip_extract_size (in MB) wins when set. private_path private Folder of private files, relative to the site folder.

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
These keys make a default outgoing account when mail_server is set and no Email Account exists for sending.

Key Description mail_server, mail_port SMTP server and port. mail_login, mail_password SMTP login. use_tls SMTP with STARTTLS. auto_email_id Sender address. Default: mail_login, else notifications@example.com. email_sender_name Sender name. Default Frappe. always_use_account_email_id_as_sender, always_use_account_name_as_sender_name Force the account sender. disable_mail_smtp_authentication Send without SMTP login. mute_emails Do not send emails. email_queue_batch_size Emails sent per queue flush. Default 500. pop_timeout, imap_timeout Timeouts for incoming mail.

docs.title: Development and logging
docs.text: Key Default Description developer_mode off Write DocType and other standard changes to app files. Turns off website cache. allow_tests off Allow bench run-tests on the site. Not needed when CI is set. logging 0 2 logs each SQL query. A true value also shows tracebacks on 404 responses. enable_frappe_logger off Write request logs with frappe.logger. monitor off Record request and job metrics (frappe.monitor). disable_async off The desk does not connect to the Socket.IO server. disable_website_cache off Do not cache rendered website pages. disable_global_search off Do not update the global search index. error_report_email none Recipient of error reports that users send from the desk.

docs.title: Install and backups
docs.text:
Key Default Description admin_password none Administrator password used by bench new-site and tests. install_apps none Apps to install with every new site (after frappe). skip_setup_wizard off Do not open the setup wizard after install. backup none {"includes": [...], "excludes": [...]}: tables for a partial backup. keep_backups_for_hours 23 Hours before temporary backup files in the backup folder are deleted. lang en Language used before a user is known.

Other groups: pulse_* (telemetry) and Frappe Cloud keys. See the site config reference.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Overrides FRAPPE_DB_TYPE, FRAPPE_DB_HOST, FRAPPE_DB_PORT, FRAPPE_DB_SOCKET The matching db_* keys. FRAPPE_REDIS_QUEUE, FRAPPE_REDIS_CACHE redis_queue, redis_cache. FRAPPE_SITE Default site for bench commands. SITES_PATH Sites folder of the WSGI app (frappe.app). Default .. FRAPPE_BENCH_ROOT Bench folder. FRAPPE_SENTRY_DSN Send errors to Sentry. FRAPPE_SOCKETIO_PORT, FRAPPE_SOCKETIO_UDS socketio_port, socketio_uds for the Node Socket.IO server.

Environment variables win over both JSON files. v15 has no environment variables for db_name or db_password.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A key in site_config.json hides the same key in common_site_config.json for that site.
  • common keys in site_config.json have no effect.
  • frappe.conf is loaded per request. A long-running process (worker, scheduler, Socket.IO) reads some keys only at startup.
  • bench set-config writes valid JSON. Hand edits that break the JSON print "site_config.json is invalid", and the file is ignored.
  • Do not commit site_config.json or common_site_config.json to a repository.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: A Frappe bench runs as a set of processes: a web server, background workers, a scheduler, a realtime (socketio) server and two Redis servers. In development, bench start runs them from the Procfile. In production, the bench CLI generates supervisor (or systemd) and nginx configuration. The bench CLI is a separate package (frappe-bench). The commands on this page were checked against bench CLI 5.31.1.

docs.title: Processes
docs.text:
Process Command Description Web bench serve (development), gunicorn ... frappe.app:application (production) Serves desk, website and API requests. Worker bench worker --queue <queues> Runs background jobs from Redis queues. Scheduler bench schedule Enqueues Scheduled Job Types at their time. It does not run the jobs. Realtime bench socketio Socket.IO server for realtime events (Node). Redis cache redis-server config/redis_cache.conf Cache, locks, rate limit counters, realtime pub/sub. Redis queue redis-server config/redis_queue.conf Background job queues.

All processes serve all sites of the bench. The web process finds the site from the X-Frappe-Site-Name header or from the host name of the request (init_request in frappe/app.py).

docs.title: Workers
docs.text:
bench worker options:

Option Description --queue Queues to consume, comma-separated, for example short,default. Without it, the worker consumes all queues. --burst Stop when the queues are empty. --strategy round_robin or random dequeue order. --quiet Hide log output. -u, --rq-username / -p, --rq-password Redis ACL user and password.

bench worker-pool --queue <queues> --num-workers 2 starts a pool of workers in one process. The standard queues are short, default and long. Add your own queues in common_site_config.json with the workers key. See Background Jobs.

docs.title: Realtime
docs.text: In v15 the realtime server is Node only. bench socketio runs apps/frappe/socketio.js. The bench CLI also reads socketio_backend from common_site_config.json. v15 has no frappe.realtime.server module, so the value python falls back to Node with a warning. The desk reads socketio_port from the boot info to connect.

docs.title: Development: Procfile
docs.text:
bench init and bench setup procfile write Procfile in the bench root. bench start runs it with honcho.

redis_cache: redis-server config/redis_cache.conf
redis_queue: redis-server config/redis_queue.conf
web: bench serve --port 8000
socketio: bench socketio
watch: bench watch
schedule: bench schedule
worker: bench worker 1>> logs/worker.log 2>> logs/worker.error.log

Each entry under workers in common_site_config.json adds a line worker_<name>: bench worker --queue <name>.

docs.title: Production setup
docs.text:
Run these commands from the bench root as the bench user. They need sudo.

  1. Turn off developer mode on each site: bench --site <site> set-config developer_mode 0.
  2. Build assets: bench build --production.
  3. Run sudo bench setup production <user>. <user> is the system user that owns the bench.
  4. Check that the processes run: sudo supervisorctl status.

bench setup production <user>:

  1. Installs Ansible, fail2ban, nginx and supervisor if they are missing.
  2. Writes config/supervisor.conf (or systemd units if restart_systemd_on_update is set).
  3. Writes config/nginx.conf.
  4. Links config/supervisor.conf into the supervisor config folder and config/nginx.conf to /etc/nginx/conf.d/<bench-name>.conf.
  5. Reloads supervisor and nginx.

You cannot set both restart_supervisor_on_update and restart_systemd_on_update. bench disable-production removes the links.

docs.title: supervisor
docs.text:
config/supervisor.conf has these programs:

Program Command <bench>-frappe-web gunicorn -b 127.0.0.1:<webserver_port> -w <gunicorn_workers> ... frappe.app:application --preload <bench>-frappe-schedule bench schedule <bench>-frappe-short-worker bench worker --queue short,default <bench>-frappe-long-worker bench worker --queue long,default,short <bench>-frappe-<name>-worker bench worker --queue <name>, one per workers entry <bench>-redis-cache, <bench>-redis-queue Redis servers <bench>-node-socketio bench socketio

v15 is later than frappe 14.18.0, so the bench CLI uses multi-queue consumption and does not add a separate default worker. Groups: <bench>-web (web and socketio), <bench>-workers (scheduler and workers), <bench>-redis.

Bench config keys in common_site_config.json that change this file:

Key Default Description webserver_port 8000 Port of gunicorn. gunicorn_workers CPU count x 2 + 1 gunicorn worker processes. gunicorn_max_requests computed Restart a gunicorn worker after this many requests. http_timeout 120 gunicorn timeout in seconds. background_workers 1 Number of processes for each worker program. workers {} Extra queues: {"<name>": {"timeout": 300, "background_workers": 2}}.

After you change a key, run bench setup supervisor and sudo supervisorctl reread && sudo supervisorctl update.

docs.title: nginx
docs.text: config/nginx.conf serves /assets and public files from disk. It sends /socket.io to the socketio server and other requests to gunicorn. It sets X-Frappe-Site-Name on proxied requests. Private files are served through an internal /protected/ location after Frappe checks permission. Run bench setup nginx and sudo bench setup reload-nginx after you add a site or a domain.

docs.title: Multitenancy and DNS
docs.text:
• DNS multitenancy (bench config dns_multitenant on): all sites share port 80. nginx routes by host name. The site folder name must match the domain, for example sites/erp.example.com.
  • Port-based multitenancy (default): each site gets its own port. Set it with bench set-nginx-port <site> <port>.
  • Add more domains to a site with bench setup add-domain <domain> --site <site>.
  • Get TLS certificates with sudo bench setup lets-encrypt <site>, or bench setup wildcard-ssl <domain>.

Run bench setup nginx after each change, then reload nginx.

docs.title: Updates and maintenance
docs.text:
bench update pulls apps, installs requirements, runs migrate on all sites, builds assets and restarts. Options include --pull, --patch, --build, --requirements, --restart-supervisor, --restart-systemd, --no-backup and --reset.

For a manual upgrade of one site:

bench --site erp.example.com set-maintenance-mode on
bench --site erp.example.com ready-for-migration
bench --site erp.example.com migrate
bench --site erp.example.com set-maintenance-mode off
bench restart
  • set-maintenance-mode on sets maintenance_mode in the site config. The scheduler stops enqueuing jobs. Web requests fail with SessionStopped. To keep reads during maintenance, set allow_reads_during_maintenance to 1. Frappe then opens a read-only transaction, or connects to the replica when read_from_replica is set.
  • ready-for-migration checks three times, one second apart, and exits with code 1 if the site still has pending background jobs.
  • bench --site <site> scheduler pause and scheduler resume set pause_scheduler in the site config. scheduler disable and scheduler enable change the setting in System Settings. scheduler status shows the state. enable-scheduler and disable-scheduler are also available.
  • bench doctor shows worker and scheduler status. bench --site <site> show-pending-jobs lists queued jobs.

See Upgrading for version changes.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
• Raise gunicorn_workers for more parallel requests. Each worker is a process with its own memory.
  • Raise background_workers, or add queues under workers, for more job throughput. Put slow jobs on long so that they do not block short.
  • Run more benches behind a load balancer only with a shared database, shared Redis and shared file storage. All benches must run the same app versions.
  • Point db_host, redis_cache and redis_queue in common_site_config.json to external servers when you move them off the bench host.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not run bench start in production. It runs bench watch and the development server.
  • Do not keep developer_mode on in production. In developer mode, saving a standard DocType writes its files to the app folder.
  • Restart the workers after a code change. They keep the old code in memory.
  • Keep backups of sites/*/site_config.json. They hold the database password and encryption_key.
  • Maintenance mode in v15 blocks all web requests unless allow_reads_during_maintenance is set. Plan the downtime.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: This page shows how to upgrade a bench to v15 from v14, and what the v15 patches change on a site. It lists only changes that the v15 code and frappe/patches.txt show. The last section lists changes to prepare for before you move to v16. Read it before you upgrade, and test the upgrade on a copy of the site.

docs.title: Upgrade steps
docs.text:
1. Take a backup with files: bench --site <site> backup --with-files. Keep the encryption_key from site_config.json.
  2. Check the Python and Node versions below. Install the new versions first.
  3. Update each app to the version-15 branch. All apps on a bench must support the same Frappe version.
  4. Run bench setup requirements to install Python and Node dependencies.
  5. Run bench --site <site> migrate for each site.
  6. Run bench build.
  7. Restart the processes: bench restart in production, or start bench start again in development.

In production, turn on maintenance mode before step 5 with bench --site <site> set-maintenance-mode on, and turn it off after step 7. In v15, maintenance mode blocks all web requests unless allow_reads_during_maintenance is set. bench update from the bench CLI runs the pull, requirements, migrate, build and restart steps for you. See Deployment.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
v15 Python (requires-python in pyproject.toml) >=3.10,<3.15 Node (engines.node in package.json) >=18

If the bench runs an older Python, make a new virtual environment: bench setup env --python python3.11, then bench setup requirements.

docs.title: Upgrading to v15
docs.text:
The v15_0 patches in frappe/patches.txt make these changes when you run bench migrate:

Change Patch Event Streaming is removed from frappe. If the event_streaming app is not installed, the patch deletes the Event Streaming module and its DocTypes (Event Producer, Event Consumer, Event Update Log, Event Sync Log and others). Install the event_streaming app before you migrate to keep them. remove_event_streaming Log tables that had an integer name column without autoincrement (for example Error Log, Version, Access Log, Email Queue) get a varchar name column. remove_implicit_primary_key On MariaDB, the modified index is dropped from all child tables. drop_modified_index The expiry of Prepared Reports moves from System Settings (prepared_report_expiry_period) to Log Settings. remove_prepared_report_settings_from_system_settings Reports with disable_prepared_report set get prepared_report 0 and disable_prepared_report_automation 1. copy_disable_prepared_report_to_prepared_report Events with Event Type Cancelled get Event Type Private and Status Cancelled. move_event_cancelled_to_status Files without file_type get it from the file extension. set_file_type Contacts without full_name get it from their name parts. set_contact_full_name Email Group Members with an invalid email are set to unsubscribed. validate_newsletter_recipients HTML is removed from Workspace titles. sanitize_workspace_titles The "Background Jobs" and "Workspace Settings" items are removed from the navbar menu. remove_background_jobs_from_dropdown, remove_workspace_settings_navbar_items If website signups were on only from the old default, the patch turns on Disable Signups in Website Settings and notifies System Managers. disable_default_website_signups The snapshot report frequency in System Settings is set to Weekly. set_snapshot_report_frequency_to_weekly

docs.title: Code changes to check in your app
docs.text:
• frappe.cache is an object. Call its methods directly, for example frappe.cache.get_value(key). frappe.cache() still works for backward compatibility (__call__ in frappe/utils/redis_wrapper.py).
  • Gravatar support is removed. frappe.utils.has_gravatar and frappe.utils.get_gravatar_url are deprecated and return an empty string.
  • Test classes extend frappe.tests.utils.FrappeTestCase. See Testing.
  • If your app has Report records with disable_prepared_report in fixtures, change them to prepared_report and disable_prepared_report_automation.

docs.title: Deprecation warnings in v15
docs.text:
v15 shows a DeprecationWarning (through frappe.utils.deprecations.deprecation_warning) for these calls. They still work in v15.

Deprecated Use instead Sending cmd in the form data of a request /api/method/<dotted.path> A short method name in an RPC call (no dot) The full dotted path frappe.db.set_value on a Single DocType frappe.db.set_single_value frappe.enqueue(..., job_name=...) job_id frappe.enqueue(..., is_async=False) outside tests now=True uploadfile method upload_file. The code says uploadfile is removed in v16. super(Document, self).__init__(d) in a controller self.init_from_dict(d) frappe.db.is_column_missing frappe.db.is_missing_column frappe.utils.gzip_compress, gzip_decompress The gzip module User.validate_roles User.populate_role_profile_roles frappe.geo.country_info.get_translated_dict get_translated_countries frappe.client.get_js, frappe.utils.print_format.read_multi_pdf No replacement

To see the warnings in a run, set PYTHONWARNINGS=default::DeprecationWarning.

docs.title: Preparing for v16
docs.text:
These changes come from a comparison of the v15 code with the v16 code. Check them before you upgrade a v15 bench to v16.

  • Python 3.14 and Node 24. v16 needs Python >=3.14,<3.15 and Node >=24. Make a new virtual environment with bench setup env --python python3.14.
  • Desk route. The desk moves from /app to /desk. v16 redirects /app/... to /desk/.... Use frappe.set_route and frappe.utils.get_url_to_form instead of building /app/ URLs.
  • Modules move to separate apps. Blog (Blog Post, Blog Category, Blogger, Blog Settings), Newsletter, Energy Points, and the Dropbox, S3 and Google Drive backups are not in v16 frappe. Install blogs, newsletter, eps or offsite_backups to keep them. The leaderboards hook is not read in v16.
  • SQL strings in fields. v16 frappe.get_list and frappe.get_all raise ValidationError for SQL functions written as strings, for example "count(name) as c". Use the dict form {"COUNT": "name", "as": "c"}, which does not work in v15.
  • Default sort. New DocTypes sort by creation in v16. A v16 patch adds a creation index to all parent tables (MariaDB) and changes saved list sorts. Pass order_by="modified desc" where you need the last change first.
  • Session IDs are stored as SHA-256 hashes. Code that reads tabSessions by the raw cookie value stops working.
  • frappe.get_version is removed in v16.
  • Test classes. v16 has frappe.tests.UnitTestCase and frappe.tests.IntegrationTestCase. FrappeTestCase still works with a deprecation warning.
  • Deprecations. v16 moves deprecated functions to frappe/deprecation_dumpster.py, with a version after which each one is an error.
