docs.title: Reports, Printing and Email
docs.text:
Write script and query reports, print formats and PDFs, and send email and notifications.

Page What it covers Reports Build Script Reports and Query Reports in an app, define filters, return charts and summaries, run reports from code, and use prepared reports and report roles. Print Formats Ship Print Formats in an app, write Jinja print templates, render HTML or PDF with frappe.get_print, and know how wkhtmltopdf, WeasyPrint and the pdf_generator hook make PDFs. Email and Notifications Send email with frappe.sendmail and the Email Queue, use Email Templates, ship Notifications in an app, log Communications, handle incoming email and create system notifications.

docs.title: Email and Notifications
docs.text: Frappe sends all outgoing email through the Email Queue. Your code calls frappe.sendmail(), and the scheduler sends the queue in the background. Use a Notification to send email, system notifications, SMS or Slack messages when a document event happens, without code in the controller. Use Communication to keep an email thread on a document. For setup of email accounts and the desk side, see Email (user guide) and Notifications (user guide).

docs.title: Send email
docs.text:
frappe.sendmail(
    recipients=["user1@example.com"],
    subject="Order SO-00001 is ready",
    message="<p>Your order is ready.</p>",
    reference_doctype="Sample Order",
    reference_name="SO-00001",
    attachments=[
        {
            "print_format_attachment": 1,
            "doctype": "Sample Order",
            "name": "SO-00001",
            "print_format": "Standard",
        }
    ],
)

frappe.sendmail() builds an Email Queue document and returns it. It does not send the email now, unless now=True. The scheduler job frappe.email.queue.flush (event all) sends queued email. A default outgoing Email Account must exist, or Frappe raises frappe.OutgoingEmailError.

Parameter Default Description recipients [] List of addresses, or a comma-separated string. sender "" From address. Empty uses the outgoing Email Account. subject "No Subject" Subject line. message / content "No Message" HTML body. content wins when both are set. as_markdown False Convert the body from Markdown to HTML. template, args None Render templates/emails/<template>.html (and .txt) with args. cc, bcc [] Copy recipients. reply_to None Reply-To address. reference_doctype, reference_name None Link the email to a document. Also doctype and name. attachments None List of attachment dicts. See below. delayed True False is the same as now=True. now None Send at once, in the current request, instead of waiting for the scheduler. send_after None Do not send before this datetime. send_priority 1 Higher values are sent first. queue_separately False Make one Email Queue per recipient, in a background job. Frappe also does this for more than 100 recipients. expose_recipients None "header" shows all To recipients. "footer" adds "This email was sent to ..." text. add_unsubscribe_link 1 Add an unsubscribe link. unsubscribe_method, unsubscribe_params, unsubscribe_message None Customize the unsubscribe link. header None Add a header block to the email. with_container False Wrap the body in a styled container. print_letterhead False Add the letter head to print attachments. inline_images None List of {"filename", "filecontent"}. read_receipt None Ask for a read receipt. x_priority 3 1 highest, 3 normal, 5 lowest. email_headers None Extra headers. Frappe adds X- when it is missing. message_id, in_reply_to None Message-Id headers for threading. is_notification False Mark the email as a notification. redact_message_after_send False Replace the stored body with a placeholder after it is sent. communication None Link the Email Queue to a Communication.

docs.title: Attachments
docs.text:
Shape Description {"fname": "a.txt", "fcontent": b"..."} File content in memory. {"fid": "<File name>"} or {"file_url": "/files/a.pdf"} An existing File. Read when the email is sent. {"print_format_attachment": 1, "doctype": ..., "name": ..., "print_format": ...} A print of a document. Made with frappe.attach_print() when the email is sent.

You can also pass the return value of frappe.attach_print(doctype, name, print_format=...) directly. See Print Formats.

docs.title: Email templates in files
docs.text:
template="sample_order_ready" renders templates/emails/sample_order_ready.html from any app with args as context. A .txt file with the same name gives the plain text part.

{# sample_app/templates/emails/sample_order_ready.html #}
<p>{{ _("Hello") }} {{ customer_name }},</p>
<p>{{ _("Order {0} is ready.").format(order) }}</p>

frappe.sendmail(
    recipients=["user1@example.com"],
    subject="Order ready",
    template="sample_order_ready",
    args={"customer_name": "Customer A", "order": "SO-00001"},
)

docs.title: Email Template
docs.text:
An Email Template is a document with a Jinja subject and response (or response_html when use_html is set). Users pick it in the email dialog. Render it from code with get_formatted_email(doc).

template = frappe.get_doc("Email Template", "Sample Order Ready")
email = template.get_formatted_email(frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", "SO-00001").as_dict())
# {'subject': 'Order SO-00001 is ready', 'message': 'Hello Customer A'}

frappe.sendmail(recipients=["user1@example.com"], **email)

The whitelisted method frappe.email.doctype.email_template.email_template.get_email_template(template_name, doc, sender=None) does the same for the client. It checks read permission on the template.

docs.title: Communication
docs.text:
A Communication is one email (or comment, call, chat) linked to a document with reference_doctype and reference_name. It shows in the document timeline. The desk email dialog calls frappe.core.doctype.communication.email.make.

from frappe.core.doctype.communication.email import make

make(
    doctype="Sample Order",
    name="SO-00001",
    subject="Order update",
    content="<p>Your order ships today.</p>",
    recipients="user1@example.com",
    send_email=True,
    print_format="Standard",
)

make() only works for system users. It checks email permission on the reference document and create permission on Communication. With send_email=True, it queues the email. Without it, it only saves the Communication.

After a Communication is saved, Frappe calls on_communication_update(communication) on the reference document, if the controller has it. Otherwise it runs the default update (status and response time fields) and calls notify_communication(communication).

# sample_app/sample_app/selling/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
class SampleOrder(Document):
    def on_communication_update(self, communication):
        if communication.sent_or_received == "Received":
            self.db_set("status", "Open")

docs.title: Incoming email
docs.text:
An Email Account with enable_incoming pulls email every 10 minutes (frappe.email.doctype.email_account.email_account.pull). Each email becomes a Communication. To make documents from email:

  1. Set email_append_to on your DocType.
  2. Set subject_field and sender_field on the DocType. Optional: sender_name_field.
  3. In the Email Account, set Append To to your DocType (or set it per IMAP folder).

For a new thread, InboundMail creates a document of that DocType with the subject and sender, with ignore_mandatory, and links the Communication to it. For a reply, it finds the document from the In-Reply-To header, or by subject and sender.

The Email Account lists DocTypes with email_append_to set, and DocTypes with a Property Setter for it.

docs.title: Notifications in an app
docs.text:
A Notification sends a message when a document event happens. A standard Notification (is_standard = 1) is exported to the app when you save it in developer mode.

sample_app/sample_app/selling/notification/sample_order_submitted/
├── __init__.py
├── sample_order_submitted.json   # the Notification document
├── sample_order_submitted.md     # message (.html or .txt for other message types)
└── sample_order_submitted.py     # get_context(context)

# sample_app/sample_app/selling/notification/sample_order_submitted/sample_order_submitted.py
def get_context(context):
    context.items_count = len(context.doc.items)

<!-- sample_order_submitted.md -->
Order **{{ doc.name }}** for {{ doc.customer_name }} has {{ items_count }} items.

The message, subject and condition get doc, nowdate and frappe.utils (the safe date and number helpers). A standard Notification can only be enabled or changed in developer mode. A Notification on a child table DocType allows only Days Before and Days After.

Field Values channel Email, Slack, System Notification, SMS slack_webhook_url Link to a Slack Webhook URL document, for the Slack channel event New, Save, Submit, Cancel, Value Change, Method, Days Before, Days After, Custom condition A Python expression, checked with frappe.safe_eval method Controller method name for the Method event, for example on_payment message_type Markdown, HTML, Plain Text recipients Table of receiver_by_document_field, receiver_by_role, cc, bcc and a condition per row send_to_all_assignees Also send to the users the document is assigned to attach_print, print_format Attach a print of the document send_system_notification Also create a system notification for email recipients set_property_after_alert, property_value Set a field after the notification is sent

How events fire (Document.run_notifications in frappe/model/document.py):

Event Runs on New after_insert Save on_update Submit on_submit Cancel on_cancel Value Change on_change, not during insert or delete Method doc.run_method("<method>") with the method in method Days Before, Days After Daily job trigger_daily_alerts Custom Never by Frappe. An app calls evaluate_alert(doc, notification_name, "Custom") from frappe/email/doctype/notification/notification.py.

To fire a Method notification from code, call the method with run_method:

doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", "SO-00001")
doc.run_method("on_payment")

Notifications do not run during install, patches, or imports with mute_emails.

docs.title: Slack
docs.text: For the Slack channel, create a Slack Webhook URL document with the incoming webhook URL of the Slack channel. Set show_document_link to add a button that opens the document. send_slack_message(webhook_url, message, reference_doctype, reference_name) in frappe/integrations/doctype/slack_webhook_url/slack_webhook_url.py posts the rendered message.

docs.title: System notifications
docs.text:
A system notification is a Notification Log row. Users see it in the bell menu of the desk. Create them with enqueue_create_notification.

from frappe.desk.doctype.notification_log.notification_log import enqueue_create_notification

enqueue_create_notification(
    ["user1@example.com", "user2@example.com"],
    {
        "type": "Alert",
        "subject": "Order SO-00001 needs approval",
        "document_type": "Sample Order",
        "document_name": "SO-00001",
        "from_user": frappe.session.user,
    },
)
  • type is a link to Notification Type. Frappe installs Mention, Energy Point, Assignment, Share and Alert.
  • The logs are made in a background job after commit.
  • A user does not get a notification for their own action (for_user == from_user), except for types in the notification_self_notify_types hook (Alert and Energy Point).
  • Pass dedupe_on=["document_type", "document_name"] to skip users who already have a matching log.
  • Notification Settings decide if a log also sends an email. Types in notification_skip_email_types (Alert) never send their own email.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Hook Use email_css CSS files added to every email (["email.bundle.css"] in Frappe). make_email_body_message Functions that get the email object before it is sent. Change headers or parts. override_email_send One function (email_queue, sender, recipient, message) that sends instead of SMTP. default_mail_footer HTML added to the footer of every email. email_append_to Declared in Frappe (["Event", "ToDo", "Communication"]), but no code reads it. Use the DocType property. notification_config Function that gives open counts for the desk ("for_doctype", "for_module"). notification_self_notify_types Notification Types that also notify the user who acted. notification_skip_email_types Notification Types that never send their own email.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• frappe.sendmail() queues the email in the current transaction. If the transaction rolls back, the email is not sent.
  • now=True sends at once, before the transaction commits. If the transaction rolls back later, the email is already sent. Use it only for urgent email, like password reset.
  • In tests (frappe.flags.in_test), the queue is built but not sent over SMTP, unless frappe.flags.testing_email is set.
  • Set reference_doctype and reference_name so replies link back to the document.
  • Use _() in templates, and send with frappe.translate.print_language when the recipient uses another language.

docs.title: Print Formats
docs.text: A Print Format decides how a document looks when printed, sent as a PDF, or attached to an email. Each Print Format document is linked to a DocType (doc_type) or to a report (print_format_for = "Report"). Users design most formats in the desk (see Printing (user guide)). As a developer you ship formats in your app, render them from code, and extend the PDF pipeline.

docs.title: Kinds of Print Format
docs.text:
Kind Fields Rendered by Standard No Print Format, or "Standard" Layout of the DocType form, frappe/www/printview.py Print Format Builder format_data (layout JSON) The standard template with the saved layout Print Format Builder (Beta) print_format_builder_beta = 1, format_data PrintFormatGenerator in frappe/utils/weasyprint.py Custom Jinja custom_format = 1, print_format_type = "Jinja", html get_rendered_template() in frappe/www/printview.py Raw printing custom_format = 1, raw_printing = 1, raw_commands Sent to a printer as raw commands

print_format_type can also be JS, a format that the desk renders in the browser. Frappe does not check its html as Jinja. A format with print_format_for = "Report" is always custom and not standard.

docs.title: Print Formats in an app
docs.text:
Set standard to "Yes" and save in developer mode. export_doc() writes the JSON to the module folder. For a Jinja format, put the template in an .html file with the same name. get_print_format() reads that file before the html field.

sample_app/sample_app/selling/print_format/sample_order_slip/
├── sample_order_slip.json
└── sample_order_slip.html

{# sample_app/sample_app/selling/print_format/sample_order_slip/sample_order_slip.html #}
<h2>{{ doc.name }}</h2>
<p>{{ doc.customer_name }}, {{ doc.get_formatted("order_date") }}</p>
<table class="table table-bordered">
    {% for row in doc.items %}
    <tr>
        <td>{{ row.item }}</td>
        <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("qty") }}</td>
        <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("amount", doc) }}</td>
    </tr>
    {% endfor %}
</table>
<p class="text-right"><b>{{ _("Total") }}: {{ doc.get_formatted("total") }}</b></p>

Without developer mode, a standard Print Format cannot be saved ("Standard Print Format cannot be updated").

docs.title: Template context
docs.text:
get_rendered_template() renders the template with these variables:

Name Value doc The document. Use doc.get_formatted("<fieldname>") for values in the user's format. meta frappe.get_meta(doc.doctype) layout The form layout in sections and columns (make_layout) no_letterhead 1 when the letter head is off letter_head Rendered letter head HTML footer Rendered letter head footer HTML print_settings Print Settings as a dict trigger_print 1 when the page opens the print dialog

The Jinja globals of Website are also available, for example frappe.db.get_value and _. Methods and filters from the jinja hook work too. validate_template checks the Jinja when you save.

docs.title: Before print
docs.text:
Before it renders, Frappe sets doc.flags.in_print and calls the controller method before_print(settings). Use it to set values that only the print shows.

# sample_app/sample_app/selling/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
class SampleOrder(Document):
    def before_print(self, settings=None):
        self.print_heading = f"Order {self.name}"

docs.title: Render from code
docs.text:
frappe.get_print() (from frappe/utils/print_utils.py) returns HTML, or PDF bytes with as_pdf=True. It renders the printview page, so the print permission check applies to the current user.

html = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001")
pdf = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001", print_format="Sample Order Slip", as_pdf=True)

with open("/tmp/so-00001.pdf", "wb") as f:
    f.write(pdf)
Parameter Default Description doctype, name None The document to print. print_format None Print Format name. Empty uses the DocType default, then "Standard". style None Print Style name. Empty uses Print Settings print_style. as_pdf False Return PDF bytes instead of HTML. doc None A document object to print instead of loading it. output None A pypdf.PdfWriter. Pages are added to it. no_letterhead 0 Leave out the letter head. password None Encrypt the PDF with this password. pdf_options None wkhtmltopdf options, for example {"page-size": "A5"}. letterhead None Letter Head name to use. pdf_generator None "wkhtmltopdf" or a value that a pdf_generator hook of another app handles. Empty uses the format's pdf_generator, then wkhtmltopdf.

frappe.attach_print(doctype, name, print_format=None, ...) returns {"fname": ..., "fcontent": ...} for an email attachment. It returns a PDF when Print Settings send_print_as_pdf is on (the default), else HTML. It skips the print permission check (frappe.local.flags.ignore_print_permissions). For a Print Format Builder (Beta) format, it makes the PDF with WeasyPrint.

frappe.translate.print_language("de") is a context manager that prints in another language.

docs.title: URLs
docs.text:
URL Returns /printview?doctype=Sample Order&name=SO-00001&format=Sample Order Slip HTML print view /Sample Order/SO-00001 HTML print view (PrintPage renderer) /api/method/frappe.utils.print_format.download_pdf?doctype=Sample Order&name=SO-00001&format=... PDF download /api/method/frappe.utils.print_format.download_multi_pdf One PDF for many documents /api/method/frappe.utils.weasyprint.download_pdf PDF of a Print Format Builder (Beta) format

download_pdf takes doctype, name, format, no_letterhead, language, letterhead and pdf_generator. It checks print permission on the document.

docs.title: PDF generation
docs.text:
Frappe makes PDFs with wkhtmltopdf through pdfkit (frappe.utils.pdf.get_pdf). The pdf_generator field of Print Format has one option, wkhtmltopdf, and that is the default. Print Settings has no engine field.

get_pdf(html, options=None, output=None) does this:

  1. It turns relative URLs into absolute URLs. wkhtmltopdf loads images and CSS from the site URL.
  2. It reads page options from the .print-format CSS rule in the HTML: margin-top, margin-bottom, margin-left, margin-right, page-size, header-spacing, orientation, page-width, page-height.
  3. It sets page-size from Print Settings pdf_page_size (default A4), or pdf_page_height and pdf_page_width for Custom. The default left and right margins are 15mm.
  4. It turns off JavaScript and local file access in wkhtmltopdf.
  5. It builds the repeating header and footer with the pdf_header_html and pdf_footer_html hooks.

docs.title: The pdf_generator hook
docs.text:
Frappe ships no pdf_generator hook. An app, for example Print Designer, adds one and an extra option for the pdf_generator field. When the engine is not wkhtmltopdf, get_print(as_pdf=True) calls each function in the hook. The first one that returns bytes wins. If none returns a value, Frappe falls back to wkhtmltopdf.

# sample_app/hooks.py
pdf_generator = ["sample_app.pdf.get_sample_pdf"]

# sample_app/pdf.py
def get_sample_pdf(print_format, html, options, output, pdf_generator=None):
    if pdf_generator != "Sample Engine":
        return None
    return render_with_sample_engine(html, options)  # must return PDF bytes

To let users pick the engine, add Sample Engine to the options of the pdf_generator field of Print Format, for example with a Property Setter in your fixtures.

docs.title: Other print hooks
docs.text: Hook Called with Use on_print_pdf doctype, name, print_format Run code before wkhtmltopdf makes a PDF, for example to log it. get_print_format_template jenv, print_format Return a compiled Jinja template to use instead of the format's HTML. The last app wins. pdf_body_html jenv, template, print_format, args Render the body HTML. Frappe sets frappe.utils.pdf.pdf_body_html. The last app wins. pdf_header_html, pdf_footer_html soup, head, content, styles, html_id, css Build the repeating header and footer.

docs.title: Letter heads
docs.text: get_letter_head() uses, in order: the letterhead argument, the document's letter_head field, then the Letter Head with is_default = 1. When no_letterhead is not passed, Print Settings with_letterhead decides. Frappe renders the letter head content and footer with Jinja and {"doc": doc.as_dict()}, so you can use {{ doc.customer_name }} in a letter head.

docs.title: Print styles
docs.text: Frappe renders templates/styles/standard.css, then adds the css of the selected Print Style, then the css of the Print Format. The default style is Redesign. Frappe ships the styles in frappe/printing/print_style/ (Classic, Modern, Monochrome, Redesign).

docs.title: Raw printing
docs.text: A raw format sends printer commands (for example ESC/POS or ZPL) instead of HTML. Set raw_printing and write the commands in raw_commands with Jinja. frappe.www.printview.get_rendered_raw_commands(doc, name, print_format) returns the rendered commands. The desk sends them to the printer through QZ Tray when Print Settings enable_raw_printing is on.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A draft document of a submittable DocType prints only when Print Settings allow_print_for_draft is on (the default). A cancelled one needs allow_print_for_cancelled.
  • Fields with print_hide and fields above the user's permission level are not printed.
  • Use get_formatted() instead of raw values. Raw values do not follow the user's date, number and currency format.
  • wkhtmltopdf fetches images and CSS over HTTP from the site URL. If the server cannot reach its own host name, PDF generation hangs or images are missing.
  • wkhtmltopdf runs with disable-javascript. Scripts in a print format do not run in the PDF.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
A report is a Report document. Its report_type decides how it gets data. Use a Script Report when you need Python logic, joins or computed columns. Use a Query Report for one SQL query. Report Builder and Custom Report are saved views that users make in the desk. For the desk side, see Reports (user guide).

report_type Data comes from Made by Report Builder A saved list view of ref_doctype (json field) Users, in Report view Query Report The SQL in query Developers or System Managers Script Report execute(filters) in a Python file (standard) or report_script (not standard) Developers Custom Report A saved copy of a Query or Script Report with its own columns and filters Users, with "Save As"

docs.title: Script Report in an app
docs.text:
A standard Script Report (is_standard = "Yes") lives in the module folder of the app.

sample_app/sample_app/selling/report/sample_order_summary/
├── __init__.py
├── sample_order_summary.json   # the Report document
├── sample_order_summary.py     # execute(filters)
└── sample_order_summary.js     # filters and client options
  1. Turn on developer_mode in site config.
  2. Log in as Administrator.
  3. Create a Report with report_type "Script Report", ref_doctype "Sample Order" and a module of your app.
  4. Save. In developer mode, Frappe sets is_standard to "Yes" and writes the JSON, .py and .js boilerplate.
  5. Fill in the .py and .js files.
  6. Commit the folder. bench migrate syncs the report to other sites.

Frappe finds the module as <app>.<module>.report.<report_name>.<report_name> (get_report_module_dotted_path). A standard report cannot be edited without developer mode. Duplicate it instead.

docs.title: The Python file
docs.text:
execute(filters) gets the filter values as a frappe._dict and returns a tuple or list. Frappe reads up to six items, in this order:

Position Name Type Description 0 columns list Column definitions. Dicts or strings. 1 data list Rows. Each row is a dict (keys are column fieldname) or a list in column order. 2 message str HTML shown above the table. 3 chart dict Chart shown above the table. 4 report_summary list Number cards shown above the table. 5 skip_total_row bool Do not add the total row for this run. 
# sample_app/sample_app/selling/report/sample_order_summary/sample_order_summary.py
import frappe
from frappe import _


def execute(filters=None):
    filters = frappe._dict(filters or {})
    columns = get_columns()
    data = get_data(filters)
    return columns, data, None, get_chart(data), get_summary(data)


def get_columns():
    return [
        {"label": _("Order"), "fieldname": "name", "fieldtype": "Link", "options": "Sample Order", "width": 140},
        {"label": _("Customer"), "fieldname": "customer_name", "fieldtype": "Data", "width": 180},
        {"label": _("Order Date"), "fieldname": "order_date", "fieldtype": "Date", "width": 110},
        {"label": _("Status"), "fieldname": "status", "fieldtype": "Data", "width": 100},
        {"label": _("Total"), "fieldname": "total", "fieldtype": "Currency", "width": 120},
    ]


def get_data(filters):
    conditions = {"docstatus": ["<", 2]}
    if filters.status:
        conditions["status"] = filters.status
    if filters.from_date and filters.to_date:
        conditions["order_date"] = ["between", [filters.from_date, filters.to_date]]

    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Order",
        filters=conditions,
        fields=["name", "customer_name", "order_date", "status", "total"],
        order_by="order_date desc",
    )


def get_chart(data):
    return {
        "data": {
            "labels": [row.name for row in data],
            "datasets": [{"name": _("Total"), "values": [row.total for row in data]}],
        },
        "type": "bar",
    }


def get_summary(data):
    return [
        {"label": _("Orders"), "value": len(data), "datatype": "Int"},
        {"label": _("Total"), "value": sum(row.total for row in data), "datatype": "Currency", "indicator": "Green"},
    ]

A column can also be a string in the form "Label:Fieldtype/Options:Width", for example "Order:Link/Sample Order:150". Frappe converts it to a dict and makes the fieldname from the label.

The chart dict goes to Frappe Charts: data.labels, data.datasets[].name, data.datasets[].values, and type (for example bar, line, pie, percentage, axis-mixed). A summary item has label, value and datatype. It can also have indicator (Green, Red, Blue and other colors) and currency.

When the report has snapshot_report set, Frappe calls execute_snapshot_report(filters) in the module instead of execute.

docs.title: The JS file
docs.text:
The .js file sets frappe.query_reports["<Report Name>"]. The key must be the report name.

// sample_app/sample_app/selling/report/sample_order_summary/sample_order_summary.js
frappe.query_reports["Sample Order Summary"] = {
    filters: [
        {
            fieldname: "status",
            label: __("Status"),
            fieldtype: "Select",
            options: ["", "Draft", "Open", "Completed"],
        },
        {
            fieldname: "from_date",
            label: __("From Date"),
            fieldtype: "Date",
            default: frappe.datetime.add_months(frappe.datetime.get_today(), -1),
        },
        {
            fieldname: "to_date",
            label: __("To Date"),
            fieldtype: "Date",
            default: frappe.datetime.get_today(),
        },
    ],
    formatter(value, row, column, data, default_formatter) {
        value = default_formatter(value, row, column, data);
        if (column.fieldname === "status" && data && data.status === "Open") {
            value = `<b>${value}</b>`;
        }
        return value;
    },
    onload(report) {
        report.page.add_inner_button(__("Refresh"), () => report.refresh());
    },
};

A filter is a field definition (fieldname, label, fieldtype, options, default, reqd, depends_on, on_change, get_query). Read a value with frappe.query_report.get_filter_value("status"). Set one with frappe.query_report.set_filter_value("status", "Open").

Other keys that the report view reads: onload, formatter, get_datatable_options, after_datatable_render, get_chart_data, get_pdf_format, tree, parent_field, initial_depth, export_hidden_cols. A <report_name>.html file in the report folder is the print template of the report.

docs.title: The filters table
docs.text: The Report has a filters table (Report Filter) with fieldname, label, fieldtype, options, mandatory, default and wildcard_filter. Use it for reports that have no JS file, for example a Script Report that is not standard. Before a run, validate_filters_permissions() checks each Link filter in this table: the user needs read or select permission on the linked document.

docs.title: Script Report without a file
docs.text: A Script Report with is_standard = "No" runs report_script with safe_exec. Only a Script Manager can save it, and server scripts must be on (see Server and Client Scripts). The script gets filters. It sets data (a full result like the return value of execute) or result (rows only, with columns from the columns table).

docs.title: Query Report
docs.text:
A Query Report runs query with the filter values as SQL parameters. Write the column definition as the column alias.

select
    name as "Order:Link/Sample Order:150",
    customer_name as "Customer::150",
    total as "Total:Currency:120"
from `tabSample Order`
where docstatus < 2
    and customer_name like %(customer)s

execute_query_report() checks the query with check_safe_sql_query. Only select and explain queries pass (and with on MariaDB). Queries that read __Auth or write to a file fail. The filters in the JS file (or the filters table) give the values for %(customer)s. The result rows come back as dicts, with fieldname made from the label (order, customer, total).

docs.title: Run a report from code
docs.text:
frappe.desk.query_report.run is the method that the desk calls. It is whitelisted and has @frappe.read_only(), so it reads from the replica when read_from_replica is set.

from frappe.desk.query_report import run

result = run("Sample Order Summary", filters={"status": "Open"})
result["columns"]   # list of column dicts
result["result"]    # list of row dicts, plus a total row (a list) when add_total_row is set

The returned dict has result, columns, message, chart, report_summary, skip_total_row, status, execution_time and add_total_row. For a prepared report, it has prepared_report and doc and the saved result.

curl -b cookies.txt -G "http://<site>/api/method/frappe.desk.query_report.run" \
  --data-urlencode 'report_name=Sample Order Summary' \
  --data-urlencode 'filters={"status": "Open"}'
Parameter Type Default Description report_name str required Name of the Report. filters dict or JSON str None Filter values. ignore_prepared_report bool False Run now, also for a prepared report. custom_columns list None Extra columns from linked DocTypes. is_tree, parent_field bool, str False, None Build the total row for a tree report. are_default_filters bool True Use the saved filters of a Custom Report.

docs.title: Permissions and roles
docs.text:
get_report_doc() checks these before a run:

  1. Report.is_permitted(). The user must have one of the roles in the roles table (or in a Custom Role for the report). An empty table allows all users.
  2. The user has report permission on ref_doctype.
  3. The report is not disabled.

A new report that is not standard gets the permlevel 0 roles of ref_doctype in roles (set_doctype_roles). After the run, get_filtered_data() removes rows with Link values that the user's user permissions do not allow. Still check permissions in execute. Use frappe.get_list, or frappe.only_for("System Manager") for admin reports.

docs.title: Prepared reports
docs.text:
A prepared report runs in a background job and saves the result in a Prepared Report document with a file attachment. Use it for slow reports.

  • Set prepared_report on the Report to always run it in the background.
  • A Script Report that runs for more than 15 seconds turns on prepared_report by itself. Set disable_prepared_report_automation to stop this.
  • The job runs on the long queue. timeout on the Report sets the job timeout. The default is 1500 seconds (REPORT_TIMEOUT).
  • run() returns the last completed result for the same filters and user. Users start a new run with "Generate New Report" (frappe.core.doctype.prepared_report.prepared_report.make_prepared_report).
  • When the job is done, Frappe sends the realtime event report_generated to the user.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not write to the database in execute. With a replica, run() uses the read-only connection.
  • Use the same fieldname in columns and row dicts. Rows with other keys show empty cells.
  • A Query Report cannot skip a condition when a filter is empty. Use a Script Report for optional filters.
  • add_total_row adds a list row at the end of result. Code that reads result must handle it.
  • The report name, the folder name and the JS key must match. The folder name is the scrubbed report name.

docs.title: Jobs, Realtime and Caching
docs.text:
Run background jobs and scheduled tasks, push realtime events and cache data.

Page What it covers Background Jobs Run code outside the web request with frappe.enqueue and frappe.enqueue_doc, on RQ queues served by bench workers. Scheduler Run functions on a schedule with the scheduler_events hook, Scheduled Job Type records and the bench schedule process. Realtime Push events from the server to browsers with publish_realtime, Socket.IO rooms on the Node server, and frappe.realtime.on. Caching Cache data in Redis with frappe.cache, read documents with get_cached_doc and get_cached_value, and use the request_cache, site_cache and redis_cache decorators.

docs.title: Background Jobs
docs.text: Use a background job when work takes longer than a web request should wait: bulk updates, imports, reports, emails, calls to slow external services. Frappe puts the job on a Redis queue (RQ). A worker process (bench worker) takes the job and runs it in a fresh site context. Use frappe.enqueue for a function and frappe.enqueue_doc for a controller method.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
• Queue: a named RQ queue. Frappe has three built-in queues: short, default and long. You can add more in common_site_config.json (see Queues and timeouts).
  • Worker: a process that takes jobs from one or more queues. Start it with bench worker. In production, supervisor or systemd runs the workers (see Deployment).
  • Job ID: every job has an ID. Frappe adds the site name as a prefix, so the ID my_job becomes <site>::my_job. If you do not give an ID, Frappe makes a UUID.
  • RQ Job: a virtual DocType that shows jobs in Redis. Open it at /app/rq-job. It shows the status (queued, started, finished, failed, deferred, scheduled, canceled), arguments, timeout and exception.

docs.title: Enqueue a function
docs.text:
# sample_app/sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def recalculate_rates(category: str):
    frappe.only_for("System Manager")
    frappe.enqueue(
        "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.recalculate_item_rates",
        queue="long",
        timeout=1800,
        category=category,  # passed to the job as a keyword argument
    )

# sample_app/sample_app/jobs.py
import frappe


def recalculate_item_rates(category: str):
    for name in frappe.get_all("Sample Item", {"category": category}, pluck="name"):
        item = frappe.get_doc("Sample Item", name)
        item.rate = item.rate * 1.1
        item.save()

You can pass the dotted path as a string or the function object. All extra keyword arguments go to the function. They must be picklable.

What the worker does for each job (execute_job in frappe/utils/background_jobs.py):

  1. Connects to the site and sets the user to the user who enqueued the job (frappe.session.user at enqueue time).
  2. Sets frappe.job with site, method, job_name, kwargs and user.
  3. Runs every before_job hook.
  4. Runs the function.
  5. Commits the transaction if the function returns. Rolls back, writes an Error Log and raises again if it fails.
  6. Runs every after_job hook.

The job does not check permissions for you. The job runs with the roles of the user who enqueued it, so check permissions in the whitelisted method before you enqueue.

docs.title: Retries on deadlock
docs.text: If the function raises a deadlock, a lock wait timeout, or frappe.RetryBackgroundJobError, the worker rolls back and runs the function again. It tries up to 5 more times and waits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 seconds between attempts. Frappe has no other retry option in frappe.enqueue. A retry does not pass the user again, so it runs as Administrator.

docs.title: Enqueue after commit
docs.text:
When the job reads a document that the current request creates, enqueue it after commit. Otherwise the worker can start before the data is in the database.

def on_submit(self):
    frappe.enqueue(
        "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.notify_order",
        order=self.name,
        enqueue_after_commit=True,
    )

With enqueue_after_commit=True, frappe.enqueue returns None. If the transaction rolls back, the job is not queued.

docs.title: Deduplicate jobs
docs.text:
Give a job_id and set deduplicate=True to skip the call when the same job is queued or running.

frappe.enqueue(
    "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.rebuild_index",
    queue="long",
    job_id="sample_rebuild_index",
    deduplicate=True,
)

If a job with that ID is queued or started, frappe.enqueue writes a log line and returns None. If a finished or failed job with that ID exists, Frappe deletes it and queues a new one. deduplicate=True without job_id raises ValidationError.

Check a job from code:

from frappe.utils.background_jobs import get_job_status, is_job_enqueued

is_job_enqueued("sample_rebuild_index")  # True while queued or started
get_job_status("sample_rebuild_index")   # rq JobStatus, or None if not found

Pass the ID without the site prefix. These functions add it.

docs.title: Run a controller method in the background
docs.text:
frappe.enqueue_doc loads the document in the worker and calls one of its methods.

frappe.enqueue_doc("Sample Order", "SO-0001", "send_reminders", queue="short", timeout=300)

The worker calls frappe.get_doc(doctype, name).<method>(**kwargs). The default timeout of enqueue_doc is 300 seconds.

docs.title: The frappe.task decorator
docs.text:
@frappe.task(...) adds an enqueue attribute to a function. The decorator arguments become frappe.enqueue arguments.

@frappe.task(queue="long", timeout=1800)
def rebuild_index(category=None):
    ...


rebuild_index.enqueue(category="Hardware")

docs.title: Show progress to the user
docs.text: Version 15 has no task DocType for user-facing jobs. To show progress, send realtime events from the job with frappe.publish_progress or frappe.publish_realtime. See Realtime.

docs.title: frappe.enqueue parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Default Description method str or callable required Function to run. queue str "default" Queue name. Must be a known queue, or frappe.enqueue raises ValidationError. timeout int queue timeout Seconds before RQ stops the job. event str None Label stored with the job. Used by bench purge-jobs --event. is_async bool True False runs the job in the current process. Deprecated outside tests, use now. job_name str None Deprecated. Use job_id. now bool False Run the function now with frappe.call, in the current process and transaction. enqueue_after_commit bool False Queue the job only after the current transaction commits. on_success callable None RQ success callback. on_failure callable truncate_failed_registry RQ failure callback. at_front bool False Put the job at the front of the queue. job_id str UUID Job ID. Frappe adds <site>:: before it. deduplicate bool False Do not queue if a job with job_id is queued or started. **kwargs Arguments for the function.

Return value: the rq.job.Job. It is None when the job is deduplicated or queued after commit. With now=True, it is the return value of the function.

docs.title: Queues and timeouts
Workers and CLI
docs.text:
Command Description bench worker Start a worker for all queues. bench worker --queue short,default Start a worker for some queues. Other options: --burst (exit when the queues are empty), --strategy round_robin\|random, --quiet, -u/--rq-username, -p/--rq-password. bench worker-pool --num-workers 4 Start a pool of workers (experimental). The default is 2 workers. bench doctor Show scheduler status and the number of workers online. bench --site <site> show-pending-jobs Show jobs that wait in the queues. bench purge-jobs --site <site> [--queue] [--event] Delete pending jobs.

Workers run with a lower CPU priority than web processes. The default niceness increment is 10. Change it with background_process_niceness in common_site_config.json.

docs.title: Configuration keys
docs.text: Key Default Description workers none Extra queues and their timeouts. common_site_config.json only. max_queued_jobs unset (no limit) Queue size at which frappe.enqueue fails. rq_job_failure_ttl 7 days Seconds to keep failed jobs in Redis. rq_results_ttl 600 Seconds to keep finished job results in Redis. rq_failed_jobs_limit 1000 Maximum number of failed jobs kept per queue. background_process_niceness 10 CPU niceness increment for workers and the scheduler. use_rq_auth, rq_username, rq_password off Connect to the queue Redis with an ACL user.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not pass documents or open files as arguments. Pass names and load the data in the job.
  • A job that runs with now=True shares the caller's transaction. It does not commit.
  • The worker commits only when the job ends. A long loop holds its writes until then. Commit in batches if you must, with frappe.db.commit().
  • Code changes do not reach running workers. Restart the workers after you deploy.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: Use a cache when your code reads the same data many times and the data changes rarely: settings, master records, computed lookups. Frappe has a Redis cache shared by all processes of the bench (frappe.cache), helpers that cache whole documents in it, and decorators that cache function results per request, per process or in Redis. Pick the smallest scope that works, and always plan how the cache gets cleared.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text: Tool Stored in Lives Shared across processes @request_cache frappe.local.request_cache One request or job No @site_cache Process memory Until ttl or clear_cache() No frappe.cache / @redis_cache Redis (redis_cache URL) Until expiry or delete Yes frappe.get_cached_doc / get_cached_value Redis Until the document is saved or deleted, or the cache is cleared Yes

docs.title: frappe.cache
docs.text:
frappe.cache is a RedisWrapper (a subclass of redis.Redis). Values are pickled, so you can store dicts, lists and documents.

frappe.cache.set_value("sample_app:rates", {"Hardware": 10}, expires_in_sec=3600)
rates = frappe.cache.get_value("sample_app:rates")

# compute and store the value when it is missing
rates = frappe.cache.get_value("sample_app:rates", generator=load_rates)

frappe.cache.delete_value("sample_app:rates")
frappe.cache.delete_keys("sample_app:")  # every key that starts with the prefix

Keys are namespaced by site. frappe.cache.make_key("k") returns <db_name>|k. Options on most methods:

  • user=True adds user:<current user>: to the key. Pass a user ID to use another user.
  • shared=True uses the key as given, with no site prefix. All sites on the bench see it.
Method Description set_value(key, val, user=None, expires_in_sec=None, shared=False) Store a value. get_value(key, generator=None, user=None, expires=False, shared=False) Read a value. Calls generator on a miss and stores the result. delete_value(keys, user=None, make_keys=True, shared=False) Delete one key or a list of keys. delete_keys(key) Delete all keys that start with key. get_keys(key) List keys that start with key. exists(*names, user=None, shared=None) Count of keys that exist. hset(name, key, value), hget(name, key, generator=None), hdel(name, key), hgetall(name) Hash operations, with the site prefix. lpush, rpush, lpop, rpop, llen, lrange, ltrim, sadd, srem, smembers List and set operations.

get_value also keeps the value in frappe.local.cache for the rest of the request. A second read in the same request does not go to Redis. Pass expires=True for keys with a TTL so the local copy is not kept.

If Redis is not reachable, set_value and get_value do not raise. get_value returns None, or the generator result.

Note

frappe.cache() (called as a function) still works for backward compatibility. It returns the same object. Use frappe.cache.

docs.title: Cached documents
docs.text:
settings = frappe.get_cached_doc("System Settings")
item = frappe.get_cached_doc("Sample Item", "ITEM-0001")
rate = frappe.get_cached_value("Sample Item", "ITEM-0001", "rate")
values = frappe.get_cached_value("User", "user1@example.com", ["first_name", "user_type"], as_dict=True)
time_zone = frappe.get_single_value("System Settings", "time_zone")
  • get_cached_doc takes the same arguments as frappe.get_doc. It stores the document in Redis under document_cache::<doctype>::<name>, with no expiry.
  • Saving or deleting the document clears its cache entry (Document.clear_cache). The entry is cleared again after commit and after rollback.
  • Clear it yourself with frappe.clear_document_cache(doctype, name). Without name, it clears all cached documents of the DocType.
  • get_cached_value returns None if the document does not exist.
  • frappe.get_single_value(doctype, fieldname) reads a field of a Single DocType through get_cached_value.
  • These functions do not check permissions.

Warning

frappe.db.set_value and frappe.db.set_single_value clear the document cache. Raw SQL (frappe.db.sql) and frappe.qb updates do not. After such writes, call frappe.clear_document_cache.

docs.title: Decorators
docs.text: All three are in frappe.utils.caching. frappe.request_cache is an alias. There is no frappe.site_cache alias in v15. Import site_cache from frappe.utils.caching.

docs.title: request_cache
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.caching import request_cache


@request_cache
def get_item_rate(item: str) -> float:
    return frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", item, "rate")

Calls with the same arguments in one request or job run once. Arguments must be hashable. Unhashable arguments skip the cache.

docs.title: site_cache
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.caching import site_cache


@site_cache(ttl=300, maxsize=128)
def get_category_map() -> dict:
    return dict(frappe.get_all("Sample Item", fields=["name", "category"], as_list=True))


get_category_map.clear_cache()  # clear for all sites in this process

The key is the JSON of the arguments, so the arguments must be JSON serializable. Each site has its own results. The cache is per process: each web worker and background worker has its own copy, and clear_cache() only clears the current process. ttl is one timer for the whole function: when it ends, all results of the function are cleared. frappe.clear_cache() clears all site_cache entries in the current process. When maxsize is reached, the oldest entry is removed.

docs.title: redis_cache
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.caching import redis_cache


@redis_cache(ttl=600)
def get_open_order_count(customer: str) -> int:
    return frappe.db.count("Sample Order", {"customer_name": customer, "status": "Open"})


get_open_order_count.clear_cache()
Argument Default Description ttl 3600 Seconds to keep each result. user None True caches one result for each session user. shared False True shares the results across sites.

The cache key is <module>.<function>::<hash of arguments>. clear_cache() deletes every result of the function. A None result is cached too.

docs.title: Clear the cache
docs.text:
bench --site frappe.localhost clear-cache
bench --site frappe.localhost clear-website-cache

frappe.clear_cache()                       # all site keys and site_cache
frappe.clear_cache(doctype="Sample Item")  # DocType meta and related caches
frappe.clear_cache(user="user1@example.com")  # user caches (roles, permissions, defaults)

A full frappe.clear_cache() deletes all Redis keys of the site except keys that match the persistent_cache_keys hook. Then it runs every clear_cache hook.

# sample_app/hooks.py
persistent_cache_keys = ["sample_app:rates*"]  # kept by frappe.clear_cache()
clear_cache = "sample_app.cache.clear_sample_cache"  # called by frappe.clear_cache()

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Never cache data that depends on permissions in a key that other users can read. Use user=True.
  • Changes from site_cache do not reach other processes. Do not use it for data that users edit.
  • Cached documents are copies. Changing a cached document does not change the database. Use frappe.get_doc when you will save.
  • Cached documents have no expiry. A write that bypasses the document API leaves an old copy until you clear it.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Performance
  • Database
  • Configuration
  • Hooks reference

docs.title: Realtime
docs.text: Use realtime events to push data from the server to open browser tabs: a progress bar, a refresh after a background job, a message to one user. Server code calls frappe.publish_realtime. Frappe publishes the event on the Redis channel events. The Node Socket.IO server reads the channel and sends the event to the browsers in the target room. Browser code listens with frappe.realtime.on.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
• Event: a name, such as doc_update or sample_order_ready, and a JSON message.
  • Room: a group of sockets on one site. Each site is a Socket.IO namespace (/<site>).
  • Socket.IO server: a separate Node process, apps/frappe/socketio.js. bench socketio starts it. It listens on socketio_port (default 9000). It reads the events channel from the redis_queue Redis.

Version

v15 has only the Node server. It has no Python Socket.IO server and no custom handlers in Python apps.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: On connect, the server calls frappe.realtime.get_user_info on the web server with the sid cookie or the Authorization header. The host and origin of the request must match. The socket gets user and user_type from the answer.

docs.title: Rooms
docs.text:
Room Who is in it How a socket joins user:<user> All sockets of that user on the site On connect website All sockets on the site, guests too On connect all Sockets of System Users on the site On connect doctype:<doctype> Sockets that show a list of that DocType doctype_subscribe, needs read permission doc:<doctype>/<name> Sockets that have the form open doc_subscribe, needs read permission open_doc:<doctype>/<name> Sockets that view the form now. Used for doc_viewers. doc_open, needs read permission task_progress:<task_id> Sockets that follow a task task_subscribe or progress_subscribe

The desk subscribes for you. A form subscribes to its document on load. A list view subscribes to its DocType. The server checks permission with the whitelisted methods frappe.realtime.can_subscribe_doc and frappe.realtime.can_subscribe_doctype.

docs.title: Publish from the server
docs.text:
frappe.publish_realtime(
    event="sample_order_ready",
    message={"order": "SO-0001", "status": "Ready"},
    user="user1@example.com",
    after_commit=True,
)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Default Description event str "task_progress" if a task ID is set, else "global" Event name. message dict {} JSON message. room str see below Room name. Overrides the other targets. user str None Send to the room user:<user>. doctype, docname str None Send to the room doc:<doctype>/<docname>. task_id str frappe.local.task_id Send to the room task_progress:<task_id>. Forces after_commit=False. after_commit bool False Send only after the transaction commits. Dropped on rollback. Duplicate events are sent once.

When room is not given, the first match wins: task_id, then user, then doctype and docname. If none is given, the event goes to the all room (System Users of the site).

Special cases:

  • msgprint without user goes to the current user.
  • list_update always goes to doctype:<doctype>. The DocType comes from doctype or from message["doctype"].
  • docinfo_update always goes to doc:<doctype>/<docname>.

Use after_commit=True when the browser reloads data after the event. Otherwise the browser can read the database before your changes are committed.

frappe/realtime.py also has room name helpers: get_user_room(user), get_doc_room(doctype, docname), get_doctype_room(doctype), get_site_room(), get_website_room() and get_task_progress_room(task_id). Use them with room=:

from frappe.realtime import get_website_room

frappe.publish_realtime("sample_banner", {"text": "Closed today"}, room=get_website_room())

docs.title: Progress bar
docs.text:
frappe.publish_progress sends the progress event. The desk shows a progress dialog.

def import_items(rows):
    for i, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
        ...
        frappe.publish_progress(i * 100 / len(rows), title="Importing items", description=f"Row {i}")

Signature: publish_progress(percent, title=None, doctype=None, docname=None, description=None, task_id=None). With doctype and docname, everyone with the form open sees the progress. Without them, only the current user sees it.

docs.title: Events the framework sends
docs.text:
Event Room When Message doc_update doc:<doctype>/<name> After a document is saved (notify_update), after commit doctype, name, modified list_update doctype:<doctype> Same, for DocTypes that are not single, child or read-only doctype, name, user docinfo_update doc:<doctype>/<name> A Comment or Communication on the document changes varies doc_viewers open_doc:<doctype>/<name> A user opens or closes the form doctype, docname, users msgprint user:<user> frappe.msgprint(..., realtime=True) message progress user or doc room frappe.publish_progress percent, title, description

notify_update does not send events while patches run (frappe.flags.in_patch). Set doc.flags.notify_update = False to skip it for one save. doc.db_set(..., notify=True) also calls it.

docs.title: From the CLI
docs.text:
bench --site frappe.localhost publish-realtime sample_event --message '{"status": "Open"}' --user Administrator

Options: --message, --room, --user, --doctype, --docname, --after-commit. The message is sent as a string, not as an object.

docs.title: Listen in the browser
docs.text:
// sample_app/public/js/sample_order.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    refresh(frm) {
        frappe.realtime.off("sample_order_ready");
        frappe.realtime.on("sample_order_ready", (data) => {
            if (data.order === frm.doc.name) {
                frm.reload_doc();
            }
        });
    },
});

Client API (frappe.realtime, also frappe.socketio):

Method Description on(event, callback) Listen for an event. Does nothing if the socket was not created. off(event, callback) Stop listening. Without callback, removes all listeners for the event. emit(event, ...args) Send an event to the server. publish(event, message) Same as emit with one argument. doctype_subscribe(doctype) / doctype_unsubscribe(doctype) Join or leave doctype:<doctype>. doc_subscribe(doctype, name) / doc_unsubscribe(doctype, name) Join or leave doc:<doctype>/<name>. Throttled to one call each second. task_subscribe(task_id) / task_unsubscribe(task_id) Join or leave task_progress:<task_id>.

The client tries to reconnect 3 times. If disable_async is set in site config, the client does not connect.

The Node server accepts only the subscribe events in the table above, plus ping and open_in_editor. An app cannot add its own server-side handlers in v15. To reach a group of users, publish to a user, document or DocType room from Python.

docs.title: Configuration keys
docs.text:
Key File Default Description socketio_port common_site_config.json 9000 Port of the Socket.IO server. Also sent to the desk in boot. socketio_uds common_site_config.json none Listen on this Unix socket instead of the port. redis_queue common_site_config.json none Redis that carries the events channel. webserver_host, webserver_port common_site_config.json none Where the Socket.IO server sends permission checks. Without them, it uses the request origin. disable_async site unset Turn off the realtime client in the desk.

Environment variables FRAPPE_SOCKETIO_PORT, FRAPPE_SOCKETIO_UDS, FRAPPE_REDIS_QUEUE and FRAPPE_BENCH_ROOT override the files.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Events are not stored. A browser that is not connected when you publish misses the event.
  • A user sees events in user:<user> and all without a permission check. Do not put data there that the user must not read.
  • publish_realtime does nothing if Redis is down. It does not raise.
  • In a background job, publish after your writes commit, or use after_commit=True.

docs.title: Scheduler
docs.text: Use the scheduler to run a function at fixed times: each few minutes, hourly, daily, or on a cron expression. You declare the function in the scheduler_events hook of your app. Frappe stores each entry as a Scheduled Job Type record. The bench schedule process checks these records and puts due jobs on a background queue. A worker then runs them.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. bench migrate (and app install) reads scheduler_events from every installed app. It creates or updates one Scheduled Job Type per method, and deletes records whose method is no longer in the hooks.
  2. The bench schedule process wakes up each 60 seconds by default (scheduler_tick_interval).
  3. For each site, it skips the site if the scheduler is inactive (see Enable and disable).
  4. For each Scheduled Job Type that is not stopped, it computes the next run from last_execution and the frequency. If the run is due, it enqueues the job.
  5. The job ID is scheduled_job::<method>. A job that is still queued or running is not queued again.
  6. The worker runs the method, commits, and writes a Scheduled Job Log row (Start, Complete or Failed).

The scheduler only queues jobs. If no worker runs, no scheduled job runs.

docs.title: Declare scheduled events
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
scheduler_events = {
    "all": [
        "sample_app.tasks.sync_stock",
    ],
    "hourly": [
        "sample_app.tasks.send_reminders",
    ],
    "daily": [
        "sample_app.tasks.close_old_orders",
    ],
    "daily_long": [
        "sample_app.tasks.rebuild_rates",
    ],
    "weekly": [],
    "monthly": [],
    "cron": {
        "*/15 * * * *": ["sample_app.tasks.poll_service"],
        "30 2 * * 1-5": ["sample_app.tasks.weekday_report"],
    },
}

# sample_app/tasks.py
import frappe


def close_old_orders():
    for name in frappe.get_all("Sample Order", {"status": "Open", "docstatus": 0}, pluck="name"):
        frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name).add_comment("Comment", "Checked by scheduler")

The method takes no arguments. It runs as the user Administrator, the user that the scheduler process uses when it enqueues. Run bench migrate after you change scheduler_events. If the method path cannot be imported, migrate prints a warning and skips it.

docs.title: Event keys
docs.text:
The key in scheduler_events sets the frequency of the Scheduled Job Type. Frappe converts daily_long to Daily Long.

Key Frequency Runs Queue all All Each scheduler_interval seconds (default 240, so each 4 minutes) default hourly Hourly At minute 0 of each hour default hourly_long Hourly Long At minute 0 of each hour long hourly_maintenance Hourly Maintenance At minute 0 of each hour long daily Daily At 00:00 default daily_long Daily Long At 00:00 long daily_maintenance Daily Maintenance At 00:00 long weekly Weekly Sunday 00:00 default weekly_long Weekly Long Sunday 00:00 long monthly Monthly 1st day of the month, 00:00 default monthly_long Monthly Long 1st day of the month, 00:00 long yearly, annual Yearly, Annual 1 January, 00:00 default cron Cron The cron expression (dict key) default

Times are in the system time zone of the site. Use a _long or _maintenance key for slow work, so it does not hold up the default queue. A Cron job always goes to the default queue.

Note

get_next_execution computes a per-site minute offset for the _maintenance frequencies, but it does not apply it. In v15, maintenance jobs run at minute 0, the same as hourly_long and daily_long.

Cron expressions use the croniter syntax. An invalid expression fails validation on save with "Bad Cron Expression".

docs.title: Scheduled Job Type
docs.text:
Open the list at /app/scheduled-job-type. The record name is the last two parts of the method path, for example tasks.close_old_orders. Fields:

Field Description method Dotted path of the function. frequency See the table above. cron_format Cron expression. Required for Cron. stopped Check to stop this job. Migrate keeps this value. create_log Write a Scheduled Job Log for each run. Always on for frequencies other than All. last_execution Time of the last run. The next run is computed from it. next_execution Read only. The next run time. server_script Set for jobs that come from a Server Script of type Scheduler Event. scheduler_event Link to a Scheduler Event record. Migrate does not delete jobs that have it.

The form has an Execute action (System Manager only). It queues the job now through execute_event.

Run a job now from the CLI. This runs it in the current process, not in a worker:

bench --site frappe.localhost trigger-scheduler-event sample_app.tasks.close_old_orders

docs.title: Enable and disable
docs.text:
The scheduler is inactive for a site when one of these is true:

  • maintenance_mode is set in site config.
  • pause_scheduler is set in site config.
  • disable_scheduler is set in site config.
  • System Settings > Enable Scheduled Jobs (enable_scheduler) is off.
Command Effect bench --site <site> enable-scheduler Sets enable_scheduler = 1 in System Settings. bench --site <site> disable-scheduler Sets enable_scheduler = 0. bench --site <site> scheduler enable\|disable Same as the two commands above. bench --site <site> scheduler pause\|resume Sets or clears pause_scheduler in site_config.json. bench --site <site> scheduler status [-f json] Prints enabled or disabled. bench --site <site> set-maintenance-mode on\|off Sets maintenance_mode. Scheduled jobs do not run in maintenance mode. bench schedule Starts the scheduler process for all sites of the bench. bench doctor Shows scheduler status per site and workers online.

The whitelisted method frappe.utils.scheduler.activate_scheduler (Administrator only) enables the scheduler and clears pause_scheduler. It fails in maintenance mode.

Note

On Frappe Cloud, a site with no user activity for dormant_days (System Settings, "Run Jobs only Daily if Inactive For (Days)") runs scheduled jobs only once each 24 hours. This check is off in developer mode and on other hosts.

docs.title: Configuration keys
docs.text: Key File Default Description scheduler_tick_interval common_site_config.json 60 Seconds between scheduler checks. scheduler_interval site or common 240 Interval of all events, in seconds. Converted to whole minutes. pause_scheduler site unset Pause scheduling for the site. disable_scheduler site unset Disable scheduling for the site. maintenance_mode site unset Stops the scheduler and blocks writes.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A job that is still running when its next run is due is skipped, not queued twice.
  • Long jobs on default hold up short ones. Use a _long key. A Cron job cannot choose its queue in v15.
  • trigger-scheduler-event runs in your shell, but it catches errors. Look for the traceback in the Scheduled Job Log row with status Failed.

docs.title: Permissions and Security
docs.text:
Control access with permissions, authenticate clients and write secure code.

Page What it covers Permissions How the permission engine decides access from role permissions, permission levels, user permissions, sharing and app hooks, and how to check permissions in code. Authentication Authenticate HTTP requests with a session cookie, API key and secret, or an OAuth 2 bearer token, and how CSRF, two-factor login, guests and auth hooks work. Security Write secure Frappe app code - permission checks in whitelisted methods, safe SQL, escaping, private files, rate limits, CSRF, secrets and the risks of ignore_permissions.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Each request to a Frappe site runs as one user. frappe.session.user is that user, or Guest if the request is not authenticated. Frappe sets the user from one of these, in frappe/auth.py:

Method Header or cookie Use it for Session sid cookie Browsers, the desk and portal pages API key and secret Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret> Server-to-server scripts and integrations OAuth 2 Authorization: Bearer <access_token> Third-party apps that act for a user Auth hooks anything Custom schemes in your app

All requests on this page were sent with curl to http://frappe.localhost:8001.

docs.title: Session login
docs.text:
curl -s -c cookies.txt -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"usr": "user1@example.com", "pwd": "Sample-Pass-123!"}'

{"message": "Logged In", "home_page": "/app", "full_name": "User 1"}

The response sets the sid cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) and the cookies system_user, full_name, user_id and user_image. Send the cookie with later requests:

curl -s -b cookies.txt "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

usr is the email. It can also be the user name or the mobile number when System Settings allow_login_using_user_name or allow_login_using_mobile_number is set. Log out with POST /api/method/logout.

Failed logins return HTTP 401 and are written to the Activity Log. Repeated failures lock the user and the IP for a time (LoginAttemptTracker in frappe/auth.py). The login also checks the IP allowlist of the user (restrict_ip) and the login hours (login_after, login_before).

After the password check, the login runs the on_login hooks. Logout runs on_logout. Each handler gets login_manager. v15 has no before_login hook. If System Settings disable_user_pass_login is on, password login raises frappe.AuthenticationError. See Hooks.

docs.title: CSRF
docs.text:
For a cookie session, POST, PUT, DELETE and PATCH requests must send the CSRF token of the session in the X-Frappe-CSRF-Token header (or as csrf_token in the form). Otherwise the request fails with frappe.CSRFTokenError (HTTP 400):

{"exception": "frappe.exceptions.CSRFTokenError: Invalid Request", "exc_type": "CSRFTokenError"}
  • The desk gets the token in frappe.csrf_token and frappe.call sends it for you.
  • A session gets a token the first time it is needed (frappe.sessions.get_csrf_token). A session that has no token yet is not checked.
  • Requests with token or bearer authentication have no session token, so the check does not apply.
  • The site config key ignore_csrf turns the check off for the site.

docs.title: Generate keys
docs.text:
A System Manager generates the keys for a user:

  1. Open the User in the desk.
  2. Open the API Access section.
  3. Click Generate Keys.
  4. Copy the API Secret from the dialog. It is shown only once.

From code or the API, call frappe.core.doctype.user.user.generate_keys. It requires the System Manager role and POST:

curl -s -b admin_cookies.txt -X POST \
  "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.core.doctype.user.user.generate_keys" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"user": "user1@example.com"}'

{"message": {"api_key": "1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8", "api_secret": "9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2"}}

The API key is created once and does not change. Each call makes a new secret and the old secret stops working. The secret is stored encrypted in the api_secret Password field of the User.

docs.title: Use the keys
docs.text:
curl -s "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" \
  -H "Authorization: token 1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8:9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

HTTP Basic with base64(api_key:api_secret) also works. Frappe reads every Basic header as an API key pair:

curl -s "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" \
  -H "Authorization: Basic $(printf '1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8:9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2' | base64)"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

A wrong key or secret returns HTTP 401 with "exc_type": "AuthenticationError". The failure is written to the Activity Log, at most once per interval for each user.

  • The request runs with the roles and permissions of that user. There is no separate scope.
  • The user must be enabled.
  • The restrict_ip allowlist of the user also applies (validate_ip_address).
  • No session is created and no cookie is set.
  • Two-factor authentication does not apply to token requests.

The header Frappe-Authorization-Source: <DocType> makes Frappe look up the key in another DocType instead of User. That DocType needs the fields api_key, api_secret, enabled and user. The request then runs as the value of user.

docs.title: OAuth 2
docs.text:
Frappe is an OAuth 2 and OpenID Connect provider. A third-party app gets an access token for a user and sends it as a bearer token. Set up the provider and clients in the desk. See Integrations.

Endpoint Path Authorization /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.authorize Token /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token Revocation /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.revoke_token Introspection /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.introspect_token User info (OpenID) /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.openid_profile

The functions are in frappe/integrations/oauth2.py. openid_configuration returns the OpenID discovery document.

docs.title: Authorization code flow
docs.text:
The example uses an OAuth Client with client_id <client_id>, scopes all openid, redirect URI http://localhost:9999/callback, grant type Authorization Code, response type Code and Skip Authorization on.

  1. Send the user to the authorization endpoint. A guest is redirected to /login first.

    curl -s -i -b user_cookies.txt -G "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.authorize" \
  --data-urlencode client_id=<client_id> --data-urlencode response_type=code \
  --data-urlencode scope=all --data-urlencode redirect_uri=http://localhost:9999/callback \
  --data-urlencode state=xyz

    HTTP/1.1 302 FOUND
Location: http://localhost:9999/callback?code=<authorization_code>&state=xyz

    The user sees a Confirm Access page first, unless the client has Skip Authorization set.

  2. Exchange the code for tokens. Send client_id in the form body. Do not use HTTP Basic (curl -u): Frappe reads a Basic header as an API key pair and returns HTTP 401.

    curl -s -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token" \
  -d client_id=<client_id> -d client_secret=<client_secret> \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code -d code=<authorization_code> \
  -d redirect_uri=http://localhost:9999/callback

    {"access_token": "<access_token>", "expires_in": 3600, "token_type": "Bearer",
 "scope": "all", "refresh_token": "<refresh_token>"}

  3. Call the API with the access token.

    curl -s "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

  4. When the token expires, get a new one with the refresh token. In v15 the old access token keeps working until it expires or is revoked.

    curl -s -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token" \
  -d client_id=<client_id> -d grant_type=refresh_token -d refresh_token=<refresh_token>

    {"access_token": "<new_access_token>", "expires_in": 3600, "token_type": "Bearer",
 "scope": "all", "refresh_token": "<new_refresh_token>"}

  5. To end access, revoke the token. The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with {}.

    curl -s -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.revoke_token" \
  -d token=<new_access_token>

Warning

In v15 the token endpoint finds the client by client_id only (OAuthWebRequestValidator.authenticate_client in frappe/oauth.py). It does not check client_secret. Keep authorization codes and redirect URIs private.

Tokens are stored as OAuth Bearer Token documents. The document name is the access token itself, so treat read access to that DocType as access to the tokens. An unknown, expired or revoked token returns HTTP 401. The request runs with the roles of the user who approved the token.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
When 2FA applies to a user (System Settings enable_two_factor_auth and a role with Two Factor Authentication set), POST /api/method/login does not log in at once:

  1. The first login request checks the password. The response has tmp_id and a verification object with the method (OTP App, Email or SMS). The user is still Guest.
  2. Send the code: POST /api/method/login with tmp_id and otp. On success the session is created.

The tmp_id expires after 300 seconds for SMS and Email, and after 180 seconds for an OTP App that is set up. The logic is in frappe/twofactor.py.

docs.title: Guests
docs.text:
A request without credentials runs as Guest. The only role of Guest is Guest.

  • A guest can call only methods with @frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True). Other methods return HTTP 403 with "Function ... is not whitelisted".
  • A guest can read documents only through permissions given to the Guest role.
  • Guest string arguments are sanitized for HTML unless the method sets xss_safe=True.

See Whitelisted methods.

docs.title: Custom authentication
docs.text:
The auth_hooks hook lists functions that run on every request after the built-in checks. A function can call frappe.set_user(user) to authenticate the request.

# sample_app/hooks.py
auth_hooks = ["sample_app.auth.validate_sample_header"]

# sample_app/auth.py
import frappe


def validate_sample_header():
    token = frappe.get_request_header("X-Sample-Token")
    if not token:
        return
    user = frappe.db.get_value("Sample Device", {"token": token, "enabled": 1}, "user")
    if user:
        frappe.set_user(user)

If a request has an Authorization header with two parts and no method sets a user, Frappe raises frappe.AuthenticationError (HTTP 401).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• An API secret gives full access as that user. Create a separate user with only the roles the integration needs.
  • generate_keys replaces the secret. Integrations that use the old secret stop working.
  • Do not send API keys in URLs. Use the Authorization header.
  • A cookie session that calls POST from a script must send X-Frappe-CSRF-Token.
  • Use the OAuth token endpoint without curl -u. An Authorization: Basic header is read as an API key pair.

docs.text:

  • Whitelisted methods
