docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Use this page to set up a local development environment for Frappe v15 (branch version-15). You install the bench CLI, create a bench folder that holds Frappe, create a site, and start the processes. For production servers, see Deployment.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Software Version Source of the requirement Python 3.10 to 3.14 (>=3.10,<3.15) requires-python in pyproject.toml Node.js 18 or newer engines.node in package.json Yarn any current version bench runs yarn install for app assets (yarn.lock) MariaDB 10.6 to 10.8 check_compatible_versions() in frappe/database/mariadb/setup_db.py warns outside this range PostgreSQL limited support bench new-site --db-type postgres Redis a current Redis server Used for cache, job queue and realtime events Git any current version bench new-app makes a Git repository for the new app bench CLI the frappe-bench package Creates benches, gets apps and runs processes

MariaDB is the default database. For PostgreSQL, bench new-site prints a note that PostgreSQL support is limited to Frappe v16 and above, and that fixes for earlier versions are not added.

docs.title: Install the bench CLI
docs.text:
1. Install the frappe-bench package as a tool:

    uv tool install frappe-bench

  2. Make sure the command works:

    bench --version

docs.title: Create a bench
docs.text:
A bench is a folder that holds the apps, a Python virtual environment (env/), the sites (sites/), the Redis configuration (config/) and a Procfile.

  1. Create the bench with the version-15 branch of Frappe:

    bench init frappe-bench --frappe-branch version-15 --python python3.12

  2. Go into the bench folder:

    cd frappe-bench

Useful bench init options:

Option Description --frappe-branch (alias --version) Branch of Frappe to clone. --python Path to the Python executable for env/. --frappe-path Clone Frappe from this path or URL. --skip-assets Do not build JS and CSS assets. --no-procfile Do not make a Procfile. --dev Turn on developer mode and install development dependencies.

docs.title: Create a site
docs.text:
A site is one database plus one folder in sites/. One bench can serve many sites.

  1. Create the site. Give the MariaDB root password and a password for Administrator:

    bench new-site sample.localhost --db-root-password <root-password> --admin-password <admin-password>

  2. Make the new site the default site of the bench:

    bench use sample.localhost

  3. If you develop apps on this site, turn on developer mode:

    bench --site sample.localhost set-config developer_mode 1

Common bench new-site options:

Option Default Description --db-type mariadb mariadb or postgres. --db-name generated Database name. --db-password generated Password of the site database user. --db-host, --db-port from config Database server address. --db-socket MYSQL_UNIX_PORT env var Database socket. --db-root-username (alias --mariadb-root-username) root Root user that makes the database and the user. --db-root-password (alias --mariadb-root-password) prompt Root password for MariaDB or PostgreSQL. --admin-password prompt Password of the Administrator user. --install-app none App to install after the site is made. Use more than once for more apps. --set-default off Make the site the default site. --source-sql none Start the database from an SQL file. --force off Replace a site or database that already exists. --setup-db/--no-setup-db --setup-db With --no-setup-db, do not create the database user and database. Only bootstrap.

docs.title: Start the bench
docs.text:
1. Start all processes from the Procfile:

    bench start

  2. Open http://sample.localhost:8000 in the browser.

  3. Log in as Administrator with the admin password.

The desk opens at /app. The route /desk redirects to /app (website_redirects in frappe/hooks.py).

Version

In Frappe v16, the desk moved to /desk.

bench start runs these processes:

Process Command Purpose redis_cache redis-server config/redis_cache.conf Cache (redis_cache in common_site_config.json). redis_queue redis-server config/redis_queue.conf Job queue and realtime pub/sub (redis_queue). web bench serve --port 8000 Python web server for all sites. socketio bench socketio Realtime (Socket.IO) server on Node.js. watch bench watch Rebuilds JS and CSS when files change. schedule bench schedule Scheduler that enqueues scheduled jobs. worker bench worker Background job worker.

The site is found from the Host header of the request. A name that ends in .localhost points to your computer in most browsers. For other names, run bench --site <site> add-to-hosts.

The realtime server is the Node.js server in realtime/index.js (started from socketio.js). It listens on socketio_port (default 9000, set in node_utils.js).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Python 3.9 and older do not work. pyproject.toml requires Python 3.10 or newer.
  • A MariaDB version below 10.6 or 10.9 and newer shows a warning during bench new-site. The site can still be made, but the version is not tested.
  • bench new-site prompts for passwords when you do not give them. Give --db-root-password and --admin-password in scripts.
  • Without developer_mode, you cannot make a standard (non-custom) DocType. You get the error "Not in Developer Mode".
  • Do not name a site the same as an app in the bench. bench new-site stops with an error.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This page builds a small app, sample_app, with one DocType, Sample Item. You add a server validation, a whitelisted method, a form button, a list indicator and a test. Before you start, set up a bench and a site as shown in Installation. The examples use the site sample.localhost.

docs.title: 1. Create the app
docs.text:
1. In the bench folder, create the app:

    bench new-app sample_app

  2. Answer the prompts:

    Prompt Default Note App Title Sample App Also the name of the first module. Must start with a letter. App Description none App Publisher none App Email none Must be a valid email address. App License mit Create GitHub Workflow action for unittests False Adds .github/workflows/ci.yml and linter.yml.

bench new-app runs bench make-app apps sample_app. Then it installs the app into the bench Python environment and adds it to sites/apps.txt. Use --no-git to skip the Git repository.

The new app has this layout:

apps/sample_app/
├── .editorconfig
├── .eslintrc
├── .gitignore
├── .pre-commit-config.yaml
├── README.md
├── license.txt
├── pyproject.toml
└── sample_app/
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── hooks.py
    ├── modules.txt          # "Sample App"
    ├── patches.txt
    ├── config/
    ├── patches/
    ├── public/
    │   ├── css/
    │   └── js/
    ├── templates/
    │   ├── includes/
    │   └── pages/
    ├── www/
    └── sample_app/          # module "Sample App"
        └── __init__.py

The generated hooks.py has most hooks as comments. To let Frappe write field type hints into your controllers, remove the # from this line:

# sample_app/hooks.py
export_python_type_annotations = True

docs.title: 2. Install the app on the site
docs.text:
1. Install the app:

    bench --site sample.localhost install-app sample_app

  2. Turn on developer mode, so that DocTypes you make are saved as files in the app:

    bench --site sample.localhost set-config developer_mode 1

  3. Start the bench:

    bench start

docs.title: 3. Create the DocType
docs.text:
1. Open http://sample.localhost:8000/app/doctype/new.
  2. Set Name to Sample Item.
  3. Set Module to Sample App.
  4. Leave Custom? cleared.

  5. Add these fields:

    Label Fieldname Type Options Mandatory Item Name item_name Data Yes Category category Select Hardware, Software, Service (one per line) Yes Rate rate Currency No Disabled disabled Check No Description description Text Editor No

  6. In Naming, set Auto Name to field:item_name.

  7. In Permissions, keep the row for System Manager.
  8. Save.

Frappe makes the table tabSample Item and writes these files to apps/sample_app/sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/:

File Content sample_item.json DocType definition. sample_item.py Python controller. sample_item.js Form script. test_sample_item.py Test class. __init__.py Package marker.

docs.title: 4. Add a validation and a whitelisted method
docs.text:
Edit the controller. If you turned on export_python_type_annotations, the file has a block between # begin: auto-generated types and # end: auto-generated types. Keep that block as it is. Frappe rewrites it when you save the DocType.

# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/sample_item.py
import frappe
from frappe import _
from frappe.model.document import Document
from frappe.utils import flt


class SampleItem(Document):
    def validate(self):
        if flt(self.rate) <= 0:
            frappe.throw(_("Rate must be greater than zero."), title=_("Invalid Rate"))


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_items_by_category(category: str) -> list[dict]:
    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Item",
        filters={"category": category, "disabled": 0},
        fields=["name", "item_name", "rate"],
        order_by="rate desc",
    )
  • validate() runs before each insert and save. frappe.throw() raises frappe.ValidationError and stops the save.
  • get_items_by_category() is callable at /api/method/sample_app.sample_app.doctype.sample_item.sample_item.get_items_by_category.
  • frappe.get_list() applies the read permissions of the current user.
  • In a request, Frappe checks the arguments against the type annotations (frappe/utils/typing_validations.py).

Test the method with curl. Log in first and keep the session cookie in the file jar:

curl -c jar -X POST http://sample.localhost:8000/api/method/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"usr":"Administrator","pwd":"<admin-password>"}'
curl -b jar "http://sample.localhost:8000/api/method/sample_app.sample_app.doctype.sample_item.sample_item.get_items_by_category?category=Hardware"

The response has this shape:

{"message": [{"name": "Laptop", "item_name": "Laptop", "rate": 900.0}]}

docs.title: 5. Add a form script
docs.text:
The form script runs in the desk when a Sample Item form opens.

// sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/sample_item.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Item", {
    refresh(frm) {
        if (frm.is_new()) return;

        frm.add_custom_button(__("Same Category"), () => {
            frappe.call({
                method: "sample_app.sample_app.doctype.sample_item.sample_item.get_items_by_category",
                args: { category: frm.doc.category },
                callback(r) {
                    frappe.msgprint(r.message.map((d) => d.item_name).join(", "));
                },
            });
        });
    },
});

After you change JS files, reload the page. bench watch (part of bench start) rebuilds the assets.

docs.title: 6. Add a list view setting
docs.text:
Make a file <doctype>_list.js next to the controller. The desk loads it for the list view. Frappe does not make this file for you.

// sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/sample_item_list.js
frappe.listview_settings["Sample Item"] = {
    add_fields: ["disabled"],
    get_indicator(doc) {
        if (doc.disabled) {
            return [__("Disabled"), "gray", "disabled,=,1"];
        }
        return [__("Enabled"), "green", "disabled,=,0"];
    },
};

get_indicator returns [label, color, filter]. A click on the indicator applies the filter. Open /app/sample-item to see the list.

docs.title: 7. Write a test
docs.text:
Edit the generated test file:

# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/test_sample_item.py
import frappe
from frappe.tests.utils import FrappeTestCase


class TestSampleItem(FrappeTestCase):
    def test_rate_must_be_positive(self):
        doc = frappe.get_doc(
            {"doctype": "Sample Item", "item_name": "Test Item", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 0}
        )
        self.assertRaises(frappe.ValidationError, doc.insert)

    def test_get_items_by_category(self):
        from sample_app.sample_app.doctype.sample_item.sample_item import get_items_by_category

        frappe.get_doc(
            {"doctype": "Sample Item", "item_name": "Test Mouse", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 20}
        ).insert()
        names = [d.name for d in get_items_by_category("Hardware")]
        self.assertIn("Test Mouse", names)

  1. Allow tests on the site:

    bench --site sample.localhost set-config allow_tests true

  2. Run the tests of the DocType:

    bench --site sample.localhost run-tests --doctype "Sample Item"

FrappeTestCase (frappe/tests/utils.py) commits before the class starts and rolls back the database changes of the test class when the class is done.

docs.title: 8. Install the app on another site
docs.text:
1. Commit the app code to Git.
  2. On the other bench, get the app with bench get-app <git-url>.

  3. Install the app:

    bench --site <site> install-app sample_app

install-app makes the tables of all DocTypes in the app and runs the after_install hooks. After you pull new code, run bench --site <site> migrate.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Without developer_mode, saving a DocType with Custom? cleared fails with "Not in Developer Mode".
  • The dotted path of a DocType module repeats the app name: sample_app.sample_app.doctype.... The first part is the app package. The second part is the module folder.
  • Without allow_tests in the site config (or the CI environment variable), run-tests stops and prints the command to set it.
  • Do not edit the DocType JSON by hand. Change it in the desk, so Frappe updates the JSON and the table together.

docs.title: Database API
docs.text:
frappe.db is the database connection of the current site. It is an instance of MariaDBDatabase or PostgresDatabase. Both extend Database in frappe/database/database.py. Use this page to find a method and its exact signature. For usage, filters and transactions, see Database.

The signatures come from inspect.signature on a v15 site (MariaDB 10.6). Internal helpers are left out. frappe.db.db_type returns "mariadb" or "postgres". The db_type key in site config selects the class. Any value other than postgres gives MariaDB. The MariaDB class uses the PyMySQL driver, so database errors are pymysql.err classes.

Note

Methods on this page do not check permissions, unless the description says so. set_value, delete and sql do not run controller hooks.

docs.title: Read values
docs.text: Method Signature Description get_value (doctype, filters=None, fieldname='name', ignore=None, as_dict=False, debug=False, order_by='KEEP_DEFAULT_ORDERING', cache=False, for_update=False, *, run=True, pluck=False, distinct=False, skip_locked=False, wait=True) Return one value, or a tuple of values if fieldname is a list, from the first matching row. filters is a name, a dict or a list. Use None for a Single DocType. get_values (doctype, filters=None, fieldname='name', ignore=None, as_dict=False, debug=False, order_by='KEEP_DEFAULT_ORDERING', update=None, cache=False, for_update=False, *, run=True, pluck=False, distinct=False, limit=None, skip_locked=False, wait=True) Return values from all matching rows. get (doctype, filters=None, as_dict=True, cache=False) Return get_value with fieldname='*'. get_single_value (doctype, fieldname, cache=True) Return a field of a Single DocType, cast to its fieldtype. Cached in frappe.db.value_cache for the transaction by default. get_singles_value (*args, **kwargs) Alias of get_single_value. get_singles_dict (doctype, debug=False, *, for_update=False, cast=False) Return all fields of a Single DocType as a dict. get_list (*args, **kwargs) Calls frappe.get_list. Checks permissions. get_all (*args, **kwargs) Calls frappe.get_all. Does not check permissions. exists (dt, dn=None, cache=False) Return the name of a matching document, or None. dn is a name or a dict of filters. cache works only when dt and dn are strings. count (dt, filters=None, debug=False, cache=False, distinct: bool = True) Return COUNT(*) for the DocType and filters. With cache=True and no filters, the count is cached in Redis for 24 hours. estimate_count (doctype: str) Return the estimated row count from table statistics. Not cached. a_row_exists (doctype) Return True if the table has at least one row. get_creation_count (doctype, minutes) Return the number of records created in the last minutes. get_last_created (doctype) Return the creation timestamp of the last record, or None. get_descendants (doctype, name) Return the descendants of a node in a tree DocType.

docs.title: Write values
docs.text: Method Signature Description set_value (dt, dn, field, val=None, modified=None, modified_by=None, update_modified=True, debug=False) Update columns with SQL. No controller hooks or validation. Updates modified and modified_by unless update_modified=False. field can be a dict of field and value. On a Single DocType it warns that this is deprecated and calls set_single_value. set_single_value (doctype: str, fieldname: str \| dict, value=None, *, modified=None, modified_by=None, update_modified=True, debug=False) Set fields of a Single DocType. bulk_update (doctype: str, doc_updates: dict, *, chunk_size: int = 100, modified=None, modified_by=None, update_modified=True, debug=False) Update many documents. doc_updates maps each name to a dict of values. bulk_insert (doctype: str, fields: list[str], values: Iterable[Sequence], ignore_duplicates=False, *, chunk_size=10000) Insert many rows with one multi-row INSERT per chunk. No controller hooks. delete (doctype: str, filters: dict \| list \| None = None, debug=False, **kwargs) Run DELETE for matching rows. No controller hooks. truncate (doctype: str) Run TRUNCATE through sql_ddl. This commits first and cannot be rolled back.

docs.title: Raw SQL
docs.text:
Method Signature Description sql (query, values=<no value>, *, as_dict=0, as_list=0, debug=0, ignore_ddl=0, auto_commit=0, update=None, explain=False, run=True, pluck=False, as_iterator=False) Run a query and fetch all rows. Pass parameters in values, never with string formatting. query can also be a query builder object. sql_list (query, values=(), debug=False, **kwargs) Return the first column of each row as a list. sql_ddl (query, debug=False) Commit, then run a DDL query. multisql (sql_dict, values=(), **kwargs) Run the query for the current db_type from a dict like {"mariadb": ..., "postgres": ...}. There is no fallback key. mogrify (query, values) Return the query string with values substituted. escape (s, percent=True) Escape quotes, and % if percent=True. explain_query (query, values=None) Print EXPLAIN of the query in the error log. unbuffered_cursor () Context manager. Use a cursor that streams rows instead of fetching all of them. Use it with sql(..., as_iterator=True). get_description () Return the column metadata of the last query.

frappe.db has no qb attribute in v15. Use frappe.qb. See Query Builder.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text:
See Database for when Frappe commits for you.

Method Signature Description begin (*, read_only=False) Start a transaction. commit () Commit and start a new transaction. Runs before_commit and after_commit callbacks. Clears value_cache. rollback (*, save_point=None) Roll back the transaction, or to a savepoint. Runs before_rollback and after_rollback callbacks when there is no savepoint. savepoint (save_point) Make a savepoint. Rollback to it undoes only database changes, not files. release_savepoint (save_point) Release a savepoint. execution_timeout (seconds: float) Context manager. Sets a statement timeout for the block, then restores the old one. set_execution_timeout (seconds: float) Set the statement timeout of the session. get_execution_timeout () -> float Return the statement timeout in seconds. 0.0 means no limit. before_commit CallbackManager frappe.db.before_commit.add(fn) runs fn before the next commit. after_commit CallbackManager frappe.db.after_commit.add(fn) runs fn after the next commit. before_rollback CallbackManager Runs callbacks before the next rollback. after_rollback CallbackManager Runs callbacks after the next rollback.

frappe.database.database.savepoint(catch=Exception) is a context manager and decorator. It wraps a block in a savepoint and rolls back to it if catch is raised. frappe.database also exports it.

from frappe.database.database import savepoint

for name in ["Keyboard", "Monitor"]:
    with savepoint(catch=frappe.DuplicateEntryError):
        frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "Sample Item", "item_name": name}).insert()

docs.title: Error checks
docs.text:
Use these in except blocks to test a database error without database-specific codes. Each takes the exception and returns bool:

is_deadlocked, is_timedout, is_statement_timeout, is_read_only_mode_error, is_table_missing, is_missing_table, is_missing_column, is_missing_table_or_column, is_duplicate_entry, is_duplicate_fieldname, is_primary_key_violation, is_unique_key_violation, is_data_too_long, is_db_table_size_limit, is_syntax_error, is_access_denied, cant_drop_field_or_key, is_interface_error.

is_column_missing is deprecated. Use is_missing_column.

try:
    frappe.db.sql("insert into `tabSample Item` (name) values ('Keyboard')")
except Exception as e:
    if not frappe.db.is_duplicate_entry(e):
        raise

ADD INDEX IF NOT EXISTS CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS get_row_size Supported Raises NotImplementedError escape PyMySQL escape_string. Also escapes backticks psycopg2 QuotedString. None becomes an empty string

docs.title: JavaScript API
docs.text:
This page lists the client-side frappe namespaces that desk loads. Use it to find a function name and its arguments. The names come from each namespace (and class prototypes) in a logged-in v15 desk at /app. The signatures come from the source files listed in the frontmatter. Internal helpers are left out.

For usage and examples, see Client API and Form Scripts.

Note

Functions that talk to the server return a Promise or a jQuery deferred. Await them, or pass a callback where the signature has one.

docs.title: Server calls
frappe.db
docs.text:
Each function calls a method in frappe.client or frappe.desk.reportview. Permissions of the current user apply.

Function Signature Description get_value (doctype, filters, fieldname, callback, parent_doc) Return field values of the first match. Resolves with { message: {...} }, so read r.message. get_single_value (doctype, field) Resolve with one field of a Single DocType. get_list (doctype, args) Resolve with a list of records. args takes fields, filters, order_by, limit and more. Default fields is ["name"]. Default limit is 20. get_doc (doctype, name, filters) Resolve with the full document. Adds it to locals. exists (doctype, name) Resolve with true or false. Checks by name only. count (doctype, args = {}) Resolve with the number of matching records. args takes filters and limit. insert (doc) Insert a new document. doc must have doctype. set_value (doctype, docname, fieldname, value, callback) Set one value, or many with a dict as fieldname. Saves the document on the server. delete_doc (doctype, name) Delete a document. get_link_options (doctype, txt = "", filters = {}, page_length = 0) Resolve with Link search results. 
const items = await frappe.db.get_list("Sample Item", {
    fields: ["name", "rate"],
    filters: { category: "Hardware" },
    limit: 2,
});
// [{ name: "Keyboard", rate: 45 }, { name: "Monitor", rate: 250 }]

docs.title: frappe.ui.Dialog
docs.text:
new frappe.ui.Dialog(opts) makes a dialog. Dialog extends frappe.ui.FieldGroup.

Option Description title Dialog title. fields List of field definitions (fieldname, fieldtype, label, options, reqd, default, ...). size "small", "large" or "extra-large". Without it, the size comes from the number of Column Breaks. primary_action_label, primary_action(values) Main button. values comes from get_values(). secondary_action_label, secondary_action Second button. minimizable Allow the user to minimize the dialog. Method Description show(), hide() Open or close the dialog. get_values(ignore_errors, check_invalid) Return field values. Returns nothing if a mandatory field is empty. get_value(key), set_value(key, val), set_values(dict) Read or set fields. get_field(fieldname) Return the control of a field. set_df_property(fieldname, prop, value) Change a field property. set_primary_action(label, click) Change the main button. disable_primary_action(), enable_primary_action() Toggle the main button. set_title(t), set_message(text) Change title or message. clear() Clear all values. add_custom_action(label, action, css_class = null) Add a button to the footer.

Dialog has no set_query or set_alert in v15. To filter a Link field in a dialog, set get_query in the field definition.

const d = new frappe.ui.Dialog({
    title: __("New Sample Item"),
    fields: [
        { fieldname: "item_name", fieldtype: "Data", label: __("Item Name"), reqd: 1 },
        { fieldname: "rate", fieldtype: "Currency", label: __("Rate") },
    ],
    primary_action_label: __("Create"),
    primary_action(values) {
        frappe.db.insert({ doctype: "Sample Item", ...values }).then(() => d.hide());
    },
});
d.show();

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
This page lists the public names on the frappe module. Use it to find the exact name and signature of a function. The list comes from dir(frappe), read with inspect.signature on a v15 site. Internal helpers, re-exported standard library modules and exception classes are left out.

In v15, most functions are defined directly in frappe/__init__.py. Some are thin wrappers with the signature (*args, **kwargs) that import their module on first call. For these, the signature of the target function is shown, and the target file is named.

For frappe.db methods, see Database API. For frappe.utils helpers, see Utilities.

docs.title: Context objects
docs.text:
These are request-local objects. They are proxies to frappe.local and are valid only after frappe.init() and frappe.connect().

Name Type Description frappe.local Local Thread-local and request-local storage. All objects below live on it. frappe.db LocalProxy to Database Database connection of the current site. See Database API. frappe.qb LocalProxy Query builder for the current database type. See Query Builder. frappe.session LocalProxy Current session. frappe.session.user is the name of the current user. frappe.user LocalProxy Proxy to frappe.local.user. It is always None. set_user does not set it. Use frappe.session.user. frappe.form_dict LocalProxy (_dict) Request parameters (query string and form body). frappe.form LocalProxy Alias of frappe.form_dict. frappe.request LocalProxy The Werkzeug request object. frappe.response LocalProxy (_dict) Response dict. Whitelisted methods put their return value in frappe.response["message"]. frappe.flags LocalProxy (_dict) Request-scoped flags, for example frappe.flags.in_test, frappe.flags.in_import, frappe.flags.in_migrate. frappe.conf LocalProxy (_dict) Merged site_config.json and common_site_config.json. See Configuration. frappe.lang LocalProxy Language code of the current request. frappe.message_log LocalProxy (list) Messages queued by frappe.msgprint. frappe.error_log LocalProxy (list) Errors queued by frappe.errprint. frappe.debug_log LocalProxy (list) Lines queued by frappe.log. frappe.job LocalProxy Current background job info, if the code runs in a worker. frappe.cache RedisWrapper Redis cache client. frappe.cache() also works and returns the same object, for older code. See Caching. frappe.STANDARD_USERS tuple ("Guest", "Administrator"). Function Signature Description frappe.init (site: str, sites_path: str = '.', new_site: bool = False, force=False) -> None Initialize frappe for a site. Resets frappe.local. frappe.init_site (site=None) Context manager. Runs frappe.init(site) for the block, then frappe.destroy(). frappe.connect (site: str \| None = None, db_name: str \| None = None, set_admin_as_user: bool = True) -> None Connect to the site database. If site is given, it calls frappe.init(site) first. frappe.connect_replica () -> bool Connect to the read replica set in site config. frappe.destroy () Close the database connection and release frappe.local. frappe.set_user (username: str) Set the current user. Clears cached user permissions. frappe.get_user () Return a UserPermissions object for the session user. frappe.get_roles (username=None) -> list[str] Return the roles of a user. Default is the session user. frappe.get_request_header (key, default=None) Return an HTTP request header. frappe.get_site_config (sites_path: str \| None = None, site_path: str \| None = None) -> dict[str, Any] Return site_config.json merged with common_site_config.json. frappe.get_common_site_config (sites_path: str \| None = None) -> dict[str, Any] Return common_site_config.json. frappe.get_conf (site: str \| None = None) -> dict[str, Any] Return the config of a site. frappe.get_system_settings (key: str) Return one value from System Settings. frappe.get_website_settings (key) Return one value from Website Settings. frappe.get_site_path (*joins) Return the path of the current site folder, joined with joins. frappe.is_setup_complete () Return True if the setup wizard is complete. frappe.ping () Return "pong". frappe.logger (module=None, with_more_info=False, allow_site=True, filter=None, max_size=100000, file_count=20) Return a Python logger that writes to the bench log folder. frappe.log (msg: str) -> None Add a line to frappe.debug_log. frappe.errprint (msg: str) -> None Add an error line. It is sent back as exc in the response. frappe.print_sql (enable: bool = True) -> None Print every SQL query to the console. Use it to debug.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
See Controllers for the Document class and its lifecycle.

Function Signature Description frappe.get_doc (doctype, name, /, *, for_update=None) or (doctype, /) or (dict) or (**kwargs) Return a Document. With a name, load it from the database. With a Single DocType name, load the Single. With a dict, make a new unsaved document. Calls frappe.model.document.get_doc. frappe.new_doc (doctype: str, *, parent_doc=None, parentfield=None, as_dict=False, **kwargs) -> Document Return a new document with defaults set. Extra kwargs set field values. frappe.get_lazy_doc same as get_doc Alias of get_doc in v15 (get_lazy_doc = get_doc). Child tables load at once. frappe.get_cached_doc (*args, **kwargs) -> Document Same as get_doc, but return a copy from the cache if present. frappe.get_last_doc (doctype, filters=None, order_by='creation desc', *, for_update=False) Return the last created document that matches the filters. Raises DoesNotExistError if none match. frappe.get_single (doctype) Return the document of a Single DocType. frappe.copy_doc (doc: Document, ignore_no_copy: bool = True) -> Document Return an unsaved copy of a document. Clears name, owner, creation, modified, modified_by. frappe.delete_doc (doctype=None, name=None, force=False, ignore_doctypes=None, for_reload=False, ignore_permissions=False, flags=None, ignore_on_trash=False, ignore_missing=True, delete_permanently=False) Delete a document. Calls frappe.model.delete_doc.delete_doc. frappe.delete_doc_if_exists (doctype, name, force=0) Delete a document if it exists. frappe.rename_doc (doctype: str, old: str, new: str, force=False, merge=False, *, ignore_if_exists=False, show_alert=True, rebuild_search=True) -> str Rename a document and update all Link fields that point to it. frappe.get_version (doctype, name, limit=None, head=False, raise_err=True) Return the change history of a document from Version records. Each item has version, user and creation. The DocType must track changes. frappe.get_meta (doctype, cached=True) Return the metadata (DocType with custom fields and property setters applied). frappe.get_meta_module (doctype) Return the Python module of a DocType controller. frappe.is_table (doctype: str) -> bool Return True if the DocType is a child table (istable). frappe.get_doctype_app (doctype) Return the app that owns a DocType. frappe.get_precision (doctype: str, fieldname: str, currency: str \| None = None, doc=None) -> int Return the precision of a Float, Currency or Percent field. frappe.clear_document_cache (doctype: str, name: str \| None = None) -> None Remove a document from the document cache. frappe.reload_doc (module: str, dt=None, dn=None, force=False, reset_permissions=False) Reload a DocType or record from its JSON file in the module. Use it in patches. frappe.reload_doctype (doctype, force=False, reset_permissions=False) Reload a DocType from its JSON file. frappe.import_doc (path) Import documents from a JSON file, or every JSON file in a folder. frappe.make_property_setter (args, ignore_validate=False, validate_fields_for_doctype=True, is_system_generated=True, *, module=None) Make a Property Setter that overrides a DocType or DocField property.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
See Database for filter syntax.

Function Signature Description frappe.get_list (doctype, *args, **kwargs) Return records as a list of dicts. Applies permissions of the current user. The docstring says the default page length is 20, but a call without limit returns all rows. frappe.get_all (doctype, *args, **kwargs) Same as get_list, but does not check permissions. Sets limit_page_length=0 (no limit) if you do not pass it. Default fields is ["name"]. frappe.get_value (*args, **kwargs) Alias of frappe.db.get_value. frappe.get_cached_value (doctype: str, name: str, fieldname: str = 'name', as_dict: bool = False) Return field values from the cached document. Returns None if the document does not exist. frappe.get_single_value (setting: str, fieldname: str, /, *, as_dict: bool = False) Return a cached value from a Single DocType. frappe.set_value (doctype, docname, fieldname, value=None) Set a value through frappe.client.set_value. Runs validations and saves the document. frappe.get_query (*args, **kwargs) -> QueryBuilder Build a query builder object from doctype, fields and filters. Defined in frappe/query_builder/utils.py. See Query Builder. frappe.get_query_builder (type_of_db: str) Return the query builder class for mariadb or postgres.

docs.title: Messages and errors
docs.text:
Function Signature Description frappe.msgprint (msg, title=None, raise_exception=False, as_table=False, as_list=False, indicator=None, alert=False, primary_action=None, is_minimizable=False, wide=False, *, realtime=False) -> None Queue a message for the user. It is sent in __server_messages of the response. indicator is blue, green, orange, red or yellow. frappe.throw (msg, exc=ValidationError, title=None, is_minimizable=False, wide=False, as_list=False, primary_action=None) -> None Show a message and raise exc. frappe.clear_messages () Clear all queued messages. frappe.clear_last_message () Remove the last queued message. frappe.get_message_log () -> list[dict] Return the queued messages. frappe.log_error (title=None, message=None, reference_doctype=None, reference_name=None, *, defer_insert=False) Make an Error Log. Without message, logs the current traceback. Defined in frappe/utils/error.py. frappe.get_traceback (with_context: bool = False) -> str Return the traceback of the current exception. frappe.respond_as_web_page (title, html, success=None, http_status_code=None, context=None, indicator_color=None, primary_action='/', primary_label=None, fullpage=False, width=None, template='message') Send the response as an HTML message page, not JSON. frappe.redirect_to_message (title, html, http_status_code=None, context=None, indicator_color=None) Redirect to /message?id=... and show a message page. frappe.redirect (url) Raise frappe.Redirect, which sends a 301 redirect to url.

Exception classes such as frappe.ValidationError, frappe.PermissionError, frappe.DoesNotExistError, frappe.DuplicateEntryError, frappe.MandatoryError, frappe.LinkValidationError and frappe.TimestampMismatchError come from frappe/exceptions.py.

With throw=True, raise PermissionError. frappe.has_website_permission (doc=None, ptype='read', user=None, verbose=False, doctype=None) Check website (portal) permission through the has_website_permission hook. frappe.only_for (roles: list[str] \| tuple[str] \| str, message=False) Raise PermissionError if the user has none of the roles. frappe.only_has_select_perm (doctype, user=None, ignore_permissions=False) Return True if the user has only select permission on the DocType. frappe.build_match_conditions (doctype, as_condition=True) Return user permission conditions for a DocType as SQL or a list.

docs.text:

Function Signature Description frappe.whitelist (allow_guest=False, xss_safe=False, methods=None) Decorator. docs.title: Background jobs and realtime
docs.text:
See Background Jobs and Realtime.

Function Signature Description frappe.enqueue see below Put a function on an RQ queue. Calls frappe.utils.background_jobs.enqueue. frappe.enqueue_doc (doctype, name=None, method=None, queue='default', timeout=300, now=False, **kwargs) Enqueue a controller method of a document. frappe.task (**task_kwargs) Decorator. Adds .enqueue(**kwargs) to the function, which calls frappe.enqueue with task_kwargs. frappe.publish_realtime (event=None, message=None, room=None, user=None, doctype=None, docname=None, task_id=None, after_commit=False) Send a Socket.IO event to the browser. Calls frappe/realtime.py. frappe.publish_progress (percent, title=None, doctype=None, docname=None, description=None, task_id=None) Send a progress event. Desk shows a progress bar. 
# frappe/utils/background_jobs.py
frappe.enqueue(
    method: str | Callable, queue: str = "default", timeout: int | None = None, event=None,
    is_async: bool = True, job_name: str | None = None, now: bool = False, enqueue_after_commit: bool = False,
    *, on_success: Callable | None = None, on_failure: Callable | None = None, at_front: bool = False,
    job_id: str | None = None, deduplicate=False, **kwargs,
) -> Job | Any

job_name is deprecated. Use job_id. is_async=False outside of tests is deprecated. Use now=True.

docs.text:

docs.title: Strings, JSON and files
docs.text:
cint, cstr and sbool come from frappe.utils.data. The others are defined in frappe/__init__.py and are not on frappe.utils in v15. See Utilities for the rest.

Function Signature Description frappe.as_json (obj: dict \| list, indent=1, separators=None, ensure_ascii=True) -> str Return a JSON string. Handles dates, decimals and documents. frappe.parse_json (val) Parse a JSON string into a _dict. Returns other values as they are. frappe.cint (s: int \| float \| str, default: int = 0) -> int Convert to integer. frappe.cstr (s, encoding='utf-8') Convert to string. None becomes "". frappe.sbool (x: str) -> bool \| Any Convert "true", "false", "1", "0" strings to bool. frappe.scrub (txt: str) -> str Sales Order becomes sales_order. frappe.unscrub (txt: str) -> str sales_order becomes Sales Order. frappe.bold (text) Wrap text in <strong> tags. frappe.as_unicode (text, encoding: str = 'utf-8') -> str Convert bytes to str. frappe.safe_encode (param, encoding='utf-8') Encode str to bytes. frappe.safe_decode (param, encoding='utf-8', fallback_map: dict \| None = None) Decode bytes to str. frappe.safe_eval (code, eval_globals=None, eval_locals=None) Evaluate an expression with restricted globals. frappe.generate_hash (txt: str \| None = None, length: int = 56) -> str Return a random hex string. txt is not used. frappe.mock (type, size=1, locale='en') Return fake data from the faker package. frappe.read_file (path, raise_not_found=False, as_base64=False) Return the content of a file. frappe.get_file_json (path) Read a file and parse it as JSON. frappe.get_file_items (path, raise_not_found=False, ignore_empty_lines=True) Return the lines of a text file as a list. frappe.create_folder (path, with_init=False) Make a folder. With with_init=True, add __init__.py.

docs.title: REST Endpoints Reference
docs.text: This page lists every route that Frappe v15 serves under /api, and the core whitelisted methods that clients call most. For how to authenticate, filter and page, see REST API and Authentication.

docs.title: Route maps
docs.text:
frappe/api/__init__.py mounts three route sets:

Prefix Rules from Response key /api/ frappe/api/v1.py message for methods, data for resources /api/v1/ frappe/api/v1.py (same rules) same as /api/ /api/v2/ frappe/api/v2.py data for all routes. Errors are in errors

Trailing slashes are optional. An unknown route raises DoesNotExistError (HTTP 404). All routes run as the session user. Permission checks are those of the called function.

docs.title: API v1
API v2
docs.text:
Route HTTP methods Does Permission check /api/v2/method/login any Does nothing by itself. See the warning below. none /api/v2/method/logout any Log out the session. none /api/v2/method/ping any Returns "pong". none /api/v2/method/upload_file any Upload a file. Same as frappe.handler.upload_file. see Files /api/v2/method/run_doc_method GET, POST Run a whitelisted method on a document dict. Args: method, document, kwargs. read (GET), write (POST) /api/v2/method/<dotted.path> any allowed by the method Calls a whitelisted function or API Server Script. Applies override_whitelisted_methods. @frappe.whitelist rules /api/v2/method/<doctype>/<method> any allowed by the method Calls a whitelisted module function in the DocType's controller file. @frappe.whitelist rules /api/v2/document/<doctype> GET List records. Returns data. get_list permission rules /api/v2/document/<doctype> POST Insert a document from the JSON body. create /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> GET Read one document. read /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> PATCH, PUT Update fields and save. write /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> DELETE Delete. Returns HTTP 202 and "ok". delete /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/copy GET A copy of the document without name and other private properties, ready to insert. The route keeps no_copy fields. read /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/method/<method> GET, POST Call a whitelisted controller method. The saved document goes in docs. read (GET), write (POST) /api/v2/doctype/<doctype>/meta GET DocType meta. logged-in user (frappe.only_for("All")) /api/v2/doctype/<doctype>/count GET Count with optional filters. frappe.desk.reportview.get_count rules

List parameters for GET /api/v2/document/<doctype>: fields, filters, order_by, group_by, start (default 0), limit (default 20), as_dict, debug. The response has only data. To get the next page, raise start until a page has fewer rows than limit.

For run_doc_method with a document that is not saved, add "__islocal": 1 to the document dict. Without it, Frappe tries to load the document from the database.

Login in v2

In v15, LoginManager logs in only when the path is /api/method/login or the form has cmd=login. A plain POST /api/v2/method/login returns {} and leaves the session as Guest. Use /api/method/login, or add "cmd": "login" to the v2 body.

curl -b cookies.txt -X POST http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/v2/document/ToDo \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"description": "Sample REST todo"}'
curl -b cookies.txt -X PATCH http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/v2/document/ToDo/3u0lp3tjma \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"status": "Closed"}'
curl -b cookies.txt "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/v2/doctype/ToDo/count"

{"data": 5}

Version

v15 has no API discovery routes, no MCP route, and no v2 bulk routes. The QUERY HTTP method is not supported.

docs.title: Login, logout and files
docs.text:
These work on /api/method/... (v1).

Method path HTTP methods Guest Description login POST yes Log in. Args: usr, pwd. Returns message, home_page, full_name and sets the sid cookie. message is "No App" for website users. logout (frappe.handler.logout) any yes Log out the current session. frappe.handler.web_logout any yes Log out and show a "Logged Out" web page. frappe.auth.get_logged_user any no Returns the user name of the session. frappe.ping any yes Returns "pong". upload_file (frappe.handler.upload_file) any yes Upload a file as multipart form data (file, doctype, docname, fieldname, is_private, folder, file_url, file_name, optimize). Guests can upload only when System Settings allow_guests_to_upload_files is on. frappe.handler.download_file any yes Download a file by file_url, with session or token auth. frappe.core.doctype.user.user.reset_password POST yes Send a password reset link. Arg: user. frappe.core.doctype.user.user.update_password POST yes Set a new password with key or old_password. Args: new_password, logout_all_sessions. frappe.core.doctype.user.user.sign_up any yes Website sign up. Args: email, full_name, redirect_to.

Short names such as logout and upload_file resolve to frappe.handler and print a deprecation warning. Use the full dotted path in new code.

curl -c cookies.txt -X POST http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/method/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"usr": "Administrator", "pwd": "password"}'

{"message": "Logged In", "home_page": "/app", "full_name": "Administrator"}

docs.title: frappe.client methods
docs.text:
Call them as /api/method/frappe.client.<name> or /api/v2/method/frappe.client.<name>. Defined in frappe/client.py. "any" means GET, POST, PUT and DELETE, the default of @frappe.whitelist.

Method HTTP methods Arguments Description get_list any doctype, fields, filters, or_filters, group_by, order_by, limit_start, limit_page_length (20), parent, as_dict, expand, debug List records with permission checks. get_count any doctype, filters, cache, debug Count records. get any doctype, name or filters, parent Get one document as a dict. get_value any doctype, fieldname (str or list), filters, as_dict, parent, debug Get field values of one record. get_single_value any doctype, field Get a field of a Single DocType. set_value POST, PUT doctype, name, fieldname (str or dict), value Set values and save the document. insert POST, PUT doc Insert a document. A child row needs parenttype, parent, parentfield. insert_many POST, PUT docs Insert many documents. save POST, PUT doc Save an existing document. rename_doc POST, PUT doctype, old_name, new_name, merge Rename a document. submit POST, PUT doc Submit a document. cancel POST, PUT doctype, name Cancel a submitted document. delete DELETE, POST doctype, name Delete a document. bulk_update POST, PUT docs Update many documents. Each item has doctype, docname and fields. has_permission any doctype, docname, perm_type (read) Returns {"has_permission": bool}. get_doc_permissions any doctype, docname Returns {"permissions": {...}}. get_password any doctype, name, fieldname Returns a decrypted Password field. System Manager only. get_time_zone any (guest) none Returns the system time zone. attach_file POST, PUT filename, filedata, doctype, docname, folder, decode_base64, is_private, docfield Attach file content to a document. is_document_amended any doctype, docname True when an amended copy exists. validate_link any doctype, docname, fields Check a Link value and fetch fields from the linked record. Needs select or read permission. get_js any items Deprecated. Returns the content of JS files under assets/. 
curl -b cookies.txt "http://frappe.localhost:8001/api/v2/method/frappe.client.get_value?doctype=User&filters=%22Administrator%22&fieldname=%5B%22full_name%22%5D"

{"data": {"full_name": "Administrator"}}

docs.title: Other core methods
docs.text:
The desk calls these. They are useful for clients too.

Method HTTP methods Description frappe.desk.reportview.get any List view data. Args like get_list (doctype, fields, filters, order_by, start, page_length). frappe.desk.reportview.get_count any Count for list view. frappe.desk.reportview.export_query any Export Report Builder data as CSV or Excel. frappe.desk.reportview.delete_items POST, DELETE Delete selected records. frappe.desk.form.load.getdoc any Load a document with docinfo for the form. frappe.desk.form.load.getdoctype any Load DocType meta and scripts for the form. frappe.desk.form.save.savedocs POST, PUT Save, submit or update a document from the form. Args: doc, action. frappe.desk.form.save.cancel POST, PUT Cancel from the form. frappe.desk.search.search_link any Results for a Link field dropdown. frappe.desk.query_report.run any Run a Query or Script Report. Args: report_name, filters. frappe.rename_doc POST, PUT Rename and update links.

frappe has about 530 whitelisted functions and controller methods in v15. App developers make new ones with @frappe.whitelist(). See Whitelisted Methods.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A method without methods= in @frappe.whitelist accepts GET, POST, PUT and DELETE. Write methods should set methods=["POST"].
  • v1 PUT /api/resource/... and v2 PATCH call doc.save(). They do not submit. Use the submit method or a document method.
  • frappe.client.get_list, /api/resource and /api/v2/document return 20 rows by default. limit_page_length=0 (v1) or limit=0 (v2) removes the limit. Use it with care on large tables.
  • System Settings has a log_api_requests field, but no code in v15 reads it. No API Request Log is written.

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text:
frappe.utils holds helpers for type conversion, dates, numbers, formatting, strings, URLs and files. Most of them live in frappe/utils/data.py. frappe/utils/__init__.py re-exports them with from frappe.utils.data import *. Import them from frappe.utils:

from frappe.utils import cint, flt, getdate, add_days, nowdate

The signatures come from inspect.signature on a v15 site. Type hints are shortened. DateTimeLikeObject means str | datetime.date | datetime.datetime. Helpers in other modules show the full import path.

Note

In v15, scrub, unscrub, bold, safe_encode, safe_decode, read_file and get_file_json are on frappe, not on frappe.utils. Import them with from frappe import scrub. See Python API.

docs.title: Example output
docs.text:
These results come from a v15 site with date format dd-mm-yyyy, number format #,##,###.## and rounding method Banker's Rounding:

from frappe.utils import (
    cint, flt, cstr, getdate, add_days, date_diff, add_to_date, get_last_day, comma_and, fmt_money, format_date,
)

cint("12.7")                      # 12
cint("abc")                       # 0
cint(None, 5)                     # 5
flt("1,234.567", 2)               # 1234.57
cstr(None)                        # ''
getdate("2026-01-15")             # datetime.date(2026, 1, 15)
add_days("2026-01-31", 1)         # '2026-02-01'  (string in, string out)
add_days(getdate("2026-01-31"), 1)  # datetime.date(2026, 2, 1)
date_diff("2026-03-01", "2026-02-01")  # 28
add_to_date("2026-01-31", months=1)    # '2026-02-28'
get_last_day("2026-02-14")        # datetime.date(2026, 2, 28)
comma_and(["a", "b", "c"])        # "'a', 'b' and 'c'"
fmt_money(1234567.891, 2, "USD")  # '$ 12,34,567.89'
format_date("2026-01-15")         # '15-01-2026'

docs.title: Type conversion
docs.text: Function Signature Description cint (s: int \| float \| str, default: int = 0) -> int Convert to integer. Returns default if conversion fails. flt (s: int \| float \| str, precision: int \| None = None, rounding_method: str \| None = None) -> float Convert to float. Ignores commas in strings. Rounds to precision if given. cstr (s, encoding='utf-8') Convert to string. None becomes "". sbool (x: str) -> bool \| Any Convert "true", "false", "1", "0" and similar strings to bool. cast (fieldtype, value=None) Cast a value to the Python type of a Frappe fieldtype. parse_json (val) Parse a JSON string into _dict. Returns other values as they are. parse_val (v) Convert SQL result values to simple Python types. encode (obj, encoding='utf-8') Encode a string to bytes.

docs.title: Current date and time
docs.text:
All values are in the system time zone (System Settings).

Function Signature Description nowdate () -> str Current date as yyyy-mm-dd. today () -> str Same as nowdate. nowtime () -> str Current time as hh:mm:ss. now () -> str Current datetime as yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss. now_datetime () Current datetime as a datetime object. get_datetime_in_timezone (time_zone) Current datetime in the given time zone. get_system_timezone () -> str The system time zone name. get_timestamp (date) Unix timestamp of the date.

docs.title: Parse dates and times
docs.text: Function Signature Description getdate (string_date=None, parse_day_first=False) -> date \| None Convert to datetime.date. No argument returns today. get_datetime (datetime_str=None) -> datetime \| None Convert to datetime.datetime. No argument returns now. get_time (time_str: str) -> time Convert to datetime.time. get_timedelta (time: str \| timedelta \| None = None) -> timedelta \| None Convert a time string to datetime.timedelta. to_timedelta (time_str: str \| time) -> timedelta Convert a string or time to timedelta. get_date_str (date_obj) -> str Return a date as yyyy-mm-dd. get_datetime_str (datetime_obj) -> str Return a datetime as yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss. get_time_str (timedelta_obj) -> str Return a timedelta as hh:mm:ss. guess_date_format (date_string: str) -> str Guess the format string of a date. is_invalid_date_string (date_string: str) -> bool Return True if the string is empty or not a date.

docs.title: Date arithmetic
docs.text:
Functions that take a date string return a string. Functions that take a date or datetime return the same type.

Function Signature Description add_days (date, days) Add days. add_months (date, months) Add months. add_years (date, years) Add years. add_to_date (date=None, years=0, months=0, weeks=0, days=0, hours=0, minutes=0, seconds=0, as_string=False, as_datetime=False) Add any mix of units. date_diff (string_ed_date, string_st_date) -> int Days between two dates (end minus start). days_diff (string_ed_date, string_st_date) -> int Same as date_diff. month_diff (string_ed_date, string_st_date) Months between two dates. time_diff (string_ed_date, string_st_date) Difference as timedelta. time_diff_in_seconds (string_ed_date, string_st_date) Difference in seconds. time_diff_in_hours (string_ed_date, string_st_date) Difference in hours. get_first_day (dt, d_years: int = 0, d_months: int = 0, as_str: bool = False) First day of the month. get_last_day (dt) Last day of the month. get_first_day_of_week (dt, as_str=False) First day of the week. The start day comes from System Settings, Sunday by default. get_last_day_of_week (dt) Last day of the week. get_quarter_start (dt, as_str: bool = False) First day of the quarter. get_quarter_ending (date) Last day of the quarter. get_year_start (dt, as_str=False) First day of the year. get_year_ending (date) -> date Last day of the year. get_timespan_date_range (timespan: str) -> tuple \| None (start_date, end_date) for "last week", "this month", "today" and the other timespan filter values. is_last_day_of_the_month (dt) Return True if the date is the last day of its month. get_weekday (datetime=None) -> str Weekday name, for example "Sunday". get_weekdays () All weekday names. get_month (datetime=None) -> str Month name, for example "January". convert_utc_to_system_timezone (utc_timestamp) Convert a UTC datetime to the system time zone. convert_utc_to_timezone (utc_timestamp, time_zone) Convert a UTC datetime to a time zone.

docs.title: Format for display
docs.text:
These use the formats from System Settings and the user. Use frappe.format_value to format by fieldtype.

Function Signature Description format_date (string_date=None, format_string=None, parse_day_first=False) -> str Format a date in the user date format. formatdate same as format_date Alias of format_date. format_time (time_string=None, format_string=None) -> str Format a time in the user time format. format_datetime (datetime_string, format_string=None) -> str Format a datetime in the user format. global_date_format (date, format='long') Localized date such as January 1, 2012. pretty_date (iso_datetime: datetime \| str) -> str Relative time such as 2 hours ago. format_duration (seconds: float \| int, hide_days: bool = False) -> str Format seconds as a duration such as 1d 2h 3m 4s. duration_to_seconds (duration) Convert a duration string to seconds. fmt_money (amount, precision=None, currency=None, format=None) -> str Format a number with digit groups and an optional currency symbol. money_in_words (number, main_currency=None, fraction_currency=None) Amount in words with currency, for example USD One Thousand, Two Hundred And Fifty and Fifty Cent only. in_words (integer: int, in_million=True) -> str Integer in words. get_user_date_format () -> str Date format of the current user. get_user_time_format () -> str Time format of the current user.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text: Function Signature Description rounded (num, precision=0, rounding_method=None) Round with the method from System Settings. If none is set, it uses Banker's Rounding (legacy). With Banker's Rounding, rounded(2.5) is 2.0. ceil (s) Round up. floor (s) Round down. safe_div (numerator, denominator, precision: int = 2) -> float Divide. Returns 0 if denominator is 0. remainder (numerator, denominator, precision: int = 2) Remainder of a division. round_based_on_smallest_currency_fraction (value, currency, precision=2) Round to the smallest fraction of the currency.

Same as frappe.generate_hash. sha256_hash (input: str \| bytes) -> str SHA-256 hex digest. comma_and (some_list, add_quotes=True) Join with commas and and. comma_or (some_list, add_quotes=True) Join with commas and or. new_line_sep (some_list) Join with new lines. unique (seq) -> list Remove duplicates and keep the order. has_common (l1, l2) -> bool Return True if the lists share an item. is_subset (list_a: list, list_b: list) -> bool Return True if list_a is a subset of list_b. create_batch (iterable, size: int) Yield batches of size items. dict_with_keys (dict, keys) Return a new dict with only keys. remove_blanks (d: dict) -> dict Remove keys with falsy values. Changes d in place. The docstring says "" and None, but the code also removes 0 and False. compare (val1, condition: str, val2, fieldtype=None) -> bool Compare two values with a filter operator such as ">" or "in". evaluate_filters (doc, filters: dict \| list \| tuple) Return True if a document or dict matches the filters.

docs.text:
Module frappe.utils.file_manager. To work with files in code, prefer the File DocType. See Files.

docs.text:
Module frappe.utils.response. respond_as_web_page and redirect_to_message are on frappe in v15. See Python API.

docs.text:
Every hook key, site config key and bench command.

Page What it covers Hooks Reference Every hooks.py key that Frappe Framework v15 reads, with its shape, the file that reads it, and what it does. Site Config Reference Every site_config.json and common_site_config.json key that Frappe Framework v15 reads, with its default and meaning. CLI Reference Every bench command that the frappe app provides in v15, with its options and whether it needs a site.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: This page lists every bench command that the frappe app adds in v15. The list and the options come from the click definitions in frappe/commands/. Commands of the bench tool itself (init, get-app, new-app, start, setup ...) are not on this page. Run all commands from the bench root (frappe-bench/).

docs.title: How commands find the site
docs.text:
bench loads frappe.commands.commands and the commands list of every other app (<app>/commands/__init__.py or <app>/commands.py). It wraps them in one group that takes these options before the command name:

Option Description --site <site> Site to run on. --site all runs on every site, for commands that loop over sites. --verbose Verbose output. --force Force flag. Some commands read it (for example run-patch, reload-doc). --profile Run the command under cProfile and print the top 100 lines.

When --site is not given, bench uses the FRAPPE_SITE environment variable, then default_site from common_site_config.json (set with bench use <site>). A sites/currentsite.txt file is not supported. bench only prints a warning when it finds one.

bench --site frappe.localhost migrate
bench --site all clear-cache
bench --site frappe.localhost execute frappe.client.get_count --args '["ToDo"]'

In the tables below, "Needs site" means:

  • Yes: the command runs on the site from --site (or the default site). Without one, it fails with "Please specify --site sitename".
  • Optional: the command also works without a site, or takes --site after the command name.
  • No: the command does not use a site.

Run bench <command> --help to see the same options on your bench.

Version

v15 has 91 frappe commands. These develop commands do not exist in v15: enable-app, disable-app, list-sites, bypass-patch, sync-desktop-icons, setup-chrome, run-microbenchmarks. In v15 the test commands are in frappe/commands/utils.py.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Put global options before the command: bench --site s1 migrate, not bench migrate --site s1. Only commands that define their own --site (for example doctor, show-pending-jobs, ready-for-migration, purge-jobs) accept it after the name.
  • bench execute evaluates --args and --kwargs as Python literals. Quote them for the shell.
  • restore, reinstall, drop-site and uninstall-app delete data. Take a backup first.

docs.title: Hooks Reference
docs.text: This page lists every key in an app's hooks.py that the framework reads in v15. Use it to look up the shape of a hook value and the code that reads it. For how hooks work and how values from many apps merge, see Hooks.

docs.title: How to read this page
docs.text:
• frappe.get_hooks("key") collects the key from all installed apps and returns a list. A single string value becomes a one-item list.
  • A dict value is merged key by key. Each inner value also becomes a list. For example, doc_events["*"]["on_update"] is a list of dotted paths from all apps.
  • "Last wins" means the framework uses only the last item ([-1]). Apps load in install order, so the app installed last wins.
  • "First wins" means the framework uses only the first item ([0]).
  • "All run" means the framework calls every dotted path in the list, in app order.
  • "Per app" means the framework reads the key with app_name=<app> and uses only that app's value.
  • Paths in the "Read in" column are relative to apps/frappe.

The Audit System Hooks report (frappe/custom/report/audit_system_hooks) shows the merged value of each hook on a site. In code, check a value from the console:

frappe.get_hooks("calendars")   # ['Event']

docs.title: App metadata
docs.text:
Key Shape Read in Description app_name str frappe/utils/boilerplate.py Python package name of the app. Written by bench new-app. app_title str frappe/utils/change_log.py, frappe/email/email_body.py, frappe/gettext/translate.py, frappe/desk/doctype/changelog_feed/changelog_feed.py, frappe/core/doctype/user_invitation/user_invitation.py Display name. Used in version info, in .pot headers, in the changelog feed, in invitation emails and as the email header title (last wins). app_publisher str frappe/modules/utils.py, frappe/gettext/translate.py Copyright holder in boilerplate files and .pot headers. Per app. app_description str frappe/utils/change_log.py Description shown in version info. Per app. app_email str frappe/gettext/translate.py Bug report address in the .pot catalog header. Per app. app_license str frappe/utils/boilerplate.py License name. Only the boilerplate generator uses it. app_logo_url str frappe/core/doctype/navbar_settings/navbar_settings.py Navbar logo when Navbar Settings has none. When exactly two apps set one, the second logo is used. <branch>_version str frappe/utils/change_log.py, frappe/commands/utils.py Version label for a branch, for example develop_version. Shown when the app is not on master, and by bench version. add_to_apps_screen list of dict frappe/apps.py Adds the app to the apps screen (/apps). Keys: name, logo, title, route, has_permission (dotted path). The tile always shows the app that sets the hook. name is used only to find a workspace of the app's modules when the user cannot open route. required_apps list of str frappe/installer.py, frappe/boot.py, frappe/core/doctype/installed_applications/installed_applications.py Apps to install before this app. bench install-app installs them first. uninstall-app refuses to remove an app that another app requires. 
# sample_app/hooks.py
app_name = "sample_app"
app_title = "Sample App"
app_publisher = "Example Corp"
required_apps = ["frappe"]
add_to_apps_screen = [
    {
        "name": "sample_app",
        "logo": "/assets/sample_app/logo.svg",
        "title": "Sample App",
        "route": "/app/sample-item",
        "has_permission": "sample_app.api.check_app_permission",
    }
]

docs.title: App lifecycle (install, migrate, build, tests)
docs.text:
All keys in this table are lists of dotted paths. "Per app" keys run only the hooks of the app that the event is about.

Key Read in Called with Description before_install frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Runs before the app is installed. If a function returns False, the install stops. after_install frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Runs after the app's DocTypes sync. after_sync frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Runs at the end of install_app, after fixtures sync. before_app_install frappe/installer.py app_name All apps. Runs before any app is installed. after_app_install frappe/installer.py app_name All apps. Runs after any app is installed. before_uninstall frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Runs before the app is removed. after_uninstall frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Runs after the app is removed. before_app_uninstall frappe/installer.py app_name All apps. Runs before any app is removed. after_app_uninstall frappe/installer.py app_name All apps. Runs after any app is removed. before_migrate frappe/migrate.py nothing Per app, for every installed app. Runs at the start of bench migrate. after_migrate frappe/migrate.py nothing Per app, for every installed app. Runs at the end of bench migrate. after_build frappe/commands/utils.py nothing Per app. Runs after bench build for the apps that were built. after_app_build frappe/commands/utils.py list of built apps Per app, for every app on the bench. Runs after a build. before_tests frappe/test_runner.py, frappe/parallel_test_runner.py nothing Per app. Runs before the tests of the app. bench run-tests --skip-before-tests skips it. never_skip_patches frappe/modules/patch_handler.py not called Patch paths that bench migrate --skip-failing cannot skip. fixtures frappe/utils/fixtures.py, frappe/translate.py not called Records to export with bench export-fixtures and import on migrate. Items are DocType names or dicts with doctype, filters, or_filters. 
# sample_app/hooks.py
after_install = "sample_app.setup.install.after_install"
after_migrate = ["sample_app.setup.install.sync_defaults"]
fixtures = [{"doctype": "Custom Field", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]}]

docs.title: Keys that frappe declares but does not read
docs.text:
frappe/hooks.py sets email_append_to, otp_methods and require_type_annotated_api_methods. No code in v15 reads them through get_hooks. jenv is deprecated. A v13 patch only prints a warning when an app sets it. Use jinja.

Version

These hooks exist only in later versions: before_login, on_social_login, extend_doctype_class, workflow_methods, after_file_upload, storage_drivers, before_enable, after_enable, before_disable, after_disable, require_type_annotated_api_methods (read), use_json_request_body, send_sms, send_token_via_sms, doctype_kanban_js. Setting them in a v15 app does nothing.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A key with a typo does nothing and gives no error. Check the value with frappe.get_hooks("<key>").
  • Merged hooks are cached. Run bench --site <site> clear-cache after you change hooks.py.
  • For "last wins" keys, the app install order decides which app wins.
  • A has_permission hook that returns True stops the hooks of the apps installed before it. Return None when your app has no opinion.

docs.title: Site Config Reference
docs.text: This page lists every key in site_config.json and common_site_config.json that the framework reads in v15. For how the two files merge, how to set keys and how environment variables override them, see Configuration.

docs.title: How to read this page
docs.text:
• Frappe reads sites/common_site_config.json first, then sites/<site>/site_config.json. A site key overrides a common key with the same name. The result is frappe.conf (same object as frappe.local.conf).
  • Scope "Common" means the key is read without a site (through frappe.get_common_site_config(), frappe.get_conf() outside a site, or the Node realtime server). Set it in common_site_config.json. "Site" keys work in either file.
  • "Default" is the value the code uses when the key is missing. An empty cell means the feature is off or the value is empty.
  • Set a key with bench --site <site> set-config <key> <value>, or bench set-config -g <key> <value> for the common file. Add -p to parse the value as a Python literal.
bench --site frappe.localhost set-config developer_mode 1
bench set-config -g redis_cache "redis://127.0.0.1:13000"
bench --site frappe.localhost set-config -p allow_cors '["https://app.example.com"]'

In code, read a key from frappe.conf. A missing key returns None.

frappe.conf.developer_mode      # 1 or None
frappe.conf.get("max_file_size")

docs.title: Database
docs.text: Key Scope Default Description db_type Site mariadb mariadb or postgres. Env: FRAPPE_DB_TYPE. db_name Site Database name. Frappe also uses it as the database user. db_password Site Database password. db_host Site 127.0.0.1 Database host. Env: FRAPPE_DB_HOST. db_port Site 3306 (MariaDB) or 5432 (Postgres) Database port. Env: FRAPPE_DB_PORT. db_socket Site Unix socket path. Env: FRAPPE_DB_SOCKET. db_schema Site public Postgres schema. db_ssl_ca Site MariaDB: CA file. Turns on SSL. db_ssl_cert, db_ssl_key Site MariaDB: client certificate and key. Both are needed. db_ssl_check_hostname Site MariaDB: check the server host name in SSL. read_from_replica Site Send read-only requests and frappe.read_only code to the replica. replica_host Site Host of the read replica. replica_db_port Site Port of the read replica. different_credentials_for_replica Site Use replica_db_name (as the user) and replica_db_password for the replica. replica_db_name, replica_db_password Site Replica credentials. max_writes_per_transaction Site 200000 Max write queries in one transaction before Frappe raises an error. enable_db_statement_timeout Site Set a query timeout: 1.5 x http_timeout for requests, 1.5 x job timeout for jobs. http_timeout Site 300 Request timeout in seconds, used for the statement timeout. rds_db Site On new site, grant a limited privilege set instead of ALL PRIVILEGES (for Amazon RDS). root_login Common root (MariaDB) Database root user for new-site, drop-site, restore. Only the Postgres setup reads this key. It asks for the user when the key is missing. root_password Common Database root password. When missing, Frappe asks for it.

Env: FRAPPE_REDIS_CACHE. redis_queue Common redis://127.0.0.1:11311 Redis URL for job queues and realtime. Env: FRAPPE_REDIS_QUEUE. redis_cache_sentinel_enabled Common Use Redis Sentinel for the cache. redis_cache_sentinels Common [] List of "host:port" Sentinel nodes. redis_cache_master_service Common Sentinel master name. redis_cache_sentinel_username, redis_cache_sentinel_password Common Sentinel credentials. redis_cache_master_username, redis_cache_master_password Common Master credentials. redis_queue_sentinel_enabled, redis_queue_sentinels, redis_queue_master_service, redis_queue_sentinel_username, redis_queue_sentinel_password, redis_queue_master_username, redis_queue_master_password Common Same as the redis_cache_* keys, for the queue. use_rq_auth Common Connect to the queue with a Redis ACL user. rq_username, rq_password Common rq_username: the bench id Redis ACL credentials. bench create-rq-users writes them. bench_id Common bench path with / replaced by - Bench identifier. workers Common {} Custom queues: {"<queue>": {"timeout": <seconds>}}. max_queued_jobs Site 500 Max jobs in a queue before enqueue fails. rq_failed_jobs_limit Site 1000 Max failed jobs kept in the failed registry. rq_job_failure_ttl Site 604800 (7 days) Seconds RQ keeps failed jobs. rq_results_ttl Site 600 Seconds RQ keeps job results. background_process_niceness Common 10 Nice increment for worker and scheduler processes. disable_scheduler Site Do not enqueue scheduled jobs for this site. pause_scheduler Site Pause the scheduler (set by bench scheduler pause). scheduler_tick_interval Common 60 Seconds between scheduler ticks. scheduler_interval Site 240 Seconds between runs of all events. Rounded down to whole minutes in the cron format. maintenance_mode Site Requests stop with SessionStopped, or run read-only (next key). Scheduled jobs do not run. Set by bench set-maintenance-mode. allow_reads_during_maintenance Site In maintenance mode, run requests in read-only mode instead of stopping them.

docs.text: Key Scope Default Description default_site Common Site for commands without --site. Set by bench use. Env: FRAPPE_SITE. webserver_port Common Port of bench serve. Added to site URLs in development. The realtime server calls the web server on this port. webserver_host Common Host the realtime server uses to call the web server. http_port Site Port added to site URLs. Sent to the browser in boot for live reload. host_name Site Base URL of the site, for example https://erp.example.com. docs.title: Frappe Cloud and telemetry
docs.text:
These keys are set by Frappe Cloud. You do not set them on a self-hosted site.

Key Scope Description fc_communication_secret, fc_base_url, saas_billing_site_name Site Billing. fc_base_url and saas_billing_site_name apply in developer mode only. subscription Site Subscription data sent in boot. fc_team, pulse_api_key, pulse_host, pulse_ingest_endpoint Site Telemetry client. push_relay_server_url Site Relay server for push notifications.

Version

These later-version keys are not read in v15: allowed_referrers, client_cache_max_bytes, file_chunk_size, storage_v2 and the storage_* keys, the chromium_* keys, db_user, mariadb_root_*, postgres_root_*, socketio_worker_threads, smtp_no_ehlo_after_auth, use_ssl, esbuild_target. The FRAPPE_DB_NAME, FRAPPE_DB_USER and FRAPPE_DB_PASSWORD environment variables are not read either.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A process reads the config when it calls frappe.init. Restart the web server and workers after you change Redis or database keys.
  • A key in site_config.json hides the same key in common_site_config.json.
  • Without allow_reads_during_maintenance, maintenance mode stops all requests, not only writes.
  • The auth_method key for the site config email account is not read. The code passes ("auth_method"), a string, not a tuple, so it looks up each character.

docs.title: DocTypes Reference
docs.text:
This page lists every DocType that the frappe app ships, grouped by module. Use it to find the exact DocType name and its module. The list is generated from frappe/*/doctype/*/*.json. It has 275 DocTypes, the same as the count of non-custom DocTypes on a v15 site.

Flags come from the DocType JSON:

Flag JSON property Meaning single issingle One record only. Values are in tabSingles. child istable Child table. Rows belong to a parent document. submittable is_submittable Has Submit and Cancel (docstatus). tree is_tree Nested set tree with lft and rgt. virtual is_virtual No table. The controller supplies the data.

For child tables, the description names the parent DocType and the Table field. See DocTypes for how DocTypes work.

docs.title: Core (94)
docs.text: DocType Flags Description Access Log Log of exports, prints and report downloads by users. Activity Log Log of logins, logouts and other activity. Amended Document Naming Settings child Child table of Document Naming Settings (amend_naming_override). Audit Trail single Tool to compare versions of a document over a date range. Block Module child Child table of Module Profile (block_modules), User (block_modules). Comment Comments, likes, assignments and other timeline entries of a document. docs.title: Field Types
docs.text: The fieldtype of a DocField sets the database column, the desk control and the validation of a field. Use this page to choose a fieldtype and to set its options. The list of fieldtypes comes from the fieldtype options in frappe/core/doctype/docfield/docfield.json. Column types come from setup_type_map() of each database class. MariaDB column types were checked with SHOW COLUMNS on a v15 site.

docs.title: How a column is built
docs.text:
get_definition() in frappe/database/schema.py turns a DocField into a column type:

  • Currency, Float and Percent get decimal(length, precision). The default is decimal(21,9). If precision is greater than length, it is set to length.
  • A length on a varchar field changes the size. Values below 64 become 64.
  • An Int field with length above 11 becomes Long Int (bigint). On MariaDB, a length below 11 sets int(length).
  • Check and Int columns are NOT NULL with default 0 if none is set. Currency, Float and Percent are the same. These are the only NOT NULL value columns.
  • A default adds a column default, unless it is a shortcut such as Today or starts with :.
  • unique = 1 adds a unique constraint, except for text and longtext columns.
