  • Hooks

docs.title: Views
docs.text: A view shows the documents of one DocType in a different form. The list view is the default view. Other views show the same documents as a table, a board, a calendar and more.

docs.title: Switch view
docs.text:
1. Open the list of a DocType.
  2. Click the view switcher at the top right. It shows the name of the current view, for example List View.
  3. Click a view.

Some views have more than one board or calendar. Select one in the view's own dropdown. For example, Report View has Select Report in the sidebar, Calendar View has Select Calendar in the sidebar, and Kanban View has Select Kanban in the page header.

The URL of a view is /app/<doctype-slug>/view/<view>, for example /app/sample-item/view/report.

The switcher shows only the views that the DocType supports:

View Shows when List View Always. Report View Always. Dashboard View Always. Kanban View Always, except for File. Calendar View, Gantt View The DocType has calendar settings (frappe.views.calendar["<DocType>"]), for example from <doctype>_calendar.js. Image View The DocType has an Image Field. Tree View The DocType is a tree (Is Tree), or has tree settings in <doctype>_tree.js. Map View The DocType has a Geolocation field named location, or fields named latitude and longitude, or list settings with get_coords_method. Inbox View DocType Communication, and you have an email account.

If View Switcher (view_switcher) is off on your User, the switcher does not show.

docs.title: Report View
docs.text:
Report View shows documents in a table, like a spreadsheet. Use it to pick columns, edit values in cells, group rows and export data.

  • Filters and sort work the same as in the list view. The row under the header filters each column. For numbers, use >5, <10, =324 or a range such as 5:10.
  • Double-click a cell to edit the value. The change saves at once. You can edit a cell only if you have write permission, the field is not read only, and the document is not submitted or cancelled. A field with Allow on Submit stays editable after submit.
  • Click a column header menu to sort, remove or move the column, or to add a column before it.
  • Click Add Group to group rows by a field. Select an aggregate: Count, Sum or Average.

The ... menu of Report View has these items:

Item What it does Show Totals Adds a row with column totals. Print Prints the rows as shown. Toggle Chart Shows or hides a chart of the data. Toggle Sidebar Hides or shows the sidebar. Pick Columns Selects columns, also from child tables. Export Exports the rows. Shows if you can export the DocType. Setup Auto Email Sends the saved report by email on a schedule. Save the report first. Save Saves changes to the current saved report. Save As Saves the current columns, filters and sort as a new report. Delete Deletes the saved report. List Settings Opens the list settings of the DocType. Shows for a System Manager.

A saved report is a Report document of type Report Builder. Open it from Select Report in the sidebar. Refer to Reports.

docs.title: Kanban View
docs.text:
A kanban board shows documents as cards in columns. Each column is one value of a Select field. Drag a card to another column to change the value.

To create a board:

  1. Open the view switcher and click Kanban View. If the DocType has boards, select Create New Kanban Board in Select Kanban.
  2. Type a Kanban Board Name.
  3. In Columns based on, select a Select field, for example Category.
  4. Click Save.

If the DocType has no Select field, the dialog asks you to add one with Customize Form. Boards for Note and ToDo are private (private = 1).

On the board:

  • Click + Add Sample Item at the top of a column to create a document in that column.
  • Click a card to open the document. Click + on a card to assign it.
  • Click + Add Column to add a column. The column menu (...) has Archive and a color for the column.
  • Click Filter to filter the cards. Click ... > Save filters to keep them in the board.
  • Click ... > Kanban Settings to set Show Labels and the fields shown on cards.
  • Click ... > Delete Kanban Board to delete the board.

A board is a Kanban Board document (kanban_board_name, reference_doctype, field_name, columns, filters, private, fields, show_labels).

docs.title: Calendar View
docs.text:
Calendar View shows documents on a calendar by their date fields. Frappe has calendars for Event and ToDo.

  • Click Month, Week or Day to change the range. Click Today to go to today.
  • Select or drag across time slots to create a new document.
  • Drag an event to change its dates.
  • Click Hide Weekends or Show Weekends.

To make one more calendar for a DocType, create a Calendar View document. Set the Reference Document Type, Subject Field, Start Date Field and End Date Field. Select it in Select Calendar in the sidebar.

docs.title: Gantt View
docs.text: Gantt View shows documents as bars on a timeline. It uses the same start and end fields as the calendar. Drag a bar to change the dates.

docs.title: Tree View
docs.text:
Tree View shows a tree DocType as nested nodes. Click a node to expand it.

  • Expand All and Collapse All expand or collapse all nodes.
  • The node menu has Edit (or Details without write permission), Add Child, Rename and Delete.
  • The ... menu has View List, Print, Refresh and Rebuild Tree.

docs.title: Dashboard View
docs.text:
Dashboard View shows charts and number cards for the DocType, for example /app/sample-item/view/dashboard.

  1. Click ... > Customize Dashboard. If the dashboard is empty, click Customize in the page.
  2. Add, remove or move charts and cards.
  3. Click Save Customizations to keep the changes, or Discard to drop them.

Your layout is saved in your user settings. To go back to the default, click ... > Reset Dashboard Customizations. Refer to Dashboards.

docs.title: Image View
docs.text: Image View shows documents as a grid of images from the Image Field of the DocType. For example, open /app/user/view/image to see users with their photos.

docs.title: Map View
docs.text: Map View shows documents as markers on a map. It reads the location Geolocation field, or the latitude and longitude fields.

docs.title: Inbox View
docs.text: Inbox View shows Communication documents of your email account as an inbox. Select the email account in the sidebar. Refer to Email.

docs.title: For developers
Related
docs.text:
• List view
  • Reports
  • Dashboards
  • List view settings

docs.title: Customization
docs.text:
Change forms and fields without code, and define document workflows.

Page What it covers Customize Form Change the fields, layout and properties of a standard DocType from the desk with Customize Form, Custom Field and Property Setter. Workflow Move documents through approval states with Workflow, Workflow State, transitions, conditions and Workflow Action.

docs.title: Customize Form
docs.text: Use Customize Form to change a standard DocType on one site without editing the app code. You can add fields, hide or reorder fields, change labels and other field properties, and change DocType settings such as the title field or the sort order. Your changes survive app updates, because Frappe stores them in two separate DocTypes: Custom Field and Property Setter.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Record DocType What it stores Name format New field Custom Field A field that you add to a DocType. Frappe adds a column to the database table. <DocType>-<fieldname>, for example ToDo-custom_sample_ref Changed property Property Setter One changed property of a DocType, a field, a link, an action or a state. <DocType>-<field or row or "main">-<property>, for example ToDo-priority-reqd
  • When you add a field and do not give a fieldname, Frappe makes one from the label and adds the prefix custom_. A label "Sample Ref" gives custom_sample_ref.
  • Property Setter doctype_or_field ("Applied On") is one of DocField, DocType, DocType Link, DocType Action or DocType State.
  • Frappe merges Custom Fields and Property Setters into the DocType meta when it loads the meta (frappe.get_meta).
  • Only users with the System Manager role can use Customize Form.

docs.title: What you cannot customize
docs.text:
Customize Form rejects these DocTypes:

  • Core DocTypes in frappe.model.core_doctypes_list, for example DocType, User, Role, Report, Print Format, Custom Field and Property Setter. The error is "Core DocTypes cannot be customized."
  • Single DocTypes. The error is "Single DocTypes cannot be customized."
  • Custom DocTypes (DocTypes with custom set, such as Sample Item). The error is "Only standard DocTypes are allowed to be customized from Customize Form." The Customize menu item opens the DocType form for these instead, where you edit the DocType directly.

docs.title: Open Customize Form
docs.text:
1. Open the list or a form of the DocType, for example ToDo.
  2. Open the menu (the ... button).
  3. Select Customize. In the list view the shortcut is Ctrl+J.

You can also go to /app/customize-form and select the DocType in Enter Form Type (doc_type).

The form has two tabs:

  • Details shows the DocType properties, the Fields table, and the Document Actions, Document Links and Document States tables.
  • Form shows the form builder. Drag fields, sections, columns and tabs to change the layout. Click a field to edit its properties in the right panel. Click Add field to add a Custom Field.

Click Show Preview to see the form as users see it. Click Update to save. Frappe then creates or updates the Custom Fields and Property Setters, updates the database table if a column changed, and clears the cache of the DocType.

docs.title: Add a field
docs.text:
1. Open Customize Form for ToDo.
  2. In the Form tab, click Add field in the column where you want the field.
  3. Select the field type and enter the label, for example "Sample Ref".
  4. Set other properties in the right panel, for example Mandatory or In List View.
  5. Click Update.

To delete a Custom Field, remove it in the form builder and click Update. You cannot delete a standard field. Hide it instead.

docs.title: Change a standard field
docs.text:
You can change properties of standard fields, for example the label, Hidden, Mandatory, Read Only, In List View, Default, Depends On and the permission level. Each changed property becomes one Property Setter.

Frappe limits field type changes. You can change the type only inside a group of compatible types (ALLOWED_FIELDTYPE_CHANGE in frappe/custom/doctype/customize_form/customize_form.py). If the new type is shorter and saved values are too long, Frappe shows "Data Too Long" and lists the documents.

docs.title: DocType properties
docs.text:
These properties are in the Details tab. The list is not complete.

Label Fieldname Description Change Label (via Custom Translation) label Shows another name for the DocType. Frappe saves it as a Translation record. Search Fields search_fields Fields that Link field search also looks in. Title Field title_field Field shown as the document title. Show Title in Link Fields show_title_field_in_link Shows the title, not the name, in Link fields. Image Field image_field Field used as the document image. Quick Entry quick_entry Opens a small dialog for new documents. Track Changes track_changes Saves a Version record for each change. Track Views track_views Logs who opened a document. Allow Import (via Data Import Tool) allow_import Allows Data Import for this DocType. Allow Auto Repeat allow_auto_repeat Adds an auto_repeat Custom Field so documents can repeat. Max Attachments max_attachments Maximum number of attachments per document. Naming Rule / Auto Name naming_rule, autoname How new documents get a name. Default Print Format default_print_format Print format used by default. Default View default_view View that opens from the sidebar, for example List or Report. Sort Field / Sort Order sort_field, sort_order Default sort of the list view. Allow document creation via Email email_append_to Creates documents from incoming email.

docs.title: Actions menu
docs.text:
The Actions button has these items:

Item What it does Go to {DocType} List Opens the list view. Not shown for child tables. Set Permissions Opens the Role Permissions Manager for this DocType. Reload Loads the current customizations again. Reset Layout Deletes the Property Setters for field_order and insert_after. Reset All Customizations Deletes all Property Setters and Custom Fields of the DocType that are not system generated. Property Setters for naming_series and options stay. Trim Table Removes database columns that no field uses anymore. You cannot undo this. Export Customizations Shown only in developer mode. See below.

To customize a child table, use Customize Child Table and select the table.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
Do not ask users to repeat customizations on each site. Ship them with your app.

Export from the desk. In developer mode, click Actions > Export Customizations. Select a module. Frappe writes the Custom Fields, Property Setters and links to <module>/custom/<doctype>.json in your app, and does the same for each child table. If Sync on Migrate is set, bench migrate applies the file on each site. If Export Custom Permissions is set, the file also holds the Custom DocPerm rules. Migrate then deletes the Custom DocPerm rules of the DocType and inserts the ones from the file.

Create them in code. Use create_custom_fields in an install hook or a patch. It creates the fields that do not exist and updates the ones that do.

# sample_app/setup.py
from frappe.custom.doctype.custom_field.custom_field import create_custom_fields
from frappe.custom.doctype.property_setter.property_setter import make_property_setter


def after_install():
    create_custom_fields(
        {
            "ToDo": [
                {
                    "fieldname": "sample_ref",
                    "label": "Sample Ref",
                    "fieldtype": "Data",
                    "insert_after": "description",
                }
            ]
        }
    )
    make_property_setter("ToDo", "priority", "reqd", 1, "Check")
  • create_custom_fields(custom_fields, ignore_validate=False, update=True) creates the records as Administrator, clears the cache and updates the table.
  • make_property_setter(doctype, fieldname, property, value, property_type, for_doctype=False, ...) ignores permissions. Set for_doctype=True for a DocType property.
  • You can also export Custom Field and Property Setter records with the fixtures hook. See Fixtures and Patches and Extending Apps.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A field type change that makes a column smaller can fail if saved values are too long.
  • Many fields can hit the database row size limit. Frappe then shows "Database Table Row Size Limit".
  • Reset All Customizations also removes Custom Fields that other users added. Export them first if you need them.
  • Customizations that an app ships with is_system_generated set stay after a reset.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Role Permissions Manager
  • Form View
  • Extending Apps
  • DocTypes

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: A Workflow controls how a document moves from one state to the next, and which role can move it. Use it when a document needs review or approval before it is submitted, for example "Pending" to "Approved". When a workflow applies to a document, the form shows an Actions menu instead of the standard Submit and Cancel buttons.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Term DocType Meaning Workflow Workflow The rule set for one DocType: states and transitions. State Workflow State A named stage, for example "Pending". It has an optional icon and button style. Action Workflow Action Master A named step a user clicks, for example "Approve". Transition Workflow Transition (child) "From state X, role R can do action A to go to state Y." Workflow Action Workflow Action A to-do record that Frappe creates for users who can act on a document in its current state.

The current state of each document is stored in the field named in Workflow State Field (default workflow_state). If the DocType has no such field, Frappe adds a hidden Custom Field of type Link to Workflow State when you save the workflow.

A DocType has only one active workflow. When you save a workflow with Is Active set, Frappe clears Is Active on all other workflows of that DocType.

docs.title: Create a workflow
docs.text:
1. Go to /app/workflow/new.
  2. Enter a Workflow Name and select the Document Type.
  3. In Document States, add one row for each state.
  4. In Transitions, add one row for each allowed move between states.
  5. Select Is Active.
  6. Save.

You can also edit states and transitions on a canvas in the Workflow Builder (/app/workflow-builder). The builder is marked beta.

docs.title: Document States
docs.text: Field Description State (state) A Workflow State record. Doc Status (doc_status) 0 Draft, 1 Submitted, 2 Cancelled. A non-submittable DocType can only use 0. Only Allow Edit For (allow_edit) The role that can edit the document in this state. Update Field / Update Value Set a field of the document to a fixed value when it enters this state. Is Optional State Do not create Workflow Action records for this state. Send Email On State (send_email) Default on. Send the action email when the document enters this state (needs Send Email Alert on the workflow). Next Action Email Template An Email Template for that email. Message A message to show for this state. Don't Override Status Do not show the workflow state as the list view status.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
Field Description State / Next State The state before and after the action. Action A Workflow Action Master record. Allowed (allowed) The role that can do this action. Allow Self Approval Default on. When off, the document owner cannot do this action. Administrator is always allowed. Send Email To Creator (send_email_to_creator) Default off. When off, the action email is not sent to the document owner. Condition Optional Python expression. The action shows only when it is true.

Transition conditions get doc (the document as a dict) and a limited frappe object: frappe.db.get_value, frappe.db.get_list, frappe.session, and frappe.utils.now_datetime, add_to_date, get_datetime, now.

doc.total > 0 and doc.customer_name != "Customer A"

Frappe checks these rules when it saves a workflow:

  • Each transition must use states from Document States.
  • A transition cannot start from a Cancelled state.
  • A transition cannot go from Submitted (1) back to Draft (0).
  • A transition cannot go from Draft (0) to Cancelled (2).

docs.title: Workflow options
docs.text:
Field Default Description Is Active 0 Only the active workflow applies. Don't Override Status 0 Keep the document status in list view instead of the workflow state. Send Email Alert 0 Email the users who can do the next action. Workflow State Field workflow_state The field that stores the state.

When you save a workflow, Frappe sets the state field of existing documents that have no state yet. It uses the first state row for each docstatus.

docs.title: Use a workflow on a document
docs.text:
1. Open the document.
  2. Click Actions.
  3. Select an action.

The menu shows only the transitions from the current state that your roles allow and whose condition is true. After the action, Frappe saves, submits or cancels the document to match the docstatus of the next state. It also adds a "Workflow" comment to the timeline.

To apply an action to many documents, select them in the list view and use the Actions menu. Fewer than 20 documents run at once. From 20 to 500 documents run in a background job. More than 500 documents are rejected.

docs.title: Workflow Action records
docs.text: After each save, cancel or update after submit, Frappe creates Workflow Action records with status Open for the roles that can do the next transition. The user sees them in the Workflow Action list. When Send Email Alert is on, Frappe also emails these users. The email has links to do the action without logging in to desk. When a user does the action, the records change to Completed.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A user can only change the state with a valid transition. A direct edit of the state field fails with "Workflow State transition not allowed".
  • Data Import cannot insert documents in a state other than the first state.
  • If the state stored on a document is not in the workflow, save fails. Update the workflow or the document.
  • A cancelled state blocks the standard Cancel button. Use a transition to the cancelled state.
  • Activating a second workflow for the same DocType deactivates the first one without a message.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Server API in frappe/model/workflow.py: apply_workflow(doc, action), get_transitions(doc), bulk_workflow_approval(docnames, doctype, action), get_workflow_name(doctype).
  • get_workflow_name(doctype) caches the active workflow name in Redis (workflow hash).
  • process_workflow_actions runs from doc_events for * (on_update, on_cancel, on_trash, on_update_after_submit) in frappe/hooks.py.
from frappe.model.workflow import apply_workflow, get_transitions

doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", "SO-00001")
[t.action for t in get_transitions(doc)]
apply_workflow(doc, "Approve")

docs.title: Data, Reports and Printing
docs.text:
Import and export data, run reports, build dashboards and print documents.

Page What it covers Data Import and Export Insert or update many records from CSV, Excel or Google Sheets with Data Import, map columns, read the import log, and export records with Data Export. Reports Build and save Report Builder reports, run Query and Script Reports, use prepared and snapshot reports for slow reports, and export results to Excel or CSV. Dashboards Show counts and charts with Number Card and Dashboard Chart, group them in a Dashboard, and add them to workspaces. Printing Print documents, download PDFs made with wkhtmltopdf, and design Print Formats with the Print Format Builder, Jinja HTML or raw commands, plus Letter Head and Print Settings.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text: A Number Card shows one number, such as the count of open orders. A Dashboard Chart shows data over time or by group. A Dashboard puts cards and charts on one page. You can also add cards and charts to a workspace. Use them to give users a quick view of the data they work with.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: DocType Route What it is Number Card /app/number-card One number from a DocType, a report or a whitelisted method. Dashboard Chart /app/dashboard-chart A chart from a DocType, a report or a custom source. Dashboard /app/dashboard A named set of charts and cards. Shown at /app/dashboard-view/<name>. Dashboard Chart Source /app/dashboard-chart-source Code in an app that gives data to a Custom chart. Dashboard Settings none Per-user chart setup (chart_config), such as saved chart filters.

docs.title: Make a Number Card
docs.text:
1. Go to /app/number-card/new.
  2. Enter a Label. The label is also the name of the card.
  3. Set Type to Document Type.
  4. Select the Function: Count, Sum, Average, Minimum or Maximum.
  5. Select the Document Type, for example Sample Order.
  6. If the function is not Count, select the number field in Aggregate Function Based On.
  7. Click the filters table and set filters, for example status = Open.
  8. Save.
  9. Click Add Card to Dashboard to put it on a Dashboard.
Field Default Description type Document Type, Report or Custom. function For Document Type. parent_document_type Needed when the Document Type is a child table. report_name, report_field, report_function For Report: the report, the number column, and Sum, Average, Minimum or Maximum. method For Custom: dotted path of a whitelisted method. filters_json Fixed filters. dynamic_filters_json Filters with JavaScript expressions, for example frappe.datetime.get_today(). show_percentage_stats 1 Shows the change from the previous period. stats_time_interval Daily Period for the change: Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Yearly. is_public 0 Makes the card available to all users. color, background_color Card colors. show_full_number 0 Shows the full number instead of a short form.

docs.title: Make a Dashboard Chart
docs.text:
1. Go to /app/dashboard-chart/new.
  2. Enter Chart Name.
  3. Select the Chart Type.
  4. Select the Document Type and set the fields for that chart type.
  5. Select the display Type: Line, Bar, Percentage, Pie, Donut or Heatmap.
  6. Set filters in the filters table.
  7. Save.
  8. Click Add Chart to Dashboard to put it on a Dashboard.
Chart Type Fields to set Result Count Time Series Based On (a date field), Timespan, Time Interval Number of records per period. Sum / Average Same as Count, plus Value Based On Sum or average of a number field per period. Group By Group By Based On, Group By Type (Count, Sum, Average), Number of Groups One value per group, for example per status. Report Report Name, X Field, Y Axis, or Use Report Chart Chart from the data of a report. Custom Chart Source Data from a Dashboard Chart Source in an app.

Timespan can be Last Year, Last Quarter, Last Month, Last Week or Select Date Range. Time Interval can be Yearly, Quarterly, Monthly, Weekly or Daily. Cancelled documents are never counted.

The chart menu on a dashboard has Refresh, Edit, Reset Chart, and a link to the list or report of the source. Chart data is cached. Refresh gets new data and shows the time in Last synced.

docs.title: Make a Dashboard
docs.text:
1. Go to /app/dashboard/new.
  2. Enter Dashboard Name.
  3. Add charts in the Charts table. Set the Width of each chart to Half or Full.
  4. Add cards in the Cards table.
  5. Save.
  6. Click Show Dashboard.

Is Default makes this the default dashboard. Chart Options takes JSON that applies to all charts on the dashboard.

docs.title: Add cards and charts to a workspace
docs.text:
1. Open the workspace.
  2. Click Edit.
  3. Add a Chart block or a Number Card block.
  4. Select an existing chart or card, or make a new one.
  5. Save the workspace.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
• System Managers see all charts and cards.
  • A user sees a Document Type chart or card when they can read its DocType. A Report chart or card needs access to the report.
  • If a chart has rows in its Roles table, a user needs one of those roles.
  • Charts and cards are also limited to the modules the user can see.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• A Custom Number Card calls the whitelisted method in method with filters. Return a number, or a dict with value and the formatting keys such as fieldtype.
  • A Custom chart reads frappe.dashboards.chart_sources["<Source Name>"] from <module>/dashboard_chart_source/<source_name>/<source_name>.js in your app. Set method there to the Python method that returns the chart data.
  • Cards and charts with Is Standard set are exported to the module of the app when you save in developer mode. A standard chart cannot be edited on a site without developer mode.
  • Chart data comes from frappe.desk.doctype.dashboard_chart.dashboard_chart.get and card data from frappe.desk.doctype.number_card.number_card.get_result.
  • Ship charts and cards in a workspace of your app. See Workspaces, Sidebar and Dock.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A Number Card or a chart cannot use a Single DocType.
  • Aggregate Function Based On of a Number Card lists number fields. A Currency field shows only when its options are Company:company:default_currency.
  • A new chart gets the default currency in Currency. A count chart then shows its values as amounts. Clear Currency for count charts.
  • Chart data is cached per chart. Use Refresh after a large data change.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Reports
  • Views
  • Desk
  • Workspaces, Sidebar and Dock

docs.title: Data Import and Export
docs.text: Data Import inserts or updates many records from a CSV or Excel file, or from a public Google Sheet. Data Export downloads records as CSV or Excel. Use them to move data in from another system, to change many records at once, or to get a template to fill in.

docs.title: Before you import
docs.text:
• The DocType must allow import (Allow Import in the DocType or Customize Form).
  • You need the import permission on the DocType.
  • Most core DocTypes cannot be imported. User, Role and Print Format can.
  • The scheduler must be active, because the import runs in a background job. In developer mode, the import runs in the request.

docs.title: Import records
docs.text: Go to /app/data-import/new. You can also open the list view of the DocType and select Import from the menu. This opens the Data Import list for that DocType.

docs.title: 1. Set up the import
docs.text:
1. Select the Document Type.
  2. Select the Import Type.
  3. Save.
  4. Optional: click Download Template to get a file with the right columns.
  5. Attach the file in Import File, or enter a URL in Import from Google Sheets.
Import Type Result Insert New Records Each row makes a new document. Update Existing Records Each row updates the document in the ID column. A row with no change fails with "No changes to update". Option Default Description Don't Send Emails (mute_emails) 1 Do not send emails or notifications during the import. Submit After Import 0 Submit each document. Submittable DocTypes only. Show Only Failed Logs 0 Show only failed rows in the import log.

docs.title: 2. Preview and map columns
docs.text:
After you attach the file, the form shows a preview of the first rows. Frappe matches each column header to a field.

  • Click Map Columns to change which field a column goes to, or select Don't Import to skip a column. Save to apply the change.
  • If a value is not valid, the form shows it in the Import File Errors and Warnings section, grouped by row and column. Fix the file and attach it again.

The import does not start while there are warnings that are not of type info. Frappe saves them in Template Warnings (template_warnings).

docs.title: 3. Import
docs.text:
Click Start Import. Frappe shows the progress, and then the result: how many records were inserted or updated.

  • Frappe commits after each successful row. A failed row does not undo the rows before it.
  • The status of the import becomes Success, Partial Success, Error or Timed Out.
  • If some rows fail, fix the data and click Retry. Rows that were imported before are not imported again.
  • On Partial Success, click Export Errored Rows to get a file with only the failed rows.

docs.title: Import log
docs.text: Each imported or failed row makes a Data Import Log record with the document name, the row numbers, a success flag and the error. The form shows the log in a table with Row Number, Status and Message. Click Export Import Log to download it.

docs.title: Export records
docs.text:
There are two ways to export records.

From a list view: select records, then use Actions > Export. Or click Download Template on the Data Import form. The Export Data dialog has these options:

Option Values File Type Excel or CSV Export Type All Records, Filtered Records, 5 Records or Blank Template Fields The fields of the DocType and its child tables. Use Select Mandatory or Select All.

The exported file has the same format that Data Import reads, so you can edit it and import it with Update Existing Records.

Data Export page: go to /app/data-export. Select the DocType in Select Doctype, the File Type (Excel or CSV), filters and fields, then click Export. Select Export without main header to leave out the header notes and column descriptions.

To export the rows shown in a report, use Export in the menu of the report view. See Reports.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• When you update records, include the ID column. Frappe finds the document by it.
  • In Insert mode, Frappe sets the name from the file only when the DocType uses Prompt naming.
  • A workflow DocType can only import documents in the first workflow state.
  • Child table rows go on the lines below their parent row, with the parent columns empty.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Import from the command line:
bench --site frappe.localhost data-import --file sample-items.csv --doctype "Sample Item" --type Insert

--type is Insert or Update. Add --submit-after-import to submit. The path is relative to the sites folder. The --mute-emails flag is always on and is not passed to the import.

  • Import or export JSON records from code with import_doc(path) and export_json(doctype, path, filters=None) in frappe/core/doctype/data_import/data_import.py. bench import-doc <path> uses import_doc.
  • Rows per batch: data_import_batch_size in site config (default 1000). See Site Config.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• List View
  • Customize Form
  • Permissions
  • CLI

docs.title: Printing
docs.text: Every document in the desk can be printed or saved as a PDF. A Print Format controls what the printed page shows. Use the print view to print a document or download it as a PDF. Make a Print Format when the standard layout does not fit, for example when an invoice needs a custom header or a narrow receipt layout. Frappe v15 makes PDFs with wkhtmltopdf.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: Name DocType What it is Print view page print The preview at /app/print/<DocType>/<name>. You pick the format, language and letter head there. Print Format Print Format A layout for one DocType (or one report). Made in a Print Format Builder, or written as Jinja HTML. Standard format none The layout Frappe makes from the form when no Print Format is selected. Letter Head Letter Head A header and footer (image or HTML) added to the top and bottom of a print. Print Style Print Style Site-wide CSS for printed pages. Standard styles: Redesign, Modern, Classic, Monochrome. Print Settings Print Settings (Single) Site defaults: page size, draft and cancelled printing, raw printing, print server. Print Heading Print Heading A named heading text that a print can show.

docs.title: Print a document
docs.text:
1. Open the document.
  2. Click the print icon in the form toolbar. The print view opens.
  3. In the sidebar, select a Print Format, a Language and a Letter Head.
  4. Click Print to open the browser print dialog.

The toolbar has these buttons:

Button Action Full Page Opens the print in a new tab at /printview. PDF Makes the PDF on the server with wkhtmltopdf and opens it. Refresh Renders the preview again. Form icon Goes back to the form. Print Opens the browser print dialog.

The link Try the new Print Designer opens the Print Designer app if it is installed, or its page on the Frappe Cloud marketplace. The ... menu has Print Settings and Customize, and repeats Full Page, PDF and Refresh. Raw Printing Setting shows when Enable Raw Printing is on in Print Settings. Select Network Printer shows when Enable Print Server is on.

Note

Draft documents print with a "Draft" heading when Always add "Draft" Heading for printing draft documents is on in Print Settings. Cancelled documents print only when Allow Print for Cancelled is on.

docs.title: Make a Print Format with the builder
docs.text:
Frappe v15 has two builders. The classic Print Format Builder (print_format_builder = 1) is at /app/print-format-builder/<name>. The newer builder (print_format_builder_beta = 1) is at /app/print-format-builder-beta/<name>.

To start from the print view:

  1. Open the print view of a document.
  2. Click ... > Customize.
  3. Enter New Print Format Name.
  4. Optional: turn on Use the new Print Format Builder.
  5. Click Start. Frappe makes the Print Format and opens the builder.

If the selected format was made in a builder, Customize opens that format in its builder. If it is a custom HTML format, Customize opens the Print Format form.

To start from the Print Format form, go to /app/print-format/new, select the DocType, keep Custom Format off and save. Then click Edit Format.

docs.title: Classic builder
docs.text:
1. Drag fields from the sidebar onto a section. Drag a field back to the sidebar to remove it.
  2. Click Add a new section to add a section.
  3. Click the gear icon of a section to set No of Columns and Section Heading, or to remove it.
  4. Click Select Columns on a table field to pick the child table columns.
  5. Click Edit Heading to change the heading HTML.
  6. Drag Custom HTML onto the page to add your own Jinja HTML block.
  7. Click Edit Properties to open the Print Format form.
  8. Click Save.

docs.title: New builder
docs.text: The left panel sets Page Margins, Google Font, Font Size and Page Number, and lists the Fields. The fields list also has Custom HTML, ID (name), Spacer and Divider. On the page you can Create Letter Head, Edit Header and Edit Footer. Click Show Preview to see the print of a document. Click Save to keep the change.

docs.title: Write a Jinja Print Format
docs.text:
Use a Jinja format when you need full control of the HTML.

  1. Go to /app/print-format/new and select the DocType.
  2. Turn on Custom Format.
  3. Keep Print Format Type as Jinja.
  4. Write the template in HTML.
  5. Save.
<h2>{{ doc.customer_name }}</h2>
<p>{{ _("Order Date") }}: {{ doc.get_formatted("order_date") }}</p>
<table class="table table-bordered">
  {% for row in doc.items %}
  <tr>
    <td>{{ row.item }}</td>
    <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("qty") }}</td>
    <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("rate", doc) }}</td>
  </tr>
  {% endfor %}
</table>
<p class="text-right">{{ _("Total") }}: {{ doc.get_formatted("total") }}</p>

The template gets doc, meta, layout, no_letterhead, letter_head, footer and print_settings, plus the Jinja globals such as frappe and _. Frappe validates the template on save. Frappe does not validate a format with Print Format Type JS as Jinja.

docs.title: Raw printing
docs.text: For label and receipt printers, turn on Custom Format and Raw Printing, then write printer commands in Raw Commands. Turn on Enable Raw Printing in Print Settings first. The browser sends raw commands to the printer through the QZ Tray client.

docs.title: Print Format for a report
docs.text: Set Print Format For to Report and select the Report. Frappe sets Custom Format for report formats, so you write the HTML yourself.

docs.title: Print Format fields
docs.text: Field Default Description print_format_for DocType DocType or Report. standard No Yes saves the format in the app. Shows only in developer mode. custom_format 0 Write the format as HTML instead of in a builder. print_format_type Jinja Jinja or JS. pdf_generator wkhtmltopdf The only option in v15. default_print_language Language used when the print view opens. margin_top, margin_bottom, margin_left, margin_right 15 Page margins in mm. font_size 14 Font size. page_number Hide Position of the page number. align_labels_right, show_section_headings, line_breaks 0 Layout options for builder formats. absolute_value 0 Show negative numbers without the sign. css Custom CSS for this format. disabled 0 Hides the format.

docs.title: Set the default format
docs.text: • In the Print Format form, click Set as Default. For a custom DocType this sets default_print_format on the DocType. For other DocTypes it makes a Property Setter. The button shows only when you can write Customize Form.

docs.title: Letter Head
docs.text:
1. Go to /app/letter-head/new.
  2. Enter Letter Head Name.
  3. Set Letter Head Based On to Image or HTML.
  4. Add the header Image, or save and then write the Header HTML.
  5. Set Footer Based On and add the footer the same way.
  6. Turn on Default Letter Head to use it when no letter head is picked.

Header and footer HTML are Jinja. They get doc when they render.

docs.title: Print Settings
docs.text:
Go to /app/print-settings.

Field Default Description send_print_as_pdf 1 Attach prints to emails as PDF. repeat_header_footer 1 Repeat the letter head header and footer on each PDF page. pdf_page_size A4 Default PDF page size. Custom shows PDF Page Height (in mm) and PDF Page Width (in mm). with_letterhead 1 Print with the default letter head. allow_print_for_draft 1 Allow printing of draft documents. add_draft_heading 1 Add a "Draft" heading to draft prints. allow_print_for_cancelled 0 Allow printing of cancelled documents. allow_page_break_inside_tables 0 Let a table split across pages. enable_print_server 0 Print to a network printer through Network Printer Settings. enable_raw_printing 0 Allow raw command formats. print_style Redesign Default Print Style. font, font_size Default Default print font and size.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Get the HTML or PDF of a document in Python with frappe.get_print. The PDF engine comes from the pdf_generator field of the format, or wkhtmltopdf.
html = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001", print_format="Sample Order Jinja")
pdf = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001", as_pdf=True)  # bytes
  • Use frappe.attach_print(doctype, name, ...) to get a PDF attachment dict for frappe.sendmail.
  • The download URL is /api/method/frappe.utils.print_format.download_pdf?doctype=...&name=...&format=.... It checks print permission on the document.
  • wkhtmltopdf must be on the PATH of the bench. The print view shows "Invalid wkhtmltopdf version" when it finds a wrong build. Use wkhtmltopdf 0.12.x with patched qt.
  • Add Jinja methods and filters for templates with the jinja hook ({"methods": [...], "filters": [...]}).
  • Add a PDF engine with the pdf_generator hook. frappe.get_print calls each hook function when the engine is not wkhtmltopdf. A function returns the PDF bytes, or None when the engine is not its own. Frappe itself registers no function for this hook.
  • Other hooks: get_print_format_template, on_print_pdf, pdf_header_html, pdf_body_html, pdf_footer_html.
  • A Print Format with Standard = Yes is saved in the app and can be changed only in developer mode. See Print Formats.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A standard Print Format cannot be changed on a site. Duplicate it and edit the copy.
  • A Print Format with Custom Format on needs HTML, or Raw Commands when Raw Printing is on.
  • PDF generation runs wkhtmltopdf as a process on the server. It loads images and styles from the site URL, so the server must be able to reach its own site URL.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text: A report shows records as a table, with filters, totals, charts and export. Frappe has four report types. Use Report Builder to save a column and filter setup of one DocType without code. Use a Query Report or a Script Report when you need joins, calculations or data from many DocTypes. Every report is a Report document.

docs.title: Report types
docs.text:
report_type Who makes it Where it runs Notes Report Builder A user with create permission on Report Report view of one DocType Columns, filters, sort, group by and totals are saved as JSON in the json field. Query Report Script Manager (non-standard) or a developer /app/query-report/<name> One SQL SELECT in the query field. Script Report Script Manager (non-standard) or a developer /app/query-report/<name> Python. In an app: an execute(filters) function. On a site: the Script field. Custom Report Report Manager /app/query-report/<name> A saved copy of a Query or Script Report with its own columns and filters. reference_report points to the original.

A report is Standard (is_standard = Yes) when it is part of an app. A standard report cannot be changed or deleted on a site. Duplicate it, or use Save in the report to make a Custom Report.

docs.title: Make a Report Builder report
docs.text:
1. Open the list of the DocType, for example /app/sample-order.
  2. Switch the view to Report. The URL becomes /app/sample-order/view/report.
  3. Add filters with Filter, and a group with Add Group.
  4. Click a column header to sort or remove the column. Use ... > Pick Columns to add columns, also from child tables.
  5. Click ... > Save As and enter a name.

The new report opens at /app/<doctype>/view/report/<report name>. The page title shows Not Saved after you change it. Click ... > Save to keep the change.

The ... menu of the report view has these items. Some show only when you have the permission.

Item What it does Show Totals Adds a total row for number columns. Print Prints the table. Needs print permission on the DocType. Toggle Chart Shows a chart. Pick the X axis field, Y axis fields and chart type. Toggle Sidebar Shows or hides the sidebar. Pick Columns Selects the columns to show. Export Downloads the rows (see Export). Setup Auto Email Makes an Auto Email Report that sends this report on a schedule. Save / Save As Save updates this report. It shows for a non-standard report when you can write Report or own the report. Save As makes a new report. Delete Deletes the saved report. User Permissions Opens the User Permission list filtered on this saved report. Shows for a System Manager on a saved report. List Settings Opens the list settings of the DocType. Shows for a System Manager.

docs.title: Run a Query or Script Report
docs.text:
1. Search for the report name in the awesomebar, or open /app/query-report/<Report Name>.
  2. Set the filters at the top. The report runs again on each change.
  3. Use the Actions menu or the ... menu for more actions.
Item What it does Refresh Runs the report again. Edit Opens the Report document. Report Managers only. Print Prints the report. PDF Makes a PDF of the report. Export Downloads the data. Setup Auto Email Makes an Auto Email Report. Add Column Adds a column from a linked DocType. User Permissions Opens User Permissions for the report DocType. System Managers only. Save Saves your columns and filters as a Custom Report. Report Managers only. Create Card (Actions) Makes a Number Card from a number column. Needs create permission on Number Card. Set Chart / Add Chart to Dashboard (Actions) Makes a chart from the report and adds it to a Dashboard. Needs create permission on Dashboard Chart.

docs.title: Prepared reports
docs.text:
A prepared report runs in a background job and saves the result. Use it for a report that takes a long time.

  • Turn on Prepared Report (prepared_report) in the Report document.
  • For a Script Report, Frappe turns it on for you when one run takes more than 15 seconds. To stop this, turn on Disable Prepared Report Automation.
  • Timeout (In Seconds) sets the job timeout. The default is 1500 seconds (25 minutes).

When a report is prepared:

  1. Set the filters and click Generate New Report.
  2. Frappe makes a Prepared Report with status Queued. The status changes to Started when a worker picks it up.
  3. When the job ends, the status is Completed or Error. The open report refreshes, or an alert shows a link to the result.
  4. Click Edit to change the filters, or Rebuild to run it again with the same filters.

In a completed Prepared Report document, click Show Report to open the result. Click Download as CSV to make a CSV file in a background job. The file is attached to the Prepared Report and you get a notification.

docs.title: Snapshot reports
docs.text:
A snapshot report reads data from a DuckDB copy of the database instead of the live database. Use it for heavy standard Script Reports.

  1. In System Settings, turn on Enable Snapshot Reports.
  2. Set Frequency to Daily or Weekly (default Weekly). Frappe makes a scheduled job that runs frappe.database.duckdb.database.start_duckdb_sync.
  3. In the standard Script Report, turn on Snapshot Report and add the DocTypes to copy in Doctype To Sync.
  4. In the report module, write execute_snapshot_report(filters). Frappe calls it instead of execute.

The report shows data from the time of the last DuckDB Sync, not live data.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
Export opens a dialog with these options:

Option Default Description File Format Excel Excel or CSV. Export in Background off Makes the file in a background job. CSV Delimiter , CSV only. CSV Quoting Non-numeric Minimal, All, Non-numeric or None. CSV Preview CSV only. Shows the first rows with the current settings.

In a Query or Script Report, the dialog can also show Include indentation (tree reports), Include filters (when filters are set) and Include hidden columns (when the report allows it). In the report view, the dialog also asks if you want to export all matching rows when there are more rows than the page shows, and has Translate values. Export shows only when you have export permission on the DocType.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
• A user can open a report when they can read its Ref DocType and have one of the roles in its Roles table.
  • Non-standard Query and Script Reports can be saved only by a user with the Script Manager role.
  • Disabled hides the report.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Write Query and Script Reports in an app as files in <module>/report/<report_name>/. See Reports (developer).
  • Run a Query or Script Report from code or the API with frappe.desk.query_report.run(report_name, filters).
  • frappe.core.doctype.prepared_report.prepared_report.make_prepared_report(report_name, filters) queues a prepared report.
  • frappe.desk.query_report.save_report(reference_report, report_name, columns, filters) makes a Custom Report.
  • frappe.desk.reportview.save_report(name, doctype, report_settings) saves a Report Builder report.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A Report Builder report works on one DocType and its child tables. Use a Query or Script Report for joins.
  • A prepared report shows the result of the last run, not live data. Check the Finished At time.
  • When Administrator saves a new report in developer mode, Frappe sets is_standard to Yes and writes it to the app.

docs.title: System Administration
docs.text:
Configure the system, take backups and monitor logs and jobs.

Page What it covers System Settings Site-wide settings in System Settings (formats, login, password, email, files, backups, scheduler), plus the basics of Website Settings and Navbar Settings. Backups Take, download, schedule, encrypt and restore site backups with bench, the Download Backups page, and the Dropbox, Google Drive and S3 backup integrations. Logs and Monitoring Find errors and check site health with Error Log, Activity Log, Access Log, Scheduled Job Log, RQ Job, RQ Worker, Recorder, System Health Report, System Console and Log Settings.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: A site backup has up to four files: the database dump, the public files, the private files, and a copy of site_config.json. You take backups with bench backup and restore them with bench restore. System Managers can download recent database backups from the desk, and can send backups to Dropbox, Google Drive or an S3 bucket. Take a backup before each update, and schedule regular backups on production servers.

docs.title: Backup files
docs.text:
Frappe saves backups in sites/<site>/private/backups/. You can change the folder with the backup_path key in site_config.json. File names start with the date and time and the site name, with dots changed to underscores:

File Example name Database 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-database.sql.gz Site config 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-site_config_backup.json Public files 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-files.tar Private files 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-private-files.tar
  • Partial backups (with includes or excludes) have -partial before -database.
  • Encrypted backups have -enc before the extension.
  • With --compress, file archives are .tgz.

docs.title: Take a backup
docs.text:
# database and site config only
bench --site frappe.localhost backup

# also public and private files
bench --site frappe.localhost backup --with-files

# all sites of the bench
bench --site all backup

Options of bench backup:

Option Description --with-files Also back up public and private files. --compress Compress the file archives (.tgz). -i, --include, --only DocTypes to back up, separated by commas. -e, --exclude DocTypes to leave out, separated by commas. --backup-path Folder for all backup files. --backup-path-db, --backup-path-files, --backup-path-private-files, --backup-path-conf Path for each file. --ignore-backup-conf Ignore the includes and excludes in site config. --verbose Print more output. --old-backup-metadata Use the older backup metadata format.

bench backup prints a summary with the path and size of each file.

docs.title: Includes and excludes in site config
docs.text:
To always back up only some DocTypes, or to always leave some out, add a backup key to site_config.json:

{
 "backup": {
  "excludes": ["Version", "Deleted Document"]
 }
}

Use includes for the other case. With includes, Frappe also backs up a set of base tables that a site needs. Frappe skips DocTypes that have no table, without a message. This applies to site config and to --include and --exclude.

docs.title: Schedule backups
docs.text:
Frappe does not take local backups on its own. On a server, use the bench CLI to add a cron job:

bench setup backups

This adds a cron job that runs bench --verbose --site all backup every 6 hours and writes to logs/backup.log.

To send backups off the server on a schedule, use one of the backup integrations.

docs.title: Old backups
docs.text:
Frappe deletes old backups in two ways:

  • Each new backup first deletes all files in the backup folder that are older than 23 hours. Set keep_backups_for_hours in site config to change this.
  • An hourly job (frappe.desk.page.backups.backups.delete_downloadable_backups, in hourly_maintenance) keeps the newest Number of Backups (backup_limit, default 3) sets and deletes the rest.

Copy backups to another server or storage if you need to keep them longer.

docs.title: Download backups from the desk
docs.text:
1. Go to Download Backups (/app/backups). You need the System Manager role.
  2. Click a backup to download the database file.

The page shows the newest database backups, up to Number of Backups. Each download makes an Access Log entry. The buttons are:

Button What it does Set Number of Backups Opens System Settings at Number of Backups. Download Files Backup Queues a backup with files on the long queue. Frappe emails you the download links when it is done. Get Backup Encryption Key Shows the encryption key after you confirm your password.

docs.title: Encrypt backups
docs.text:
1. Go to System Settings > Backups.
  2. Set Encrypt Backups (encrypt_backup).
  3. Save.

Frappe then encrypts the database and file archives with gpg. The gpg program must be installed on the server. The key is backup_encryption_key in site_config.json. Frappe creates it the first time it needs it. Store the key outside the server. Without it, you cannot restore an encrypted backup.

docs.title: Restore a backup
docs.text:
Warning

bench restore replaces the whole database of the site. Take a backup of the site first.

bench --site frappe.localhost restore \
  sites/frappe.localhost/private/backups/20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-database.sql.gz \
  --with-public-files sites/frappe.localhost/private/backups/20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-files.tar \
  --with-private-files sites/frappe.localhost/private/backups/20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-private-files.tar
  • If the path does not exist, bench restore also looks in sites/<site>/private/backups and in the bench folder.
  • For an encrypted file, Frappe uses --encryption-key. Without it, Frappe uses backup_encryption_key in site config. If decryption fails, the restore stops.
  • --admin-password sets the Administrator password after the restore.
  • Frappe asks you to confirm when the backup comes from a newer version of Frappe. --force skips this check and the SQL file validation.
  • Other options: --db-root-username, --db-root-password, --db-name and --install-app.
  • Run bench --site <site> migrate after a restore from an older version.

A partial backup cannot be restored with bench restore. Use bench --site <site> partial-restore <file>. It restores only the tables in the file, into the existing site.

docs.title: Backup integrations
docs.text:
Frappe has three Single DocTypes that send backups to remote storage. Each has a Take Backup Now button (Take Backup for Google Drive). The scheduled jobs are in the scheduler_events hook of frappe/hooks.py. Each job runs only when the integration is enabled and the frequency matches. If a backup fails, Frappe emails the notification address. Send Email for Successful Backup also sends an email on success. It is on by default for Dropbox and S3, and off for Google Drive.

DocType Route Frequency options Jobs Dropbox Settings /app/dropbox-settings Daily, Weekly daily_maintenance, weekly_long Google Drive /app/google-drive Daily, Weekly daily_maintenance, weekly_long S3 Backup Settings /app/s3-backup-settings Daily, Weekly, Monthly, None daily_maintenance, weekly_long, monthly_long

docs.title: Dropbox
docs.text:
1. Go to Dropbox Settings.
  2. Select Enabled.
  3. Enter Send Notifications To.
  4. Select the Backup Frequency.
  5. Enter App Access Key and App Secret Key of your Dropbox app. You can also set dropbox_access_key and dropbox_secret_key in site config.
  6. Save.
  7. Click Allow Dropbox Access.
  8. Approve the access in Dropbox.

Frappe uploads the database backup and the site config to the /database folder. If File Backup (default on) is set, it also uploads public files to /files and private files to /private/files. Set Limit Number of DB Backups and Number of DB Backups (default 5) to delete older database backups in Dropbox.

docs.title: Google Drive
docs.text:
1. Enable Google in Google Settings (/app/google-settings) first. See Integrations.
  2. Go to Google Drive.
  3. Select Enable.
  4. Enter the Backup Folder Name.
  5. Select the Frequency.
  6. Enter Send Notification To.
  7. Save.
  8. Click Authorize Google Drive Access.
  9. Approve the access in Google.

Frappe creates the backup folder in Google Drive and saves its ID in Backup Folder ID. Set File Backup to also upload the files. Last Backup On shows the time of the last upload.

docs.title: S3
docs.text:
Label Fieldname Default Description Enable Automatic Backup enabled 0 Turns on the scheduled backups. Send Notifications To notify_email Required. Backup Frequency frequency Daily, Weekly, Monthly or None. Required. Access Key ID / Access Key Secret access_key_id, secret_access_key Credentials. Required. Endpoint URL endpoint_url https://s3.amazonaws.com Change it for other S3-compatible storage. Bucket Name bucket Required. Backup Files backup_files 1 Also uploads public and private files. Backup Path backup_path Folder in the bucket. Empty means the root of the bucket.

On save, Frappe checks that it can open the bucket. It shows "Bucket {0} not found." or "Do not have permission to access bucket {0}." if the check fails. Each backup goes to a folder named after the date and time of the backup.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.backups import new_backup

odb = new_backup(ignore_files=True, force=True)
print(odb.backup_path_db)
  • frappe.utils.backups.new_backup(...) takes a backup and returns the BackupGenerator. Without force=True, it reuses a complete backup set (database, files, private files and config) from the last 6 hours if one exists.
  • frappe.utils.backups.fetch_latest_backups() returns the paths of the latest backups. It needs System Manager.
  • Site config keys: backup, backup_path, keep_backups_for_hours, backup_encryption_key, dropbox_access_key and dropbox_secret_key. See Site Config reference.
