docs.title: Logs and Monitoring
docs.text: Frappe records errors, logins, data access, scheduled job runs and background jobs in log DocTypes. Use them to find out why something failed, who did what, and whether workers and the scheduler run. Use the Recorder and the System Health Report to look at performance and the state of the site. Most of these DocTypes need the System Manager role.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: DocType Route What it records Error Log /app/error-log Unhandled exceptions and errors logged by code. Activity Log /app/activity-log Login, logout and impersonation. Access Log /app/access-log Exports, printed documents, report views, private file and backup downloads. Scheduled Job Log /app/scheduled-job-log One row per run of a scheduled job. RQ Job /app/rq-job Background jobs in Redis queues. RQ Worker /app/rq-worker Background workers that run now. Recorder /app/recorder Requests and jobs with their SQL queries, while recording is on. System Health Report /app/system-health-report A live summary of workers, scheduler, database, cache, email and errors.

docs.title: Error Log
docs.text:
Frappe adds an Error Log for each unhandled exception in a request or a background job. Code can also add one with frappe.log_error.

Label Fieldname Description Title method Short description, often the last line of the traceback. Error error Full traceback. Reference DocType / Reference Name reference_doctype, reference_name The document the error is about, if known. Seen seen Set when a user opens the log. The list shows "Seen" or "Not Seen". Trace ID trace_id ID of the request or job.

When the log has a reference document, the form shows Show Related Errors. It lists the Error Logs of the same document.

During read-only requests, Frappe queues the Error Log in Redis and inserts it later (deferred_insert). Clear Error Logs in the list menu deletes all Error Logs.

docs.title: Activity Log and Access Log
docs.text:
Activity Log has Operation (operation: Login, Logout or Impersonate), Status (status), User, IP Address and Subject. Failed logins also show here. Use it to audit who logged in and from where.

Access Log has User, Export From, Reference Document, Report Name, Filters, File Type, Method and Timestamp. Use it to see who exported or printed data.

docs.title: Scheduled Job Log
docs.text: Each run of a scheduled job adds a row with Scheduled Job (scheduled_job_type), Status (Scheduled, Complete or Failed) and Details (the traceback if it failed). Open the Scheduled Job Type to see the frequency and the last run. See Scheduler.

docs.title: RQ Job and RQ Worker
docs.text:
RQ Job and RQ Worker are virtual DocTypes. They read the jobs and workers from Redis. Nothing is saved in the database.

RQ Job fields: Job ID, Job Name, Queue (default, short or long), Status (queued, started, finished, failed, deferred, scheduled or canceled), Timeout, Time Taken, Arguments and Exception.

  • The list shows "Scheduler: Active" or "Scheduler: Inactive". If inactive, use Actions > Enable Scheduler.
  • Actions > Remove Failed Jobs deletes all failed jobs of the site.
  • On a job with status started or queued, Force Stop job stops it.

RQ Worker shows Queue(s), Status, Current Job ID, Successful Job Count, Failed Job Count, Last Heartbeat and Utilization %. If the list is empty, no worker runs. See Background Jobs.

docs.title: Recorder
docs.text:
The Recorder captures web requests and background jobs with their SQL queries, timings, call stacks and EXPLAIN output. Only Administrator can use it.

  1. Go to Recorder (/app/recorder).
  2. Click Start.
  3. In Configure Recorder, set the options.
  4. Click Start Recording.
  5. Do the slow action in another tab.
  6. Click Stop.
  7. Open a row to see its queries.

Option Default Description Record Web Requests / Request path filter on, / Records requests whose path starts with the filter. Record Background Jobs / Background Jobs filter on, empty Records jobs whose name matches the filter. Empty records all. Record SQL queries on Generate EXPLAIN for SQL queries on Capture callstack of SQL queries on Run cProfile off Adds Python profile output. It is slow.

Recording stops on its own after 5 minutes. On a recorded request, Suggest Optimizations proposes database indexes, and Add Indexes adds the ones you select. Use Clear to delete all recordings. Export and Import in the menu move recordings between sites.

From the command line, use bench --site <site> start-recording and bench --site <site> stop-recording.

docs.title: System Health Report
docs.text:
Open System Health Report (/app/system-health-report). Frappe builds the report each time you open it. It does not save it.

Section What it shows Background Jobs Number of workers, pending jobs per queue, worker use. Background Jobs Check runs a test job and shows its status. Scheduler Scheduler Status, the Oldest Unscheduled Job, and Failing Scheduled Jobs (last 7 days). Database Database type and version, storage use, Storage Usage By Table. MariaDB Variables Bufferpool Size and Binary Logging. Cache Number of keys and Memory Usage of Redis. Realtime (SocketIO) SocketIO Ping Check and SocketIO Transport Mode. File Storage and Backups Size of public and private files, number and size of backups on the server. Users Total users, new users and failed logins in the last 30 days, active sessions, last 10 active users. Emails Outgoing, pending, failed, handled and unhandled emails of the last 7 days. Errors Total Errors (last 1 day) and Top Errors.

docs.title: System Console
docs.text:
System Console (/app/system-console) runs Python or SQL on the site from the desk. You need the System Manager role.

  • Type Python runs the code in the same restricted environment as Server Scripts. It needs server_script_enabled in common_site_config.json. See Server and Client Scripts.
  • Type SQL runs only SELECT and EXPLAIN queries (and read-only CTEs on MariaDB). It cannot read the __Auth table.
  • Frappe rolls back all changes unless Commit is set.
  • Each run adds a Console Log with the script and whether it committed.
  • Show Processlist lists the running database queries.

docs.title: Log Settings and cleanup
docs.text:
Log Settings (/app/log-settings) sets how long Frappe keeps each log. Each row in Logs to Clear has Log DocType and Clear Logs After (days). A daily job deletes older rows. Defaults come from the default_log_clearing_doctypes hook, for example:

Log DocType Days Error Log 14 Scheduled Job Log 7 Email Queue 30 Activity Log 90 Integration Request 90

To shrink a large log table at once, use the CLI. It copies recent rows to a new table and swaps the tables:

bench --site frappe.localhost clear-log-table --doctype "Scheduled Job Log" --days 30

The command backs up the old table first. Add --no-backup to skip this.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
try:
    process_sample_order(order)
except Exception:
    frappe.log_error(title="Sample Order sync failed", reference_doctype="Sample Order", reference_name=order.name)
  • frappe.log_error(title=None, message=None, reference_doctype=None, reference_name=None, *, defer_insert=False) saves the current traceback if you do not pass message. It returns the inserted Error Log. With defer_insert=True, or in a read-only request, it queues the log and returns None.
  • To make your own log DocType clearable, add a static method clear_old_logs(days) to its controller, and add it to the hook:
# sample_app/hooks.py
default_log_clearing_doctypes = {
    "Sample Sync Log": 30,
}
  • The Recorder API is in frappe/recorder.py (frappe.recorder.start, stop, get, delete). See Performance.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Background Jobs
  • Scheduler
  • Performance
  • Backups

docs.title: System Settings
docs.text:
System Settings is a Single DocType with the site-wide settings: language, time zone, date and number formats, login and password rules, email, file uploads, backups and the scheduler. Only the System Manager role can open it. Go to /app/system-settings. Changes apply to all users after you save.

The form has these tabs: Details, Login, Password, Email, Files, App, Updates, Backups and Advanced. The tables below list the main fields of each tab. Field labels are as shown in the form.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Label Fieldname Default Description Application Name app_name Frappe Hidden field. Name on the login page. Country country Country of the site. Language language Default language. Time Zone time_zone System time zone. Currency currency Default display currency. Enable Onboarding enable_onboarding 0 Shows onboarding steps. Disable Document Sharing disable_document_sharing 0 Nobody can share documents. Date Format date_format For example dd-mm-yyyy or yyyy-mm-dd. Time Format time_format HH:mm:ss HH:mm:ss or HH:mm. Number Format number_format For example #,###.## or #.###,##. Use Number Format from Currency use_number_format_from_currency 0 Uses the number format of the currency. First Day of the Week first_day_of_the_week Sunday Used in date pickers and calendars. Float Precision float_precision Decimal places for Float fields. Currency Precision currency_precision If empty, it comes from the number format. Rounding Method rounding_method Banker's Rounding (legacy) Also Banker's Rounding or Commercial Rounding. Apply Strict User Permissions apply_strict_user_permissions 0 See User Permissions.

docs.title: Login and Password
docs.text:
The Login tab has session, login method, brute force and two-factor settings. The Password tab has the password policy. See Users and Roles for the full tables. Main fields:

  • Session Expiry (idle timeout) (session_expiry), default 170:00. It must be in the format hh:mm.
  • Document Share Key Expiry (in Days) (document_share_key_expiry), default 30.
  • Max signups allowed per hour (max_signups_allowed_per_hour), default 300.
  • Enable Two Factor Auth (enable_two_factor_auth). When you turn it on, Frappe sets two-factor authentication on the role All.
  • Enable Password Policy (enable_password_policy), default on, with Minimum Password Score (minimum_password_score), default 2.

docs.title: Email
docs.text: Label Fieldname Default Description Email Footer Address email_footer_address Your organization name and address in the footer. Email Retry Limit email_retry_limit 3 Send attempts before an email fails. Disable Standard Email Footer disable_standard_email_footer 0 Hide footer in auto email reports hide_footer_in_auto_email_reports 0 Include Web View Link in Email attach_view_link 1 Store Attached PDF Document store_attached_pdf_document 1 Saves the PDF on the Communication. Welcome Email Template / Reset Password Template welcome_email_template, reset_password_template Custom Email Template for these emails.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Label Fieldname Default Description Max File Size (MB) max_file_size Upload size limit. Max Zip Extract Size (MB) max_zip_extract_size Size limit when you extract a zip file. Allowed File Extensions allowed_file_extensions One extension per line. Empty allows all. Frappe saves them in upper case. Allow Guests to Upload Files allow_guests_to_upload_files 0 For example for web forms. Allowed Doctypes for Guest Uploads allowed_doctypes_for_guest_uploads Shown when guest uploads are on. Force Web Capture Mode for Uploads force_web_capture_mode_for_uploads 0 Strip EXIF tags from uploaded images strip_exif_metadata_from_uploaded_images 1 Delete Background Exported Reports After (Hours) delete_background_exported_reports_after 48

docs.title: App and Updates
docs.text:
• Default App (default_app) on the App tab: the app that opens after login. A user can override it with the Default App field on the User form.
  • Disable System Update Notification (disable_system_update_notification) and Disable Change Log Notification (disable_change_log_notification) on the Updates tab.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
Label Fieldname Default Description Number of Backups backup_limit 3 Backups to keep. Older ones are deleted. Minimum 1. Encrypt Backups encrypt_backup 0 Encrypts new backups with gpg.

See Backups.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
Label Fieldname Default Description Max auto email report per user max_auto_email_report_per_user 20 Limit of Auto Email Report records per user. Max Report Rows max_report_rows 100000 Rows the report view can show. Enable Snapshot Reports enable_snapshot_reports 0 Adds a scheduled job (DuckDB Sync). Set Frequency to Daily or Weekly. Enable Scheduled Jobs enable_scheduler 0 Runs scheduled jobs only if set. Run Jobs only Daily if Inactive For (Days) dormant_days 4 Applies only to sites on Frappe Cloud, and not in developer mode. 0 turns this off. Show Full Error and Allow Reporting of Issues to the Developer allow_error_traceback 1 Shows tracebacks to users. Allow Sending Usage Data for Improving Applications enable_telemetry 1 Link Field Results Limit link_field_results_limit 10 Maximum 50. Show Absolute Datetime in Timeline show_absolute_datetime_in_timeline 0

You can also turn the scheduler on or off with bench --site <site> enable-scheduler and bench --site <site> disable-scheduler. If disable_scheduler is set in site_config.json, the scheduler does not run, whatever the setting.

docs.title: Website Settings
docs.text:
Website Settings (/app/website-settings) controls the public website. Basic fields:

Label Fieldname Default Description Home Page home_page Route of the website home page. Title Prefix title_prefix Added to the title of each web page. App Name app_name Frappe Name on the login page. Disable signups disable_signup 1 Turns off self sign-up on the login page. App Logo app_logo Logo on the login page. Brand Image / FavIcon banner_image, favicon Brand in the navbar and the browser icon. Footer Items footer_items Links in the footer. Robots.txt robots_txt Content of /robots.txt.

See Website for the other settings.

docs.title: Navbar Settings
docs.text:
Navbar Settings (/app/navbar-settings) controls the desk navbar.

Label Fieldname Description Application Logo app_logo Logo in the desk. The app_logo of Website Settings takes priority. Settings Dropdown settings_dropdown Items in the user menu. Help Dropdown help_dropdown Items in the help menu. Announcement Widget announcement_widget Text shown above the desk.

Each Navbar Item has Item Label, Item Type (Route, Action or Separator), Route or Action, Hidden and Condition. Standard items come from the standard_navbar_items and standard_help_items hooks. Frappe adds them when it installs the site (frappe/utils/install.py). Use Hidden to hide one.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
frappe.get_system_settings("enable_scheduler")         # cached for the request
frappe.db.get_single_value("System Settings", "date_format")
frappe.db.set_single_value("System Settings", "enable_scheduler", 1)
  • frappe.get_system_settings(key) reads the cached document (frappe.get_cached_doc) and keeps it on frappe.local for the request.
  • When you save System Settings, Frappe also saves each changed value as a global default (frappe.db.set_default).
  • To set values when your app is installed, use an after_install hook.
  • Site config keys, such as disable_scheduler, are in Configuration.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Disable Username/Password Login fails unless a Social Login Key, LDAP or Login with email link is enabled. This prevents a lockout.
  • Turning on Enable Two Factor Auth affects all users through the role All.
  • Enable Scheduled Jobs is off by default. The setup wizard turns it on. If it is off, scheduled jobs, such as the email queue, do not run.
  • The Log API Requests (log_api_requests) field is on the Advanced tab, but no code in v15 reads it. It has no effect.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Users and Roles
  • Backups
  • Scheduler
  • Configuration

docs.title: Users and Permissions
docs.text:
Manage users and roles, role permissions and user permissions.

Page What it covers Users and Roles Create users, give them roles, group roles with Role Profiles, limit modules with Module Profiles, and set password, login and two-factor rules. Role Permissions Set what each role can do on each DocType with the Role Permissions Manager, permission levels, rights and "Only If Creator". User Permissions Limit a user to specific records with User Permission, including applicable DocTypes, default values, descendants, strict mode and the permitted documents report.

docs.title: Role Permissions
docs.text: Role permissions decide what a user can do with a DocType. Each rule gives one role a set of rights, such as Read or Write, on one DocType at one permission level. A user gets the rights of all their roles together. Use the Role Permissions Manager to change these rules on a site. To limit a user to some records only, add User Permissions on top.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
• Rule: one row with a DocType, a role, a level and rights. The DocType JSON of an app holds the standard rules in DocPerm.
  • Custom rules: when you change any rule in the manager, Frappe copies all standard rules of that DocType to Custom DocPerm and edits the copies. From then on, Frappe uses only the Custom DocPerm rules for that DocType.
  • Permission level (permlevel): level 0 controls access to the document. Levels 1 and higher control groups of fields. Each field has a Permission Level property. A role needs access at level 0 first, or the higher levels have no effect.
  • Only If Creator (if_owner): the rule applies only to documents that the user created (owner).
  • Administrator has all rights on all DocTypes.

docs.title: Rights
docs.text:
Right Fieldname What it allows Select select Search and select records in Link fields, without opening them. Read also gives Select. Read read Open and view documents. Write write Change existing documents. Create create Make new documents. Delete delete Delete documents. Submit submit Submit documents. Only for submittable DocTypes. Cancel cancel Cancel submitted documents. Only for submittable DocTypes. Amend amend Amend cancelled documents. Only for submittable DocTypes. Print print Print and download PDF. Email email Send email from the document. Report report Open the Report view and reports of the DocType. Import import Use Data Import. The DocType must allow import. Export export Export data from the Report view. Share share Share documents with other users.

At levels higher than 0, only Read and Write apply.

docs.title: Open the Role Permissions Manager
docs.text:
1. Go to Role Permissions Manager (/app/permission-manager). You need the System Manager role.
  2. In the filters at the top, select a Document Type, a role in Roles, or both.

You can also open it from the list view menu (Role Permissions Manager) or from Customize Form (Actions > Set Permissions). The route /app/permission-manager/Sample Item opens it for one DocType.

docs.title: Add a rule
docs.text:
1. Click Add A New Rule.
  2. Select the Document Type, for example Sample Item.
  3. Select the Role, for example Sample Role.
  4. Enter the Permission Level. Use 0 for document access.
  5. Click Add. The new rule has Read set.
  6. Select the other rights in the table. Each click saves at once.

To remove a rule, click the red delete button at the end of the row. A DocType must keep at least one rule.

docs.title: Restore the standard rules
docs.text: Click Restore Original Permissions. Frappe asks you to confirm. It then deletes all Custom DocPerm rules of the DocType and uses the rules from the DocType JSON again.

docs.title: Field-level permissions
docs.text:
1. Open Customize Form for the DocType.
  2. Set Permission Level of the fields to protect, for example 1.
  3. Click Update.
  4. In the Role Permissions Manager, add a rule for the role at level 1.
  5. Set Read, and set Write if the role may change these fields.

Roles without a level 1 rule do not see these fields.

docs.title: Only If Creator
docs.text: Set Only If Creator on a level 0 rule to give the rights only for documents that the user created. The user can still see the list, but only their own documents. You cannot set Report on a rule with Only If Creator. Frappe clears it.

docs.title: Pages and reports
docs.text: Use Role Permission for Page and Report (/app/role-permission-for-page-and-report) to set which roles can open a desk page or a report. Select Set Role For (Page or Report), select the item, and edit the roles.

docs.title: Check a permission
docs.text: Use Permission Inspector (/app/permission-inspector). Select a DocType, a Document, a User and a Permission Type. The Output explains each step of the check.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
Standard rules live in the permissions list of the DocType JSON in your app. Change them in the DocType form in developer mode. Code that checks permissions:

frappe.has_permission("Sample Item", "write")                       # current user, DocType level
frappe.has_permission("Sample Item", "read", doc="Support Plan", user="user1@example.com")

For the has_permission and permission_query_conditions hooks, see Permissions for developers.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• After the first change in the manager, app updates to the DocType JSON rules do not apply on that site. Click Restore Original Permissions to get them.
  • Do not give the same rules to many roles. Give one user many roles instead.
  • Rules apply to the Report view and reports. Removing Report hides them.
  • Users who are not Administrator do not see rules for roles marked Is Custom in the manager.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• User Permissions
  • Users and Roles
  • Customize Form
  • Permissions for developers

docs.title: User Permissions
docs.text:
A User Permission limits one user to some records of a DocType. Role permissions say what a user can do with a DocType. User permissions say which records they can do it on. For example, give user1@example.com access to the Sample Item "Support Plan" only. The user then sees only that Sample Item, and only documents whose Link fields to Sample Item point to it.

User permissions do not give access. The user still needs a role rule from the Role Permissions Manager.

docs.title: How Frappe applies a User Permission
docs.text:
Assume a User Permission for user1@example.com with Allow = Sample Item and For Value = Support Plan.

  1. The DocType itself. The user can open only the Sample Items listed in their User Permissions.
  2. Linked DocTypes. In every DocType with a Link field to Sample Item, the user can open only documents where the link value is an allowed Sample Item. When a user opens a document, Frappe also checks the Link fields of its child table rows.
  3. Empty links. Documents with an empty link field stay visible, unless Apply Strict User Permissions is set in System Settings.
  4. Ignored fields. Link fields with Ignore User Permissions (ignore_user_permissions) set are not checked.

Frappe applies the same rules to the list view, reports, Link field search and frappe.get_list. Administrator and Guest are never limited.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Label Fieldname Default Description User user The user to limit. Allow allow The DocType of the allowed record. For Value for_value The allowed record. Is Default is_default 0 Uses this value as the default in Link fields of new documents. A user can have one default per DocType. Apply To All Document Types apply_to_all_doctypes 1 Applies the rule in all DocTypes that link to Allow. Applicable For applicable_for Applies the rule in this DocType only. Shown when Apply To All Document Types is cleared. Hide Descendants hide_descendants 0 For tree DocTypes. Gives access to For Value only, not to the records below it.

Frappe rejects a duplicate rule with "User permission already exists". A duplicate has the same user, Allow, For Value, Applicable For and Apply To All Document Types.

docs.title: Add User Permissions
docs.text:
1. Go to User Permission (/app/user-permission).
  2. Click Add / Update.
  3. Select For User, for example user1@example.com.
  4. Select Document Type, for example Sample Item.
  5. Select Document Name, for example Support Plan.
  6. Set Is Default if this value should fill new documents.
  7. Set Apply to all Documents Types, or clear it and select the Applicable Document Types.
  8. Click Submit.

With Apply to all Documents Types, or with all applicable DocTypes selected, the dialog makes one User Permission with Apply To All Document Types set. Otherwise it makes one User Permission per selected DocType. If rules exist for the same user and record, the dialog title changes to "Update User Permissions".

You can also open the list from:

  • The User form: Permissions > Set User Permissions.
  • The list view menu of a DocType: User Permissions.
  • The Role Permissions Manager: Set User Permissions.

To delete all rules of one user for one DocType, click Bulk Delete in the User Permission list.

Note

In v15 the Apply to all Documents Types box is cleared when the dialog opens, although the code tries to set it (frappe/core/doctype/user_permission/user_permission_list.js passes "checked" as the value). If you click Submit without setting it or selecting DocTypes, the dialog shows "Please select applicable Doctypes".

docs.title: Strict user permissions
docs.text:
Apply Strict User Permissions (apply_strict_user_permissions) is in System Settings > Details > Permissions. Default: off.

When it is on, a user with User Permissions for a DocType does not see documents where the link to that DocType is empty. Single DocTypes are never checked in strict mode.

docs.title: Check what a user can see
docs.text:
Use the report Permitted Documents For User (/app/query-report/Permitted Documents For User). Its filters are User, DocType and Show Permissions. It needs the System Manager role.

The report lists the documents of the DocType that the user can read. With Show Permissions set, it adds one column per right.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
from frappe.permissions import add_user_permission

add_user_permission(
    "Sample Item", "Support Plan", "user1@example.com",
    applicable_for="Sample Order",  # omit to apply to all DocTypes
    is_default=0,
)
  • add_user_permission(doctype, name, user, ignore_permissions=False, applicable_for=None, is_default=0, hide_descendants=0) does nothing if the same rule exists.
  • frappe.core.doctype.user_permission.user_permission.get_user_permissions(user) returns the rules as a dict keyed by DocType. Frappe caches it in Redis under user_permissions and clears it when a rule changes.
  • Set ignore_user_permissions on a Link field in the DocType JSON when the field must not limit access.
  • For the has_permission and permission_query_conditions hooks, see Permissions for developers.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A User Permission on a DocType that many DocTypes link to, such as a company or a department, limits all of them. Use Applicable For to narrow it.
  • Strict mode hides documents with empty links. Users can lose access to records they created before the link was set.
  • In a tree DocType, a rule on a parent also allows all descendants, unless Hide Descendants is set.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Role Permissions
  • Users and Roles
  • System Settings
  • Permissions for developers

docs.title: Users and Roles
docs.text: Every person who logs in is a User. A user gets access through roles. A Role is a name, such as Sample Role, that permission rules refer to. You give roles to users, and you give permissions to roles. Use this page to create users, assign roles, and set login and password rules. To set what a role can do, see Permissions.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: DocType Purpose User One login account. The name is the email address. Role A named set of permissions. Role Profile A saved group of roles. Assign it to many users. Module Profile A saved list of blocked modules. Assign it to many users. User Type System User, Website User, or a custom type with a fixed role and DocTypes.

docs.title: Desk users and website users
docs.text:
The User Type (user_type) field decides if a user can open the desk.

  • System User can open the desk (/app).
  • Website User can only use the website and portal pages.

You do not set this field by hand for standard types. When you save a user, Frappe sets System User if at least one of the user's roles has Desk Access (desk_access) set. Otherwise it sets Website User.

docs.title: Automatic roles
docs.text:
Frappe adds some roles without a row in the user's role table:

Role Who gets it Guest Every user, and visitors who are not logged in. All Every logged-in user, including website users. Desk User Every System User. Administrator Only the Administrator user. That user has all roles.

Use All or Desk User in a permission rule to give access to a large group.

docs.title: Create a user
docs.text:
1. Go to User (/app/user) and click Add User.
  2. Enter Email and First Name.
  3. Keep Send Welcome Email set to send a link to set the password.
  4. Save.
  5. Open the Roles & Permissions tab and select the roles.
  6. Save.

The Roles & Permissions tab has:

  • Role Profile (role_profile_name). A user can have one Role Profile. When you select it, Frappe replaces the user's roles with the roles of the profile on save. You cannot then add other roles by hand.
  • Roles Assigned (roles). The role checkboxes.
  • Module Profile (module_profile) and the module checkboxes. A cleared module is blocked. Blocked modules do not show in the user's sidebar.

docs.title: User form buttons
docs.text:
Button What it does Permissions > Set User Permissions Opens the User Permission list for this user. See User Permissions. Permissions > View Permitted Documents Opens the report Permitted Documents For User. Password > Reset Password Sends a link to set a new password. Password > Reset OTP Secret Makes the user set up two-factor authentication again. Impersonate Logs you in as this user. You must give a reason. Frappe adds an Activity Log and notifies the user.

Impersonate shows only when you are logged in as Administrator. The server method also allows only Administrator.

docs.title: Security settings of a user
docs.text:
These fields are in the Settings tab, section Security Settings:

Label Fieldname Default Description Simultaneous Sessions simultaneous_sessions 2 Maximum number of sessions at the same time. Restrict IP restrict_ip Allowed IP addresses, separated by commas. Partial addresses such as 111.111.111 are allowed. Login After login_after The user can log in only after this hour (0-24). Login Before login_before The user can log in only before this hour (0-24). Bypass Restricted IP Address Check If Two Factor Auth Enabled bypass_restrict_ip_check_if_2fa_enabled 0 Lets the user log in from any IP address with two-factor authentication.

The API Access section has Generate Keys. It makes an API key and secret for token authentication. See Authentication.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Go to Role (/app/role) to create a role.

Label Fieldname Default Description Role Name role_name The name. It is also the document name. Home Page home_page Route to open after login, for example /app. Disabled disabled 0 If set, Frappe removes this role from all users. Desk Access desk_access 1 Users with this role become System User. Two Factor Authentication two_factor_auth 0 Users with this role must use two-factor authentication, if it is enabled in System Settings. Is Custom is_custom 0 Marks a role made on the site. Only Administrator can change it.

The View menu of the Role form has Role Permissions Manager and Show Users. System Manager also gets Action > Replicate Role. It makes a new role with the same DocType permissions, as Custom DocPerm rules.

docs.title: Role Profiles and Module Profiles
docs.text:
1. Go to Role Profile (/app/role-profile) and click Add Role Profile.
  2. Enter Role Name and select the roles.
  3. Save.
  4. Open a user and select the profile in Role Profile.

A Module Profile works the same way. Enter Module Profile Name, clear the modules to block, and select the profile in the user's Module Profile field. On save, Frappe copies the profile's blocked modules to the user.

docs.title: User Types
docs.text:
System User and Website User are standard. A custom User Type (Is Standard cleared) gives a user a fixed role and access to a list of DocTypes only. Fields:

  • Role (role), required.
  • Apply User Permission On (apply_user_permission_on) and User Id Field (user_id_field). Frappe gives the role only to users who are linked from a document of this DocType through this field.
  • Document Types (user_doctypes) with the rights Read, Write, Create, Submit, Cancel, Amend, Delete, Email, Share and Print.
  • Document Types (Select Permissions Only) and Custom Document Types (Select Permission).
  • User Type Module (user_type_modules), the allowed modules.

On save, Frappe writes Custom DocPerm rules for the role. It also gives the role read, create and write on File.

docs.title: Password policy
docs.text:
Go to System Settings > Password.

Label Fieldname Default Description Enable Password Policy enable_password_policy 1 Checks password strength. Minimum Password Score minimum_password_score 2 One of 2, 3 or 4. A higher score needs a stronger password. Logout All Sessions on Password Reset logout_on_password_reset 1 Ends other sessions after a reset. Force User to Reset Password force_user_to_reset_password Number of days after which users must set a new password. Reset Password Link Expiry Duration reset_password_link_expiry_duration 1200 (seconds) How long a reset link works. Password Reset Link Generation Limit password_reset_limit 3 Reset links per hour.

docs.title: Login settings
docs.text:
Go to System Settings > Login.

Label Fieldname Default Description Session Expiry (idle timeout) session_expiry 170:00 Idle time in hh:mm after which a user is logged out. Allow only one session per user deny_multiple_sessions 0 Ends the older session when the user logs in again. Disable Username/Password Login disable_user_pass_login 0 Needs an enabled Social Login Key, LDAP, or login with email link first. Allow Login using Mobile Number allow_login_using_mobile_number 0 Allow Login using User Name allow_login_using_user_name 0 Login with email link login_with_email_link 1 Login without a password, with a link sent by email. Allow Consecutive Login Attempts allow_consecutive_login_attempts 10 Failed attempts before Frappe locks the account. Allow Login After Fail allow_login_after_fail 60 Lock time in seconds.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
1. Go to System Settings > Login.
  2. Set Enable Two Factor Auth (enable_two_factor_auth).
  3. Select Two Factor Authentication method: OTP App (default), SMS or Email.
  4. Save.

When you enable it, Frappe sets Two Factor Authentication on the role All, so all users must use it. To use it only for some users, clear the check on All and set it on the roles that need it. Frappe asks for the second factor when a user has at least one role with two_factor_auth set. The SMS method needs a gateway URL in SMS Settings.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
user = frappe.get_doc("User", "user1@example.com")
user.add_roles("Sample Role")      # saves the user
user.remove_roles("Sample Role")   # saves the user

frappe.get_roles("user1@example.com")
# ['Sample Role', 'All', 'Guest', 'Desk User']
  • frappe.only_for("System Manager") raises frappe.PermissionError if the session user does not have the role.
  • Ship roles with your app as fixtures, or create them in after_install. See Fixtures and Patches.
  • The hooks on_login, on_session_creation and on_logout run with the login_manager argument (frappe/auth.py).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Disabling a role deletes it from all users. Enabling it again does not give it back. Standard roles cannot be disabled.
  • A user with a Role Profile loses roles that are not in the profile on the next save.
  • A user without any desk role becomes a Website User and cannot open /app.
  • Administrator and Guest cannot be disabled, deleted or renamed.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Permissions
  • User Permissions
  • System Settings
  • Authentication

docs.title: Website and Integrations
docs.text:
Publish web pages and web forms, and connect Frappe to other services.

Page What it covers Website Publish Web Pages, Web Forms, blog posts and newsletters, set up the site header, footer and home page in Website Settings, run the portal for website users, and track visits. Integrations Connect a Frappe site to other systems with Webhooks, OAuth clients, Connected Apps, Social Login Keys, LDAP, Google settings, push notifications and Dropbox, Google Drive or S3 backups.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text: Frappe can send data to other systems, let other apps log in with Frappe, let users log in with other providers, and copy backups to cloud storage. All settings are in the Integrations workspace in the desk. Use a Webhook to push document changes to another service. Use OAuth Client when another app needs access to this site. Use Social Login Key or LDAP Settings to let users log in with an outside account.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: DocType Use it to Webhook Send an HTTP request when a document changes. Webhook Request Log See each webhook request and its response or error. Slack Webhook URL Save a Slack incoming webhook URL for the Slack channel of a Notification. OAuth Client Register an app that logs in to this site with OAuth 2.0. OAuth Provider Settings (Single) Set if users must approve access for an OAuth client. Connected App Connect this site to an outside OAuth 2.0 provider, to call its API. Social Login Key Let users log in with Google, GitHub, Office 365 and other providers. LDAP Settings (Single) Let users log in with an LDAP or Active Directory account. Google Settings (Single) Google OAuth client and API key for Google Calendar, Google Contacts, Google Drive and the Drive picker. Dropbox Settings, Google Drive, S3 Backup Settings (Single) Copy site backups to Dropbox, Google Drive or an S3 bucket on a schedule. Push Notification Settings (Single) Send mobile push notifications through a relay server.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
A webhook sends a request to a URL when a document event happens.

  1. Go to /app/webhook/new.
  2. Enter a name for the webhook.
  3. Select the DocType.
  4. Select the Doc Event.
  5. Optional: enter a Condition, for example doc.status == "Open".
  6. Enter the Request URL.
  7. Select the Request Method.
  8. Set Request Structure to Form URL-Encoded or JSON.
  9. Add the data: rows in Data for form data, or a Jinja template in JSON Request Body.
  10. Save.
  11. Optional: open the Preview tab and select a document in Select Document. The tab shows Meets Condition? and the Request Body.

A JSON body is a Jinja template. It gets doc and utils:

{
  "order": "{{ doc.name }}",
  "customer": "{{ doc.customer_name }}",
  "status": "{{ doc.status }}"
}
Field Default Description webhook_docevent after_insert, on_update, on_submit, on_cancel, on_trash, on_update_after_submit or on_change. condition Python expression with doc and utils. The webhook runs only when it is true. request_url Target URL. is_dynamic_url 0 Renders the URL as a Jinja template with doc. request_method POST POST, PUT or DELETE. webhook_headers Extra headers, as key and value rows. enable_security, webhook_secret 0 Signs each request. See below. timeout 5 Request timeout in seconds. background_jobs_queue default Queue for the request job. enabled 1 Turn off to stop the webhook.

How Frappe sends a webhook:

  • Requests are queued and sent in a background job after the database commit. If a document changes more than once in one request, the last version is sent.
  • Webhooks do not run during data import, patches, install or migrate.
  • The job tries the request up to 3 times, with a short wait between tries.
  • Each failed try and each success makes a Webhook Request Log with the URL, headers, data, response and error.
  • The body is the JSON text of the data, for both request structures. Frappe adds no Content-Type header. Add one in Headers if the target needs it.
  • on_submit, on_cancel and on_update_after_submit need a submittable DocType.

docs.title: Verify the signature
docs.text:
With Enable Security on, Frappe adds the header X-Frappe-Webhook-Signature. The value is the Base64 HMAC-SHA256 of the request body, with the Webhook Secret as key.

import base64, hashlib, hmac

def is_valid(body: bytes, signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    expected = base64.b64encode(hmac.new(secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).digest()).decode()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)

docs.title: Frappe as an OAuth 2.0 provider
docs.text:
Other apps can log in users with their Frappe account and call the API with a bearer token.

  1. Go to /app/oauth-client/new.
  2. Enter App Name.
  3. Optional: add Allowed Roles to limit which users can log in through this client.
  4. Optional: turn on Skip Authorization to skip the approval page for this client.
  5. Set Scopes (default all openid).
  6. Enter the Redirect URIs of the app.
  7. Enter the Default Redirect URI.
  8. In Advanced Settings, select the Grant Type (Authorization Code or Implicit).
  9. Select the Response Type (Code or Token).
  10. Save.
  11. Give the App Client ID and App Client Secret to the app.

Endpoints:

Endpoint Path Authorize /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.authorize Token /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token Revoke /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.revoke_token User info /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.openid_profile Introspect /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.introspect_token OpenID configuration /.well-known/openid-configuration (redirects to frappe.integrations.oauth2.openid_configuration)

OAuth Provider Settings > Skip Authorization sets if users must approve access (Force) or not (Auto).

docs.title: Connected App
docs.text:
A Connected App lets this site call the API of an outside OAuth 2.0 provider for a user.

  1. Go to /app/connected-app/new.
  2. Enter Provider Name.
  3. Enter the OpenID Configuration URL.
  4. Click Get OpenID Configuration to fill the endpoints. Or enter Authorization URI, Token URI and the other URIs in Endpoints.
  5. Enter the Client Id from the provider.
  6. Enter the Client Secret.
  7. Add Scopes.
  8. Save. Frappe sets Redirect URI.
  9. Register the Redirect URI at the provider.
  10. Click Connect to and the provider name.
  11. Log in at the provider to get a token for your user.

The redirect URI is <site>/api/method/frappe.integrations.doctype.connected_app.connected_app.callback/<name>. Tokens are saved per user as Token Cache records.

docs.title: Social login
docs.text:
1. Go to /app/social-login-key/new.
  2. Turn on Enable Social Login.
  3. Select the Social Login Provider: Custom, Facebook, Frappe, GitHub, Google, Office 365, Salesforce, fairlogin or Keycloak. Frappe fills the URLs for known providers.
  4. Enter the Client ID from the provider.
  5. Enter the Client Secret.
  6. Set Sign ups to Allow or Deny new users.
  7. Save. The login page now shows a button for the provider.

Register the Redirect URL at the provider. For Google it is /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2_logins.login_via_google.

docs.title: LDAP
docs.text:
1. Go to /app/ldap-settings.
  2. Turn on Enabled.
  3. Select the Directory Server: Active Directory, OpenLDAP or Custom.
  4. Enter the LDAP Server Url.
  5. Enter the Base Distinguished Name (DN) and the Password for Base DN.
  6. In LDAP Search and Paths, enter the search paths for users and groups and the LDAP Search String.
  7. In LDAP User Creation and Mapping, enter the LDAP fields for email, username and first name.
  8. Optional: in LDAP Security, set SSL/TLS Mode to StartTLS.
  9. In LDAP Group Mappings, select the Default User Type and, for system users, the Default User Role.
  10. Optional: map LDAP groups to roles in the LDAP Group Mappings table.
  11. Save.

Users then log in with their LDAP username and password. Frappe makes a user on first login unless Do Not Create New User is on.

docs.title: Google
docs.text:
In Google Settings (/app/google-settings), turn on Enable. Enter the OAuth Client ID, Client Secret and API Key from Google Cloud. Then:

  • A Google Calendar record syncs Frappe Events with a Google calendar for one user. Click Authorize Google Calendar Access after save.
  • A Google Contacts record syncs contacts. Click Authorize Google Contacts Access after save.
  • Google Drive Picker Enabled with an App ID adds Google Drive to the file uploader.

docs.title: Backups to cloud storage
docs.text: Frappe v15 can copy site backups to Dropbox, Google Drive or an S3 compatible bucket. Each one is a Single DocType in the Backup section of the Integrations workspace. Scheduled jobs in frappe/hooks.py run the daily and weekly backups. S3 also has a monthly backup.

docs.title: S3
docs.text:
1. Go to /app/s3-backup-settings.
  2. Turn on Enable Automatic Backup.
  3. Enter the Access Key ID.
  4. Enter the Access Key Secret.
  5. Enter Send Notifications To.
  6. Enter the Bucket Name.
  7. Optional: change Endpoint URL (default https://s3.amazonaws.com) for another S3 compatible service.
  8. Optional: enter a Backup Path in the bucket.
  9. Select the Backup Frequency: Daily, Weekly, Monthly or None.
  10. Keep Backup Files on to also copy public and private files.
  11. Save. Frappe checks that the bucket exists and that the keys can access it.

Click Take Backup Now to run a backup at once.

docs.title: Dropbox
docs.text:
1. Go to /app/dropbox-settings.
  2. Enter App Access Key and App Secret Key of your Dropbox app. You can also set dropbox_access_key and dropbox_secret_key in the site config.
  3. Register <site>/api/method/frappe.integrations.doctype.dropbox_settings.dropbox_settings.dropbox_auth_finish as a redirect URI in the Dropbox app.
  4. Click Allow Dropbox Access.
  5. Log in to Dropbox and approve the access.
  6. Turn on Enabled.
  7. Enter Send Notifications To.
  8. Select the Backup Frequency (Daily or Weekly).
  9. Optional: turn on Limit Number of DB Backups and set Number of DB Backups (default 5).
  10. Save.

docs.title: Google Drive
docs.text:
1. Fill and enable Google Settings first.
  2. Go to /app/google-drive.
  3. Enter the Backup Folder Name.
  4. Select the Frequency (Daily or Weekly).
  5. Optional: turn on File Backup and Send Email for Successful backup.
  6. Save.
  7. Click Authorize Google Drive Access.
  8. Turn on Enable.
  9. Save.

Click Take Backup to run a backup at once. Last Backup On shows the time of the last upload.

All three send an email to the notification address when a backup fails. Send Email for Successful Backup also sends one after each successful backup.

docs.title: Push notifications
docs.text: Turn on Enable Push Notification Relay in Push Notification Settings. Frappe registers with the relay server and saves the API Key and API Secret. The relay server URL comes from push_relay_server_url in the site config. Frappe does not let you turn on the relay without it.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Run code on document events in an app with the doc_events hook instead of a webhook. See Extending Apps.
  • frappe.integrations.doctype.connected_app.connected_app.ConnectedApp.get_active_token(user) returns a valid token and refreshes it when it expired.
  • frappe.integrations.doctype.s3_backup_settings.s3_backup_settings.take_backup() and the take_backup methods of dropbox_settings and google_drive are whitelisted. They queue a backup job in the long queue and need the System Manager role.
  • API authentication with OAuth bearer tokens and API keys is in Authentication.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Use on_update with care. It runs on every save, so the target gets many requests.
  • A webhook body template must make valid JSON. If it does not, the request is not sent and the Webhook Request Log shows the error.
  • A webhook request log has no status field. Check the Response and Error fields.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Workflow
  • Notifications
  • Backups
  • Users and Roles
  • Authentication
  • REST API
  • Background Jobs

docs.title: Website
docs.text: Every Frappe site also serves a website. You can publish pages, a blog and newsletters, collect data with forms, and give website users a portal. Use a Web Page for content, a Web Form to let people add or edit records from the website, and Website Settings for the header, footer and home page. The desk is at /app. Website routes are at the root of the site.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: DocType What it is Web Page A page at /<route>. Content in Rich Text, Markdown, HTML, Page Builder blocks or a slideshow. Web Form A form at /<route> that makes or edits records of one DocType. Web Form Request A key that lets a person use a Web Form without a login. Blog Post, Blog Category, Blogger, Blog Settings (Single) The blog at /blog. Newsletter, Email Group, Email Group Member Emails to a list of subscribers. Published newsletters are at /newsletters. Website Settings (Single) Home page, brand, navbar, footer, login and signup, redirects, analytics. Portal Settings (Single) The sidebar menu of the portal and the default role of new signups. Website Theme Colors, fonts and SCSS of the website. Website Script (Single) JavaScript added to every website page. Help Category, Help Article A knowledge base at /kb/<category>. Marketing Campaign A named campaign. A Newsletter can link to one.

docs.title: Publish a Web Page
docs.text:
1. Go to /app/web-page/new.
  2. Enter a Title.
  3. Enter a Route, for example sample-page. If you leave it empty, Frappe makes one from the title.
  4. Select the Content Type.
  5. Write the content.
  6. Keep Published on.
  7. Save. The page is now at /sample-page.
Field Default Description content_type Page Builder Rich Text, Markdown, HTML, Page Builder or Slideshow. published 1 The page is public only when this is on. start_date, end_date A daily job publishes and unpublishes the page on these dates. show_title 0 Shows the title above the content. full_width 1 Uses the full width of the window. show_sidebar, website_sidebar Shows a Website Sidebar. enable_comments 0 Lets visitors comment. meta_title, meta_description, meta_image Tags for search engines and link previews. javascript, css Script and style for this page only. dynamic_template 0 Renders the content as a Jinja template. dynamic_route 0 Lets the route take variables. context_script Python that adds values to the template context. It runs in the safe script sandbox.

docs.title: Make a Web Form
docs.text:
A Web Form lets people make a record from the website, for example a Sample Order.

  1. Go to /app/web-form/new.
  2. Enter a Title.
  3. Select the DocType in Select DocType.
  4. In the Form tab, add fields to Web Form Fields. You can also click Get Fields to add all fields of the DocType.
  5. Set access in the Settings tab.
  6. Click Publish. It sets Published and saves the form.
  7. Open the form with the See on Website link in the sidebar.

Visitors see the form at /<route>/new. When Show List is on, they see their records at /<route>/list and edit one at /<route>/<name>/edit.

Field Default Description login_required 0 Only logged-in users can use the form. anonymous 0 Saves responses without the user. key_required 0 The form opens only with a key from a Web Form Request. allow_edit 0 Users can edit their record after they send it. allow_multiple 0 Users can send more than one response. allow_delete 0 Users can delete their responses. show_list, list_columns 0 Shows a list of the user's records. apply_document_permissions 0 Checks the permissions of the DocType for a record. When off, a user can open only records they own. allow_print, print_format 0 Lets users print their record. allow_comments, show_attachments 0 Shows comments and attachments to logged-in users. allow_incomplete 0 Lets users save without mandatory fields. button_label Save Text of the submit button. success_title, success_message, success_url What happens after the user sends the form. condition_json Filters for the records the form shows in its list. allowed_embedding_domains Origins that may embed the form, one per line. Use Copy Embed Code to get the snippet. client_script, custom_css Script and style for this form.

When you turn off both Login required and Key required in the form, the desk also turns off Allow Editing After Submit, Allow Multiple Responses, Allow Delete and Show List. Frappe accepts at most 10 submissions a minute for one Web Form.

docs.title: Give access with a Web Form Request
docs.text:
Use Key required to let a person without a login use a Web Form.

  1. Make a Web Form with Key required and Published on.
  2. Go to /app/web-form-request/new.
  3. Select the Web Form.
  4. Optional: set Expires On.
  5. Optional: add existing records in References. The key can open only these records and the records it makes.
  6. Optional: enter JSON in Web Form Values to fill the form.
  7. Optional: enter JSON in Doc Values to set fields on the saved record.
  8. Save. Frappe makes a random Key.
  9. Click Copy Link. The link is /<route>/new?web_form_request_key=<key>.

Frappe sets First Used On when the key is first used. After that the key cannot make a new record, unless Allow Multiple Responses is on. A key with a past Expires On stops working. A Link field in a guest Key required form must point to a DocType that Guest can read.

docs.title: Blog
docs.text:
A blog post is at /blog/<category>/<post>. The blog list is at /blog.

  1. Make a Blogger at /app/blogger/new. Enter Short Name (the record name) and Full Name. Link a User if the author logs in.
  2. Make a Blog Category at /app/blog-category/new. Frappe sets its route to blog/<name>.
  3. Make a Blog Post at /app/blog-post/new. Enter Title, Blog Category and Blogger.
  4. Select the Content Type (Markdown, Rich Text or HTML, default Markdown).
  5. Write the content.
  6. Turn on Published.
  7. Save.
Field Default Description published_on Set to today when you publish without a date. blog_intro Summary in the list. If empty, Frappe takes the first 200 characters of the content. featured 0 Shows the post first. A featured post needs a Meta Image. Only one post stays featured. read_time Set by Frappe from the content length. disable_comments, disable_likes 0 Turns off comments and likes on the post. hide_cta 0 Hides the call to action on this post. meta_title, meta_description, meta_image Tags for search engines. meta_description is cut to 140 characters.

Blog Settings at /app/blog-settings sets Blog Title, Blog Introduction, Enable Social Sharing, Browse by category, the call to action (Show "Call to Action" in Blog, CTA Label, CTA URL), Allow Guest to comment (default on), Comment limit and Like limit (default 5 each).

docs.title: Newsletter
docs.text:
A newsletter is an email to all members of one or more Email Groups.

  1. Make an Email Group at /app/email-group/new. Enter a Title.
  2. In the Email Group, use Action > Add Subscribers to paste email addresses, or Import Subscribers to import them from another DocType.
  3. Make a Newsletter at /app/newsletter/new. Enter Sender Email and an optional Sender Name.
  4. Add one or more Email Groups in Audience.
  5. Enter the Subject.
  6. Select the Content Type.
  7. Write the Message.
  8. Save.
  9. Optional: click Preview > Send a test email to check the email.
  10. Optional: click Preview > Check broken links to check the links.
  11. Click Send > Send now, or Send > Schedule sending to pick a date and time.

Frappe puts one email per recipient in the email queue. Members with Unsubscribed on, and addresses in Email Unsubscribe, get no email. Send Unsubscribe Link (on by default) adds an unsubscribe link. Scheduled newsletters are sent by an hourly job. A newsletter can be sent only once.

To show a newsletter on the website, turn on Published. The route is newsletters/<name>. Send Web View Link adds a link to that page and needs Published.

docs.title: Website Settings
docs.text:
Go to /app/website-settings.

Field Default Description home_page Route of the home page for visitors. title_prefix Text added before every page title. website_theme Standard The active Website Theme. app_name, app_logo Frappe App name and logo of the site. banner_image, brand_html Brand at the left of the navbar. top_bar_items Navbar links. navbar_search 0 Adds a search box to the navbar. footer_items, copyright, address, footer_logo Footer content. navbar_template, footer_template Web Templates for a custom navbar and footer. disable_signup 1 Turns off "Sign up" on the login page. hide_login 0 Hides the login link in the navbar. route_redirects Redirects from one route to another. head_html HTML added to <head> of every page. robots_txt Content of /robots.txt. google_analytics_id, google_analytics_anonymize_ip Google Analytics. enable_view_tracking 0 Logs visits as Web Page View records. show_language_picker 0 Shows a language picker on the website. show_account_deletion_link, auto_account_deletion 0, 72 Lets users ask to delete their account from /me. The account is deleted after the hours set.

docs.title: Portal
docs.text:
Website users (users without desk access) log in to the portal. /me shows their account page. The sidebar shows the portal menu.

Go to /app/portal-settings to set:

  • Default Role at Time of Signup (default_role): role given to new users who sign up.
  • Portal Menu (menu): the standard menu items. Turn each one on or off.
  • Custom Menu Items (custom_menu): your own links.
  • Hide Standard Menu: shows only custom items.
  • Default Portal Home: route to open after login.

docs.title: Help articles
docs.text:
1. Make a Help Category. Frappe sets its route to kb/<category>.
  2. Make a Help Article in that category.
  3. Turn on Published.

The article route is the category route plus the article title. When you unpublish a category, Frappe also unpublishes its articles.

docs.title: Track visits
docs.text: Turn on Enable in-app website tracking in Website Settings. Each page visit then makes a Web Page View record with the path, referrer, browser and time zone. The source, medium and campaign parameters of the URL are saved in the fields of the same name. Visits to /app, /api and asset routes are not logged. Browsers with "Do Not Track" on are not logged.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Add pages in an app with files in www/, and add routes with website_route_rules. See Website (developer).
  • A Web Form with Is Standard set is exported to the module folder of the app, with a .py and a .js file. See Web Forms.
  • Frappe routes /blog/<category> to Blog Post and /newsletters to Newsletter in website_route_rules of frappe/hooks.py.
  • frappe.email.doctype.newsletter.newsletter.subscribe(email, email_group) is a guest method that adds a subscriber after email confirmation.
  • Hooks: website_route_rules, website_redirects, update_website_context, portal_menu_items, standard_portal_menu_items, has_website_permission, webform_list_context, website_generators.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A Web Page with a past End Date cannot stay published. Frappe clears the date on save.
  • A standard Web Form can only be published or unpublished on a site. Other changes need developer mode.
  • With Login required on and Allow Multiple Responses off, /<route>/new opens the user's existing record.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Users and Roles
  • System Settings
  • Email
  • Website (developer)
  • Web Forms (developer)
